title: "apptainer build" fails on Ubuntu 24.04
body:
### Version of Apptainer

1.5.3 (noble version from PPA, pre-trixie version from GitHub, homegrown)

### Expected behavior

`apptainer build x.sif x.def` runs on Debian trixie, on Ubuntu Noble can't use user namespaces etc. (see below)

Expected: no issues

### Actual behavior

```
INFO:    User not listed in /etc/subuid, trying root-mapped namespace
INFO:    No user namespaces available, using only the fakeroot command
```
and `apt-get install openssh-client` fails
```
Setting up openssh-client (1:9.6p1-3ubuntu13.18) ...
groupadd: failure while writing changes to /etc/group
fatal: `/sbin/groupadd -g 101 _ssh' returned error code 10. Exiting.
dpkg: error processing package openssh-client (--configure):
 installed openssh-client package post-installation script subprocess returned error exit status 82
```

### Steps to reproduce this behavior

```
BootStrap: docker
From: ubuntu:24.04

%post
    apt-get update \
        && apt-get --assume-yes install \
        openssh-client \
        && apt-get clean
```
Run on Ubuntu 24.04 Desktop

### What OS/distro are you running

```
PRETTY_NAME="Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS"
NAME="Ubuntu"
VERSION_ID="24.04"
VERSION="24.04.4 LTS (Noble Numbat)"
VERSION_CODENAME=noble
ID=ubuntu
ID_LIKE=debian
HOME_URL="https://www.ubuntu.com/"
SUPPORT_URL="https://help.ubuntu.com/"
BUG_REPORT_URL="https://bugs.launchpad.net/ubuntu/"
PRIVACY_POLICY_URL="https://www.ubuntu.com/legal/terms-and-policies/privacy-policy"
UBUNTU_CODENAME=noble
LOGO=ubuntu-logo
```

### How did you install Apptainer

Downloaded from PPA, installed with `dpkg -i` (both `apptainer` and `apptainer-suid`)
Downloaded from GitHub release, same.
Built from source, installed with either `apt` or `dpkg`.


### Observations ###

- `root` can do it (of course?)
- sub[ug]id tricks didn't help, would even ask for `--ignore-subuid`
- Ubuntu has `kernel.apparmor_restrict_unprivileged_userns = 1` (Debian doesn't)
- setting `kernel.apparmor_restrict_unprivileged_userns = 0` makes `apptainer build` work (of course... as this replicates Debian's setting)
- `kernel.apparmor_restrict_unprivileged_unconfined = 1` doesn't seem to change the behaviour (for both settings of `..._userns`)
- adding `/usr/bin/apptainer{,-suid}` to the path in the AppArmor profile `/etc/apparmor.d/apptainer` makes `apptainer build` work even with `kernel.apparmor_restrict_unprivileged_userns = 1` set:
```
profile apptainer /usr/{libexec/apptainer/bin/starter{,-suid},bin/{apptainer,singularity}} flags=(unconfined) {
  userns,
  include if exists <local/apptainer>
}
```
so this would require a change in the AppArmor profile - which nobody else seems to need.

Am I seeing ghosts and using an approach that shouldn't be taken?

title: Implement multi-arch image push for ORAS
body:
Currently `apptainer push` only takes one image:

`apptainer push [push options...] <image> <URI>`

It should be possible to push _multiple_ images, each for a different arch, to the _same_ URI:

`apptainer push [push options...] <image> ... <URI>`

----

Then each image should be pushed, almost as before*, and the digest (descriptor) recorded.
\* but with a new name or tag, it should either be `name-arch:*` - or alternatively `*:tag_arch`

At the end, a v1.ImageIndex should be created with all the v1.Image that were pushed before.
And finally, this v1.ImageIndex should be pushed to the original URI (that has to be `oras://`)

This replaces the current manual workflow: https://oras.land/docs/how_to_guides/multiarch

Instead, one can do a single: `apptainer push image-amd64.sif image-arm64.sif oras://image`

After that, **both** are available: `apptainer pull image.sif oras://image` (will pick the right arch!)

This means that the URI will now be multiarch (even though the actual SIF will be for a single arch)

The go-containerregistry code involved is similar to this crane command: https://github.com/google/go-containerregistry/blob/main/cmd/crane/recipes.md#create-a-multi-platform-image-from-scratch

```
crane index append -t ${IMAGE} \
  -m ubuntu@sha256:c985bc3f77946b8e92c9a3648c6f31751a7dd972e06604785e47303f4ad47c4c \
  -m ubuntu@sha256:61bd0b97000996232eb07b8d0e9375d14197f78aa850c2506417ef995a7199a7
```

----

The image index is a simple JSON file, see `oras manifest fetch` for the exact details (OCI spec)

```json
{
  "schemaVersion": 2,
  "mediaType": "application/vnd.oci.image.index.v1+json",
  "manifests": [
    {
      "mediaType": "application/vnd.oci.image.manifest.v1+json",
      "digest": "sha256:ce54db371df60b95e3b7088ddbedd64c333424f60994dd3966a37bed51dbdecf",
      "size": 595,
      "platform": {
        "architecture": "amd64",
        "os": "linux"
      }
    },
    {
      "mediaType": "application/vnd.oci.image.manifest.v1+json",
      "digest": "sha256:fe8e9d0b66194ae46bc0cb3f4c5da639842be98d8b9b3452c893ed72c2c59e6d",
      "size": 595,
      "platform": {
        "architecture": "arm64",
        "os": "linux"
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

The temporary names/tags are not important, and could be deleted at the end....
The images are fetched using their digest, so they don't _need_ individual references.

Locally you could do something more simple, like a variable: `image-${ARCH}.sif`

EDIT: It is probably a bad idea to remove the arch name/tag, since the server will GC.
(Not all servers reflect what is used by ImageIndex, so they might delete the Image)

title: Build bundled PRoot without its Python extension
body:
## Description of the Pull Request (PR):

When building the bundled PRoot, explicitly unset the `HAS_SWIG` and `HAS_PYTHON_CONFIG` variables to disable PRoot's Python extension support.

Apptainer does not use PRoot's Python extension, and disabling it makes the bundled proot's dependencies reproducible. Otherwise, proot's dependencies [vary with whether swig and python3-config are installed on the build host](https://github.com/rootless-containers/PRoot/blob/9f70ae6f1a02f7a62c1b6f826114dbed198dac29/src/GNUmakefile#L97).

This was first observed when running E2E tests of Apptainer nested inside itself (#3580) on a GitHub CI host, which has both `swig` and `python3-config` installed. The resulting proot binary linked against `libpython`, and failed to start when Apptainer ran it to wrap mksquashfs during an unprivileged build inside a container that did not have `libpython` installed.

Also note that currently neither the RPM or Debian packages declare the `libpython` dependency. This is not necessarily an issue unless the packages are built in a machine with swig and python3-config installed, but this PR removes the possibility of that dependency existing in the bundled `proot` binary.

### Reproducing the issue

Tested on an AlmaLinux 9.8 machine with a local checkout of the `main` branch. Note the extra linked libraries on the bundled `proot` binary after we run `./scripts/compile-dependencies` with `swig` and `python3-devel` installed.

```
$ rpm -q swig python3-devel
package swig is not installed
package python3-devel is not installed
$ ./scripts/download-dependencies
...
$ ./scripts/compile-dependencies
...
$ ldd PRoot-*/src/proot
	linux-vdso.so.1 (0x00007ffc288df000)
	libtalloc.so.2 => /lib64/libtalloc.so.2 (0x00007f5d746eb000)
	libprotobuf-c.so.1 => /lib64/libprotobuf-c.so.1 (0x00007f5d746e0000)
	libc.so.6 => /lib64/libc.so.6 (0x00007f5d74400000)
	/lib64/ld-linux-x86-64.so.2 (0x00007f5d74701000)
$ sudo dnf install -y swig python3-devel
...
$ ./scripts/compile-dependencies
...
$ ldd PRoot-*/src/proot
	linux-vdso.so.1 (0x00007ffdd95ba000)
	libtalloc.so.2 => /lib64/libtalloc.so.2 (0x00007fe3acfd0000)
	libprotobuf-c.so.1 => /lib64/libprotobuf-c.so.1 (0x00007fe3acfc5000)
	libpython3.9.so.1.0 => /lib64/libpython3.9.so.1.0 (0x00007fe3acc00000)
	libcrypt.so.2 => /lib64/libcrypt.so.2 (0x00007fe3acbc6000)
	libm.so.6 => /lib64/libm.so.6 (0x00007fe3acae9000)
	libc.so.6 => /lib64/libc.so.6 (0x00007fe3ac800000)
	/lib64/ld-linux-x86-64.so.2 (0x00007fe3acfe6000)
```

  • Update github.com/stretchr/testify to v1.12.1, removing the legacy gopkg.in/yaml.v3 dependency.

1.10.1

Fixes:

  • Fix a regression introduced in v1.10.0 where TextFormatter could panic when formatting nil or panicking error and fmt.Stringer values.
  • Allow function-backed implementations of error as field values.

1.10.0

Fixes:

  • Fix reentrant logging deadlocks in formatter paths.
  • Fix race conditions in formatter and entry handling.
  • Fix generic Log, Logf, Logln, and LogFn methods unexpectedly panicking when called with PanicLevel. Use the corresponding Panic methods when panic behavior is desired.
  • Improve concurrency safety around formatter and hook access.

Features:

  • Add slog hook for forwarding Logrus entries to log/slog.
  • Add slog.Handler for forwarding log/slog records to a Logrus logger, including levels, fields, groups, context, time, and optional caller reporting. The hook and handler can also be combined to help migrate between Logrus and log/slog.
  • Add minimal, composable logging interfaces for each log level. This enables consumers to depend on narrower interfaces, making it easier to substitute or adapt logging implementations.
  • Allow Entry.Caller to be set explicitly and preserve it across derived entries, enabling custom caller detection without Logrus overwriting caller information when ReportCaller is enabled.

Changed:

  • Raise minimum supported Go version to 1.23.
  • TextFormatter now renders []byte values as raw/quoted strings instead of slice-of-ints.
  • TextFormatter now uses distinct dimmed colors for debug and trace output.
  • TextFormatter now automatically enables colors on Windows terminals with ANSI support, matching the behavior on other platforms.
  • Entry.HasCaller is now deprecated in favor of checking Entry.Caller directly.
  • Deprecated MutexWrap, which was unintentionally exposed as public API. It remains available as an alias for compatibility but should not be used

Changelog

Sourced from github.com/opencontainers/cgroups's changelog.

Releases

The release process hopes to encourage early, consistent consensus-building during project development. The mechanisms used are regular community communication on the mailing list about progress, scheduled meetings for issue resolution and release triage, and regularly paced and communicated releases. Releases are proposed and adopted or rejected using the usual project governance rules and procedures.

An anti-pattern that we want to avoid is heavy development or discussions "late cycle" around major releases. We want to build a community that is involved and communicates consistently through all releases instead of relying on "silent periods" as a judge of stability.

Parallel releases

A single project MAY consider several motions to release in parallel. However each motion to release after the initial 0.1.0 MUST be based on a previous release that has already landed.

For example, runtime-spec maintainers may propose a v1.0.0-rc2 on the 1st of the month and a v0.9.1 bugfix on the 2nd of the month. They may not propose a v1.0.0-rc3 until the v1.0.0-rc2 is accepted (on the 7th if the vote initiated on the 1st passes).

Specifications

The OCI maintains three categories of projects: specifications, applications, and conformance-testing tools. However, specification releases have special restrictions in the [OCI charter][charter]:

  • They are the target of backwards compatibility (§7.g), and
  • They are subject to the OFWa patent grant (§8.d and e).

To avoid unfortunate side effects (onerous backwards compatibility requirements or Member resignations), the following additional procedures apply to specification releases:

Planning a release

Every OCI specification project SHOULD hold meetings that involve maintainers reviewing pull requests, debating outstanding issues, and planning releases. This meeting MUST be advertised on the project README and MAY happen on a phone call, video conference, or on IRC. Maintainers MUST send updates to the dev@opencontainers.org with results of these meetings.

Before the specification reaches v1.0.0, the meetings SHOULD be weekly. Once a specification has reached v1.0.0, the maintainers may alter the cadence, but a meeting MUST be held within four weeks of the previous meeting.

The release plans, corresponding milestones and estimated due dates MUST be published on GitHub (e.g. https://github.com/opencontainers/runtime-spec/milestones). GitHub milestones and issues are only used for community organization and all releases MUST follow the project governance rules and procedures.

Timelines

Specifications have a variety of different timelines in their lifecycle.

  • Pre-v1.0.0 specifications SHOULD release on a monthly cadence to garner feedback.
  • Major specification releases MUST release at least three release candidates spaced a minimum of one week apart. This means a major release like a v1.0.0 or v2.0.0 release will take 1 month at minimum: one week for rc1, one week for rc2, one week for rc3, and one week for the major release itself. Maintainers SHOULD strive to make zero breaking changes during this cycle of release candidates and SHOULD restart the three-candidate count when a breaking change is introduced. For example if a breaking change is introduced in v1.0.0-rc2 then the series would end with v1.0.0-rc4 and v1.0.0.
  • Minor and patch releases SHOULD be made on an as-needed basis.

Release notes

Sourced from github.com/opencontainers/runc's releases.

runc v1.5.1 -- "El lujo es vulgaridad, dijo, y me conquistó."

This is the first patch release in the 1.5.z release series of runc, and primarily includes a fix for a serious regression on Ubuntu 20.04 kernels.

Fixed

  • There was a regression reported in with the maskPaths optimisation added in 1.5.0-rc.3 (#5275). On Ubuntu Focal (20.04), attempts to mount tmpfs with the nr_inodes=1 option will fail due to a downstream kernel patch (ironically originating from AUFS).   • Properly handle EINVAL for seccomp SECCOMP_FILTER_FLAG_WAIT_KILLABLE_RECV when trying to rewrite the filter. This appears to only happen if you compile runc with libseccomp >= 2.6.0 and then run it with an < 2.6.0 libseccomp. (#5347, #5354)

Static Linking Notices

The runc binaries distributed with this release are statically linked with the following GNU LGPL-2.1 licensed libraries, with runc acting as a "work that uses the Library":

  • libseccomp

Similarly, the runc binaries distributed with this release are also statically linked with the following MPLv2 licensed libraries, with runc acting as a "Larger Work":

  • libpathrs

The versions of these libraries were not modified from their upstream versions, but in order to comply with their corresponding licenses, we have attached the complete source code for those libraries which (when combined with the attached runc source code) may be used to exercise your rights under their respective licenses.

Release notes

Sourced from github.com/moby/go-archive's releases.

v0.3.3

What's Changed

  • Fix a regression introduced in v0.3.0 that caused archive extraction to reject hardlinks with absolute targets, as produced by some image builders. Absolute hardlink targets are now resolved relative to the extraction root, while paths that escape the root remain rejected. moby/go-archive#100
  • Fix a regression introduced in v0.3.0 that caused archive extraction to fail when applying permissions to device nodes, including nodes on nodev filesystems and dev/ptmx. Device nodes are now referenced without opening the underlying device before applying their mode. moby/go-archive#103
  • Set close-on-exec on file descriptors used by the Linux permission fallback to prevent them from leaking into child processes. moby/go-archive#104

Full Changelog: https://github.com/moby/go-archive/compare/v0.3.2...v0.3.3

v0.3.2

What's Changed

Fix a regression introduced in v0.3.0 that caused archive extraction to fail when paths traversed absolute symlinks inside the destination root, such as var/run -> /run. Absolute symlink targets are now resolved relative to the extraction root while relative symlink escapes remain rejected. moby/go-archive#93

Full Changelog: https://github.com/moby/go-archive/compare/v0.3.1...v0.3.2

v0.3.1

Fixes

This patch release fixes a regression introduced in v0.2.1 where archive extraction could fail when an archive omitted explicit entries for parent directories. For example, extracting etc/dnf/ without a preceding etc/ entry could return mkdirat etc/dnf: no such file or directory.

This prevented affected images from being extracted. Archive extraction now creates implied parent directories for both file and directory entries.

What's Changed

  • archive: create implied parents for directory entries moby/go-archive#92
  • archive: Tarballer.Go: suppress io.ErrClosedPipe logs on close moby/go-archive#94

Full Changelog: https://github.com/moby/go-archive/compare/v0.3.0...v0.3.1

v0.3.0

Security

This release fixes CVE-2026-17106 / GHSA-hfg8-hc9c-6c3h, where a crafted tar archive could use links to cause extraction operations to create or overwrite files outside the intended destination directory.

The issue affected Unpack, UnpackLayer, Untar, UntarUncompressed, and the ApplyLayer helpers. Users should upgrade and avoid extracting untrusted archives with earlier versions.

What's Changed

  • Hack: Add coverage testing into docker-ci
  • Runtime: Stdout/stderr logs are now stored in the same file as JSON
  • Runtime: Allocate a /16 IP range by default, with fallback to /24. Try 12 ranges instead of 3.
  • Runtime: Change .dockercfg format to json and support multiple auth remote
  • Runtime: Do not override volumes from config
  • Runtime: Fix issue with EXPOSE override
  • Builder: Create directories with 755 instead of 700 within ADD instruction

  • Runtime: List all processes running inside a container with 'docker top'
  • Runtime: Host directories can be mounted as volumes with 'docker run -v'
  • Runtime: Containers can expose public UDP ports (eg, '-p 123/udp')
  • Runtime: Optionally specify an exact public port (eg. '-p 80:4500')
  • Registry: New image naming scheme inspired by Go packaging convention allows arbitrary combinations of registries
  • Builder: ENTRYPOINT instruction sets a default binary entry point to a container
  • Builder: VOLUME instruction marks a part of the container as persistent data
  • Builder: 'docker build' displays the full output of a build by default
  • Runtime: 'docker login' supports additional options
  • Runtime: Dont save a container's hostname when committing an image.
  • Registry: Fix issues when uploading images to a private registry

0.4.8 (2013-07-01)

  • Builder: New build operation ENTRYPOINT adds an executable entry point to the container.
  • Runtime: Fix a bug which caused 'docker run -d' to no longer print the container ID.
  • Tests: Fix issues in the test suite

0.4.7 (2013-06-28)

  • Registry: easier push/pull to a custom registry
  • Remote API: the progress bar updates faster when downloading and uploading large files
  • Remote API: fix a bug in the optional unix socket transport
  • Runtime: improve detection of kernel version
  • Runtime: host directories can be mounted as volumes with 'docker run -b'
  • Runtime: fix an issue when only attaching to stdin
  • Runtime: use 'tar --numeric-owner' to avoid uid mismatch across multiple hosts
  • Hack: improve test suite and dev environment

title: Bind the NVIDIA GBM backend and X server modules with --nv and --nvccli
body:
## Description of the Pull Request (PR):

**This is a parity fix to https://github.com/NVIDIA/nvidia-container-toolkit/pull/1980, https://github.com/NVIDIA/nvidia-container-toolkit/pull/1979 and https://github.com/NVIDIA/libnvidia-container/pull/388.**

`--nv` binds every library it resolves into one flat directory on the loader's path, which serves anything the dynamic loader opens by soname. It does not serve the driver's modules that a library opens **by path**: Mesa's libgbm loads the GBM backend from a backend directory, and an X server loads `nvidia_drv.so` and `libglxserver_nvidia.so` from its module path. Those modules also sit in directories the ld cache never lists, so they were not found in the first place, and `nvliblist.conf` had drifted behind the driver.

The result on a stock host, measured below, is that a Wayland compositor in a container started with `--nv` cannot allocate a GBM buffer and falls back to software, and an X server has no `nvidia` driver to load, while `--nvccli` and CDI handle both.

This PR:

- Searches the module directories that sit next to the library directories (`gbm`, `xorg/modules/drivers`, `xorg/modules/extensions`, their `updates` counterparts and the driver's own `nvidia/xorg`), so the modules named in `nvliblist.conf` are resolved at all. This also fixes an early return that skipped those directories whenever the ld cache could not be read, which is exactly the case the `gpu library path` option exists for.
- Binds each such module at its host path as well as among the libraries, the way the NVIDIA Container Toolkit mounts the X.Org modules: a container laid out like the host then finds `nvidia_drv.so`, `libglxserver_nvidia.so` and `gbm/nvidia-drm_gbm.so` where its X server and libgbm look, and one laid out differently is told by the driver's `xorg.conf.d` snippet, which is bound too.
- Sets `GBM_BACKENDS_PATH` in the container when a `*_gbm.so` backend was bound, listing the bound-libraries directory first, then every `gbm` directory the container's own ld cache names, then whatever the image had set, so the driver's backend is found and the container's own backends still are.
- Binds a configuration file at the standard path a container's loaders read even when the host keeps it elsewhere: a file absent at its standard path is looked for under the other configuration roots (`/etc`, `/usr/share` and `/usr/local/share` hold the same trees) and under the prefixes above the `gpu library path` directories, where a driver installed outside the standard tree keeps its `share` and `etc`. A host file two entries name is bound once, so the Vulkan ICD is never handed to the loader twice. This mirrors NVIDIA/nvidia-container-toolkit#1980.
- Brings `nvliblist.conf` up to the driver's current file set: the GBM backend, the EGL platform libraries, the newer driver libraries, the EGL X11 external platform configs, the X.Org snippet under the names the distributions give it, the OpenCL ICD and the Vulkan config paths under `/etc`. It drops `libglx.so`, the name the driver's GLX module had before `libglxserver_nvidia.so`, which now matches the X server's own `libglx.so` and would shadow it.
- Creates the driver's device nodes the host lacks before binding them, through `nvidia-modprobe`, the setuid helper the driver installs so that a process without privilege can create them, which the driver's own libraries call on first use the same way and which libnvidia-container calls when it loads the kernel modules: the control node, one per GPU the driver reports, the unified memory pair and the modeset node. Nothing else on a headless host makes the modeset node before something asks for it, and a container without it cannot present through Vulkan on any X or Wayland surface. This mirrors NVIDIA/nvidia-container-toolkit#1979 and NVIDIA/libnvidia-container#388; a helper that is absent or refuses leaves the nodes as they are.

`--nvccli` needed the same treatment, since nvidia-container-cli stages the driver's libraries and its own device nodes but none of this:

- It binds the modules a loader opens by path and the configuration files, as the legacy flow does, and the EGL platform libraries and the GBM backend in the libraries directory, which its own configuration files name and it does not stage (`libnvidia-egl-gbm.so.1` among them), so `GBM_BACKENDS_PATH` finds the backend whatever the image's layout. Only that subset: the container libraries directory precedes the cache, so binding the rest would shadow what the CLI staged, CUDA compatibility included.
- `NVIDIA_DRIVER_CAPABILITIES=all` is accepted. It is the documented value for every capability, nvidia-container-cli has no flag for it, and Apptainer rejected the container outright with `unknown NVIDIA_DRIVER_CAPABILITIES value: all`. The `ngx` capability, which the CLI does accept, was missing from the set too.
- The DRM nodes are staged under `--contain` on both flows. They are what GBM, the EGL device platform and an X server open on the GPU; the legacy flow globbed only `/dev/nvidia*` and nvidia-container-cli stages no DRM node, so a contained session rendered in software while the ROCm flow had bound `/dev/dri` all along. `--nv` binds `/dev/dri` as it binds every GPU's own node; `--nvccli` binds the card and render nodes of the GPUs `NVIDIA_VISIBLE_DEVICES` names, read the way the CLI reads it (`all`, indices counted in PCI bus order over the GPUs the driver has not excluded, `GPU-` UUIDs, PCI addresses with their domain, a MIG index's GPU) and found through the PCI device's `drm` entries in sysfs, so a job given one GPU of a node sees that GPU's DRM nodes only. Outside `--contain` the full `/dev` bind covered this.

With a CDI device given as well (`--nv --device nvidia.com/gpu=all`, or `--nvccli --device ...`), a specification that mounts the same driver lays its modules out at their host paths itself and links the rest from its hooks; `--nv` then binds the libraries only, since a mount in a link's place is what a hook cannot replace (measured with #3738: `create-symlinks` fails with `device or resource busy` on a bound `gbm/nvidia-drm_gbm.so` otherwise).

## Measured

Host: 2x Tesla P100-SXM2-16GB, driver 580.178.04, Ubuntu 26.04, unprivileged user namespaces, NVIDIA Container Toolkit 1.20.0 plus a `nvidia-ctk` built from its `main` for the specification with the X11 platform libraries. Container: the Selkies desktop images, `apptainer run --nv --writable-tmpfs --contain` with no other GPU flag.

| in the container | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `/usr/lib/xorg/modules/drivers/nvidia_drv.so` | absent | the host's, at that path |
| `/usr/lib/xorg/modules/extensions/libglxserver_nvidia.so` | absent | present, with the versioned file |
| `/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/gbm/nvidia-drm_gbm.so` | absent | present, next to mesa's `dri_gbm.so` |
| `/usr/share/X11/xorg.conf.d/nvidia-drm-outputclass.conf` | absent | the host's snippet |
| `GBM_BACKENDS_PATH` | unset | bound libraries, the container's `gbm`, then the image's own; the same under `--nvccli` |
| EGL external platform configs | Wayland and GBM | plus `20_nvidia_xcb.json` and `20_nvidia_xlib.json` |
| libraries in `/.singularity.d/libs` | 33 | 48, every soname the host's driver lists |
| Wayland session on the GPU | `Failed to allocate GBM buffer`, falls back | `GPU: Tesla P100-SXM2-16GB on /dev/dri/renderD128` |
| X server with the NVIDIA driver | no module to load | loads the modules from its default module path |
| `/dev/dri` under `--contain`, `--nv` | absent | `card0..2`, `renderD128`, `renderD129` |
| `/dev/dri` under `--contain`, `--nvccli` with `NVIDIA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=1` | absent | `card2`, `renderD129`, the DRM nodes of `/dev/nvidia1`; `all` gives both GPUs', a `GPU-` UUID its GPU's, an unset value none |
| `/dev/nvidia-modeset`, `-uvm`, `-uvm-tools`, `nvidia1` removed from the host | absent in the container | created on the host by the helper (`-m`, `-u -c=0`, `-c=1`) and bound, on both flows; nothing is called when nothing is missing |
| `--nvccli` with `NVIDIA_DRIVER_CAPABILITIES=all` | `FATAL: unknown NVIDIA_DRIVER_CAPABILITIES value: all` | container starts |
| `--nvccli` GBM backend and X modules | absent | present, as with `--nv` |
| the Vulkan ICD moved to `/etc/vulkan/icd.d` on the host | not bound | bound once, at `/usr/share/vulkan/icd.d`, the first entry naming it |
| `--nv --device nvidia.com/gpu=all` with #3738 | the device's `create-symlinks` hook fails: `device or resource busy` | the hook's links in place, 34 driver entries in the ld cache, 48 libraries bound, `GBM_BACKENDS_PATH` set |

With those in place a Wayland session over `--nvccli --contain` reaches the GPU exactly as `--nv` does, provided the capability variables are set where nvidia-container-cli reads them, which is the environment Apptainer is invoked in rather than `--env`.

Eight desktop sessions were run to health on this host, each `apptainer run --writable-tmpfs --contain --cleanenv` with one GPU flag and nothing else: the Wayland and X11 backends of the EGL image and of the Debian-based image over `--nv`, the EGL image over `--nvccli`, the EGL image over `--device nvidia.com/gpu=all` (with #3738), and the EGL image over `--nv --device nvidia.com/gpu=all` (both branches merged). Every one reports the GPU on `/dev/dri/renderD128` with GLX and EGL on the driver's own libraries; the X11 sessions' framebuffer server runs `-glamor -dri /dev/dri/renderD128`, which is the path that needs the DRM node. The image that runs a native X server on the driver loads `nvidia_drv.so` and reports the GPU at its PCI address over `--nv` alone, where before it had to be told the modules by hand.

A configuration file placed only under a `gpu library path` prefix is bound at the standard path, and the bound-libraries directory stays first in `GBM_BACKENDS_PATH` when the image had set one.

`go vet`, the unit tests of the touched packages and `golangci-lint` pass; the end-to-end GPU group passes on the host above, with the added cases: the backend is bound and `GBM_BACKENDS_PATH` starts with the bound-libraries directory, the DRM render nodes are present under `--contain --nv`, `NVIDIA_DRIVER_CAPABILITIES=all` starts a container, and `--contain --nvccli` with `NVIDIA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0` shows exactly that GPU's DRM nodes; each skips where the host lacks the file or the driver's report. Unit tests cover the module-path test, the prefix, configuration-root and once-only resolution, the host-path binds, the driver's GPU report, the `NVIDIA_VISIBLE_DEVICES` forms, the DRM node lookup and the helper invocations for the nodes a host lacks.

### CI note

`debbuild-debian11` fails on every run since Debian 11 left LTS on 31 August: the final `bullseye-security` index still lists `libperl5.32`, `gpgsm`, `gnupg` and `linux-libc-dev` at their last security versions while their pool files are disappearing from the CDN edge by edge (`404 Not Found` from three different edges here, and from #3749 as well), and `archive.debian.org` does not carry `bullseye-security` yet. Nothing in this tree affects it; the job needs a decision on Debian 11 in the workflow.

- None filed.

title: Some thoughts about importing the OCI-SIF mode from Singularity
body:
### Version of Apptainer

`1.5.3`

### Ask / Question

I wanted to see what your thoughts are about porting some of the OCI-SIF capabilities from SingularityCE to Apptainer. What I mean is the ability to have multi-layered images with OCI blobs. From some analysis I did, it appears that there is a way to make such an image work with the native runtime in Apptainer w/o the need to implement OCI runtime mode (which uses `crun` / `runc`) as in Singularity. One advantage is that such an OCI-SIF image allows a more efficient management of the blobs inside.

I'd be happy to hear what do you think...

title: Run CDI device hooks and keep --device with --nv and --nvccli
body:
## Description of the Pull Request (PR):

**This is a parity fix to https://github.com/NVIDIA/nvidia-container-toolkit/pull/1980 and https://github.com/NVIDIA/nvidia-container-toolkit/pull/1979.**

`--device` applies the mounts, device nodes and environment of a CDI device but runs none of its hooks. The specification `nvidia-ctk cdi generate` writes relies on two `createContainer` hooks: `nvidia-cdi-hook create-symlinks` creates the driver's soname links (`libcuda.so.1`, `libGLX_nvidia.so.0`, `gbm/nvidia-drm_gbm.so`, ...) and `nvidia-cdi-hook update-ldcache` refreshes the container's `ld.so.cache`. Without them the driver's files are in the container but nothing resolves them: GLX clients fail with "failed to create dri3 screen", Wayland compositors with "Failed to create EGL display", and `libcuda.so.1` is not found.

This PR:

- Runs the `createRuntime` and `createContainer` hooks a CDI device declares from the RPC server, which is in the container's mount namespace, once every mount is in place and before the chroot. The hooks are handed an OCI state on stdin whose bundle holds a `config.json` naming the container root (`<session>/final`), which is where the NVIDIA hooks read it from. The other hook kinds have no counterpart in this engine and are skipped. A device that declares hooks turns on `--writable-tmpfs` the way `--nvccli` does, since the hooks write into the container root.
- Keeps the hook's capabilities across the exec. The RPC server of an unprivileged installation is not uid 0 in its user namespace, so an exec'd hook lost every capability; `update-ldcache` clones new mount and PID namespaces and failed with `fork/exec /proc/self/exe: operation not permitted`. `exec.Hook` now raises the process's permitted capabilities that are within its bounding set into the child's ambient set, which for the RPC server is `CAP_SYS_ADMIN`, `CAP_IPC_LOCK` and `CAP_MKNOD` in that namespace: the same set a hook exec'd by a root RPC server would receive. A failing hook's stderr is now part of the error instead of being discarded.
- Does not run the hooks in the setuid flow, for the reason nvidia-container-cli is refused there, and warns instead; the device's mounts, nodes and environment still apply as before.
- Keeps `--device` in effect together with `--nv` and `--nvccli`: the GPU setup returned before the CDI devices were recorded, so they were silently dropped, and a device node that `--nv` or `--rocm` already staged is not staged again instead of failing with "already exists in layout".

Tested on a 2x Tesla P100 node (driver 580.178.04, NVIDIA Container Toolkit 1.20.0, unprivileged user namespaces) with both a `--without-suid` and a `--with-suid` build:

Inside `apptainer exec --contain --device nvidia.com/gpu=all` of an Ubuntu image, unprivileged installation, before and after this PR:

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `readlink /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libGLX_nvidia.so.0` | missing | `libGLX_nvidia.so.580.178.04` |
| `readlink /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/gbm/nvidia-drm_gbm.so` | missing | `../libnvidia-allocator.so.1` |
| `ldconfig -p \| grep -c nvidia` | 0 | 34 |
| `/dev/nvidia*`, `/dev/dri/*` nodes | present | present |

The same probe with `--nv --device nvidia.com/gpu=all`, where `--device` was ignored before (no `/dev/dri` nodes, none of the X.Org driver modules the specification mounts under `/usr/lib/xorg/modules`), now shows the links, the ld cache, the nodes staged once (plus `/dev/nvidia-caps` from `--nv`), the 33 `--nv` libraries in `/.singularity.d/libs` and the X.Org modules. `--nvccli --device nvidia.com/gpu=all` gives the same result, the hooks running after nvidia-container-cli (its `create-symlinks` skips links that already exist).

A copy of the specification whose hooks are wrapped in a logging script, selected through `--cdi-dirs`, shows every hook returning 0, including `update-ldcache`, which failed with `fork/exec /proc/self/exe: operation not permitted` before the ambient capabilities were raised. A specification whose hook exits 2 after writing to stderr now fails with:

```
FATAL:   container creation failed: CDI hook /home/cc/cdi-dbg/failhook.sh failed: hook execution failed: exit status 2: boom: the device is not there
```

With `--device nvidia.com/gpu=all` alone, a Wayland compositor (labwc) in the container renders on `/dev/dri/renderD128` of the Tesla P100 and an X.Org server in a second image runs on the `nvidia` driver with GLX; both failed before with "Failed to create EGL display" and "failed to create dri3 screen".

Setuid installation (`--with-suid`, run as a regular user): `--device nvidia.com/gpu=all` warns `Skipping the CDI device hooks in setuid mode` and behaves as before (mounts, nodes, environment, no links); `--nv --device nvidia.com/gpu=all` works with the nodes staged once; `--fakeroot --device nvidia.com/gpu=all` skips the hooks too, since the setuid starter's RPC server is host root there as well (the flow in which `--nvccli` is also refused). In the unprivileged installation `--fakeroot --device nvidia.com/gpu=all` runs them inside the user namespace.

Re-validated against a specification generated from the container toolkit's `main`, which carries NVIDIA/nvidia-container-toolkit#1980: it adds the EGL X11 platform libraries, their external platform configuration files and `nvidia-xconfig`, and mounts the configuration files at the canonical container paths. The hooks link and refresh the cache there exactly as with the released specification, 36 driver entries in the container's `ld.so.cache` against 34, and the X11 platform libraries and `/etc/vulkan/icd.d/nvidia_icd.json` land where the container's loaders read them. The device's `createContainer` hooks of that specification are `create-symlinks`, `enable-cuda-compat`, `update-ldcache`, `disable-device-node-modification` and `update-application-profile`; all return 0 in this flow.

A specification and `--nv` together want the same files: `create-symlinks` fails with `device or resource busy` where a bind mount already sits in a link's place. #3740, which binds the driver's modules at their host paths, leaves them to a device that stages the same driver for that reason; with the two branches merged, `--nv --device nvidia.com/gpu=all` and `--nvccli --device nvidia.com/gpu=all` both reach the links, the refreshed cache, the bound libraries and the DRM nodes.

`make check` (golangci-lint v2.9), `go vet` and the unit tests of the touched packages pass, unprivileged and as root; `TestHook` covers the state on stdin, the stderr report and a missing hook, and `TestGetProcessBounding` compares the new getter with `/proc`.

### This fixes or addresses the following GitHub issues:

- None filed; the gap shows up with any CDI specification that relies on hooks, which the NVIDIA one does.

The unit tests of the touched packages were run unprivileged and as root; the full `make test` and `make testall` were not run.

title: Preserve OCI seccomp behavior after dependency migration

    ```go
    config.Linux.Seccomp.DefaultErrnoRet = nil
    ```

  - Add a seccomp-tagged test ensuring default OCI profiles retain this behavior.

v1.10.1

Logrus v1.10.1

This patch release fixes two issues in field formatting and handling:

  • Fix a regression introduced in v1.10.0 where TextFormatter could panic when formatting nil or panicking error and fmt.Stringer values.

Full Changelog: https://github.com/sirupsen/logrus/compare/v1.10.0...v1.10.1

v1.10.0

Logrus v1.10.0

This release focuses on substantial performance improvements, concurrency correctness, and better interoperability with modern Go logging APIs.

🚀 Performance

Major improvements across TextFormatter, entry handling, and common logger paths:

  • ~17% lower geomean runtime across the benchmark suite
  • ~27% higher geomean formatter throughput
  • Common enabled logging paths are ~30–44% faster
  • WithError is ~40% faster
  • Chained fields are ~46% faster
  • TextFormatter paths are up to ~40% faster
  • Allocation counts are reduced by ~25–74% across measured TextFormatter cases, with the largest reductions in colored output

The improvements also show up in complete logger paths:

  • Logger + TextFormatter is ~31% faster, with ~24% fewer allocations
  • Logger + JSONFormatter is ~21% faster, with ~10% fewer allocations

JSONFormatter itself remains largely unchanged in runtime performance, with small allocation reductions.

🔄 log/slog interoperability

v1.10 adds bidirectional interoperability between Logrus and Go's log/slog:

  • A Logrus slog hook can forward existing Logrus entries to an slog logger.
  • hooks/slog.NewHandler implements slog.Handler, allowing log/slog records to use an existing Logrus logger and its hooks, formatter, and output.
  • The handler preserves levels, fields, groups, context, record timestamps, and optionally caller information.
  • Caller reporting is configured per handler, without requiring Logrus's logger-wide ReportCaller option.
  • Custom slog levels can be mapped to Logrus levels.

... (truncated)

Changelog

Sourced from github.com/sirupsen/logrus's changelog.

1.10.1

Fixes:

  • Fix a regression introduced in v1.10.0 where TextFormatter could panic when formatting nil or panicking error and fmt.Stringer values.
  • Allow function-backed implementations of error as field values.

1.10.0

Fixes:

  • Fix reentrant logging deadlocks in formatter paths.
  • Fix race conditions in formatter and entry handling.
  • Fix generic Log, Logf, Logln, and LogFn methods unexpectedly panicking when called with PanicLevel. Use the corresponding Panic methods when panic behavior is desired.
  • Improve concurrency safety around formatter and hook access.

Features:

  • Add slog hook for forwarding Logrus entries to log/slog.
  • Add slog.Handler for forwarding log/slog records to a Logrus logger, including levels, fields, groups, context, time, and optional caller reporting. The hook and handler can also be combined to help migrate between Logrus and log/slog.
  • Add minimal, composable logging interfaces for each log level. This enables consumers to depend on narrower interfaces, making it easier to substitute or adapt logging implementations.
  • Allow Entry.Caller to be set explicitly and preserve it across derived entries, enabling custom caller detection without Logrus overwriting caller information when ReportCaller is enabled.

Changed:

  • Raise minimum supported Go version to 1.23.
  • TextFormatter now renders []byte values as raw/quoted strings instead of slice-of-ints.
  • TextFormatter now uses distinct dimmed colors for debug and trace output.
  • TextFormatter now automatically enables colors on Windows terminals with ANSI support, matching the behavior on other platforms.
  • Entry.HasCaller is now deprecated in favor of checking Entry.Caller directly.
  • Deprecated MutexWrap, which was unintentionally exposed as public API. It remains available as an alias for compatibility but should not be used directly.

Changelog

Sourced from github.com/opencontainers/cgroups's changelog.

Releases

The release process hopes to encourage early, consistent consensus-building during project development. The mechanisms used are regular community communication on the mailing list about progress, scheduled meetings for issue resolution and release triage, and regularly paced and communicated releases. Releases are proposed and adopted or rejected using the usual project governance rules and procedures.

An anti-pattern that we want to avoid is heavy development or discussions "late cycle" around major releases. We want to build a community that is involved and communicates consistently through all releases instead of relying on "silent periods" as a judge of stability.

Parallel releases

A single project MAY consider several motions to release in parallel. However each motion to release after the initial 0.1.0 MUST be based on a previous release that has already landed.

For example, runtime-spec maintainers may propose a v1.0.0-rc2 on the 1st of the month and a v0.9.1 bugfix on the 2nd of the month. They may not propose a v1.0.0-rc3 until the v1.0.0-rc2 is accepted (on the 7th if the vote initiated on the 1st passes).

Specifications

The OCI maintains three categories of projects: specifications, applications, and conformance-testing tools. However, specification releases have special restrictions in the [OCI charter][charter]:

  • They are the target of backwards compatibility (§7.g), and
  • They are subject to the OFWa patent grant (§8.d and e).

To avoid unfortunate side effects (onerous backwards compatibility requirements or Member resignations), the following additional procedures apply to specification releases:

Planning a release

Every OCI specification project SHOULD hold meetings that involve maintainers reviewing pull requests, debating outstanding issues, and planning releases. This meeting MUST be advertised on the project README and MAY happen on a phone call, video conference, or on IRC. Maintainers MUST send updates to the dev@opencontainers.org with results of these meetings.

Before the specification reaches v1.0.0, the meetings SHOULD be weekly. Once a specification has reached v1.0.0, the maintainers may alter the cadence, but a meeting MUST be held within four weeks of the previous meeting.

The release plans, corresponding milestones and estimated due dates MUST be published on GitHub (e.g. https://github.com/opencontainers/runtime-spec/milestones). GitHub milestones and issues are only used for community organization and all releases MUST follow the project governance rules and procedures.

Timelines

Specifications have a variety of different timelines in their lifecycle.

  • Pre-v1.0.0 specifications SHOULD release on a monthly cadence to garner feedback.
  • Major specification releases MUST release at least three release candidates spaced a minimum of one week apart. This means a major release like a v1.0.0 or v2.0.0 release will take 1 month at minimum: one week for rc1, one week for rc2, one week for rc3, and one week for the major release itself. Maintainers SHOULD strive to make zero breaking changes during this cycle of release candidates and SHOULD restart the three-candidate count when a breaking change is introduced. Release notes

Sourced from github.com/opencontainers/runc's releases.

runc v1.5.1 -- "El lujo es vulgaridad, dijo, y me conquistó."

This is the first patch release in the 1.5.z release series of runc, and primarily includes a fix for a serious regression on Ubuntu 20.04 kernels.

Fixed

  • There was a regression reported in with the maskPaths optimisation added in 1.5.0-rc.3 (#5275). On Ubuntu Focal (20.04), attempts to mount tmpfs with the nr_inodes=1 option will fail due to a downstream kernel patch (ironically originating from AUFS). Release notes

Sourced from github.com/moby/go-archive's releases.

v0.3.3

What's Changed

  • Fix a regression introduced in v0.3.0 that caused archive extraction to reject hardlinks with absolute targets, as produced by some image builders. Absolute hardlink targets are now resolved relative to the extraction root, while paths that escape the root remain rejected. moby/go-archive#100
  • Fix a regression introduced in v0.3.0 that caused archive extraction to fail when applying permissions to device nodes, including nodes on nodev filesystems and dev/ptmx. Device nodes are now referenced without opening the underlying device before applying their mode. moby/go-archive#103
  • Set close-on-exec on file descriptors used by the Linux permission fallback to prevent them from leaking into child processes. moby/go-archive#104

Full Changelog: https://github.com/moby/go-archive/compare/v0.3.2...v0.3.3

v0.3.2

What's Changed

Fix a regression introduced in v0.3.0 that caused archive extraction to fail when paths traversed absolute symlinks inside the destination root, such as var/run -> /run. Absolute symlink targets are now resolved relative to the extraction root while relative symlink escapes remain rejected. moby/go-archive#93

Full Changelog: https://github.com/moby/go-archive/compare/v0.3.1...v0.3.2

v0.3.1

Fixes

This patch release fixes a regression introduced in v0.2.1 where archive extraction could fail when an archive omitted explicit entries for parent directories. For example, extracting etc/dnf/ without a preceding etc/ entry could return mkdirat etc/dnf: no such file or directory.

This prevented affected images from being extracted. Archive extraction now creates implied parent directories for both file and directory entries.

What's Changed

  • archive: create implied parents for directory entries moby/go-archive#92
  • archive: Tarballer.Go: suppress io.ErrClosedPipe logs on close moby/go-archive#94

Full Changelog: https://github.com/moby/go-archive/compare/v0.3.0...v0.3.1

v0.3.0

Security

This release fixes CVE-2026-17106 / GHSA-hfg8-hc9c-6c3h, where a crafted tar archive could use links to cause extraction operations to create or overwrite files outside the intended destination directory.

The issue affected Unpack, UnpackLayer, Untar, UntarUncompressed, and the ApplyLayer helpers. Users should upgrade and avoid extracting untrusted archives with earlier versions.

What's Changed

  • archive: harden tar extraction against path traversal moby/go-archive#45
  • archive: do not follow reparse points in chtimes moby/go-archive#90

title: apptainer build fails inside unprivileged docker unless systempaths are unconfined
body:
### Version of Apptainer

1.5.3

### Actual behavior

If docker is run without `--privileged` and `--systempaths=unconfined` but with `--seccomp=unconfined` (for EL-based, or `--apparmor=unconfined` for debian-based) and with `--device /dev/fuse` then apptainer build commands from definition files fail with `failed to mount proc filesystem: operation not permitted`.

Although the apptainer documentation recommends using `--systempaths=unconfined` for unprivileged docker, it's a difficult setting to get with Kubernetes and with the Gitlab docker executor so it's worthwhile having a solution for this.

### Steps to reproduce this behavior

```
$ docker run -it --rm --security-opt seccomp=unconfined --device /dev/fuse rockylinux:8
# dnf install -y epel-release
...
# dnf install -y apptainer
...
# useradd user1
# su - user1
$ echo "Bootstrap: docker" >rocky8.def
$ echo "From: rockylinux:8" >>rocky8.def
$ apptainer build rocky8.sif rocky8.def
newgidmap: write to gid_map failed: Operation not permitted
ERROR  : 'newgidmap' execution failed. Check that 'newgidmap' is setuid root or has setcap cap_setgid+eip.
ERROR  : Error while waiting event for user namespace mappings: no event received
$ exit
# dnf install -y /usr/sbin/setcap
...
# setcap cap_setuid+eip /usr/bin/newuidmap
# setcap cap_setgid+eip /usr/bin/newgidmap
# su - user1
$ apptainer build rocky8.sif rocky8.def
FATAL:   failed to mount proc filesystem: operation not permitted
```

### What OS/distro are you running

Rocky 8.10

### How did you install Apptainer

EPEL

Release notes

Sourced from github.com/sirupsen/logrus's releases.

v1.10.0

Logrus v1.10.0

This release focuses on substantial performance improvements, concurrency correctness, and better interoperability with modern Go logging APIs.

🚀 Performance

Major improvements across TextFormatter, entry handling, and common logger paths:

  • ~17% lower geomean runtime across the benchmark suite
  • ~27% higher geomean formatter throughput
  • Common enabled logging paths are ~30–44% faster
  • WithError is ~40% faster
  • Chained fields are ~46% faster
  • TextFormatter paths are up to ~40% faster
  • Allocation counts are reduced by ~25–74% across measured TextFormatter cases, with the largest reductions in colored output

The improvements also show up in complete logger paths:

  • Logger + TextFormatter is ~31% faster, with ~24% fewer allocations
  • Logger + JSONFormatter is ~21% faster, with ~10% fewer allocations

JSONFormatter itself remains largely unchanged in runtime performance, with small allocation reductions.

🔄 log/slog interoperability

v1.10 adds bidirectional interoperability between Logrus and Go's log/slog:

  • A Logrus slog hook can forward existing Logrus entries to an slog logger.
  • hooks/slog.NewHandler implements slog.Handler, allowing log/slog records to use an existing Logrus logger and its hooks, formatter, and output.
  • The handler preserves levels, fields, groups, context, record timestamps, and optionally caller information.
  • Caller reporting is configured per handler, without requiring Logrus's logger-wide ReportCaller option.
  • Custom slog levels can be mapped to Logrus levels.
  • The hook and handler can be combined, providing a practical path for incrementally migrating from Logrus to log/slog without requiring an all-at-once transition.

This allows applications to migrate their logging API and logging backend independently: existing Logrus call sites can start using an slog backend, while new slog code can continue using an established Logrus setup.

🔒 Concurrency & Correctness

  • Fix reentrant logging deadlocks, including logging from within MarshalJSON or formatter code.
  • Fix generic Log, Logf, Logln, and LogFn methods unexpectedly panicking when called with PanicLevel, contrary to their documented behavior.
  • Eliminate race conditions in entry and formatter paths.
  • Improve locking boundaries around formatters and hooks.

➕ Added

  • TextFormatter now automatically enables colors on Windows terminals with ANSI support, matching behavior on other platforms.
  • Entry.Caller can now be set explicitly and is preserved across derived entries. When caller reporting is enabled, Logrus only detects and populates caller information when none was provided, allowing custom caller detection and wrapper-aware logging without adding additional caller configuration APIs.
  • Add minimal, composable logging interfaces for each log level, allowing consumers to depend on narrower interfaces and making logging implementations easier to substitute or adapt.
  • Expand CI verification to include TinyGo and every cross-compile target reported by go tool dist list, improving coverage across alternative toolchains and platforms.

... (truncated)

Changelog

Sourced from github.com/sirupsen/logrus's changelog.

1.10.0

Fixes:

  • Fix reentrant logging deadlocks in formatter paths.
  • Fix race conditions in formatter and entry handling.
  • Fix generic Log, Logf, Logln, and LogFn methods unexpectedly panicking when called with PanicLevel. Use the corresponding Panic methods when panic behavior is desired.
  • Improve concurrency safety around formatter and hook access.

Features:

  • Add slog hook for forwarding Logrus entries to log/slog.
  • Add slog.Handler for forwarding log/slog records to a Logrus logger, including levels, fields, groups, context, time, and optional caller reporting. The hook and handler can also be combined to help migrate between Logrus and log/slog.
  • Add minimal, composable logging interfaces for each log level. This enables consumers to depend on narrower interfaces, making it easier to substitute or adapt logging implementations.
  • Allow Entry.Caller to be set explicitly and preserve it across derived entries, enabling custom caller detection without Logrus overwriting caller information when ReportCaller is enabled.

Changed:

  • Raise minimum supported Go version to 1.23.
  • TextFormatter now renders []byte values as raw/quoted strings instead of slice-of-ints.
  • TextFormatter now uses distinct dimmed colors for debug and trace output.
  • TextFormatter now automatically enables colors on Windows terminals with ANSI support, matching the behavior on other platforms.
  • Entry.HasCaller is now deprecated in favor of checking Entry.Caller directly.
  • Deprecated MutexWrap, which was unintentionally exposed as public API. It remains available as an alias for compatibility but should not be used directly.

Performance:

  • Significantly improve TextFormatter performance and reduce allocations.
  • Optimize common Entry and Logger hot paths.
  • Reduce allocations in caller reporting.
  • ~17% lower geomean runtime and ~27% higher formatter throughput overall.
  • Common enabled logging paths are ~30–44% faster.
  • TextFormatter paths are up to ~40% faster, with allocation counts reduced by 25–74% across the measured formatter cases.

runc v1.5.1 -- "El lujo es vulgaridad, dijo, y me conquistó."

This is the first patch release in the 1.5.z release series of runc, and primarily includes a fix for a serious regression on Ubuntu 20.04 kernels.

Fixed

  • There was a regression reported in with the maskPaths optimisation added in 1.5.0-rc.3 (#5275). Release notes

Sourced from github.com/moby/go-archive's releases.

v0.3.3

What's Changed

  • Fix a regression introduced in v0.3.0 that caused archive extraction to reject hardlinks with absolute targets, as produced by some image builders. Absolute hardlink targets are now resolved relative to the extraction root, while paths that escape the root remain rejected. moby/go-archive#100
  • Fix a regression introduced in v0.3.0 that caused archive extraction to fail when applying permissions to device nodes, including nodes on nodev filesystems and dev/ptmx. Device nodes are now referenced without opening the underlying device before applying their mode. moby/go-archive#103
  • Set close-on-exec on file descriptors used by the Linux permission fallback to prevent them from leaking into child processes. moby/go-archive#104

Full Changelog: https://github.com/moby/go-archive/compare/v0.3.2...v0.3.3

v0.3.2

What's Changed

Fix a regression introduced in v0.3.0 that caused archive extraction to fail when paths traversed absolute symlinks inside the destination root, such as var/run -> /run. Absolute symlink targets are now resolved relative to the extraction root while relative symlink escapes remain rejected. moby/go-archive#93

Full Changelog: https://github.com/moby/go-archive/compare/v0.3.1...v0.3.2

v0.3.1

Fixes

This patch release fixes a regression introduced in v0.2.1 where archive extraction could fail when an archive omitted explicit entries for parent directories. For example, extracting etc/dnf/ without a preceding etc/ entry could return mkdirat etc/dnf: no such file or directory.

This prevented affected images from being extracted. Archive extraction now creates implied parent directories for both file and directory entries.

What's Changed

  • archive: create implied parents for directory entries moby/go-archive#92
  • archive: Tarballer.Go: suppress io.ErrClosedPipe logs on close moby/go-archive#94

Full Changelog: https://github.com/moby/go-archive/compare/v0.3.0...v0.3.1

v0.3.0

Security

This release fixes CVE-2026-17106 / GHSA-hfg8-hc9c-6c3h, where a crafted tar archive could use links to cause extraction operations to create or overwrite files outside the intended destination directory.

The issue affected Unpack, UnpackLayer, Untar, UntarUncompressed, and the ApplyLayer helpers. Users should upgrade and avoid extracting untrusted archives with earlier versions.

What's Changed

  • archive: harden tar extraction against path traversal moby/go-archive#45
  • archive: do not follow reparse points in chtimes moby/go-archive#90

Release notes

Sourced from github.com/sirupsen/logrus's releases.

v1.10.1

Logrus v1.10.1

This patch release fixes two issues in field formatting and handling:

  • Fix a regression introduced in v1.10.0 where TextFormatter could panic when formatting nil or panicking error and fmt.Stringer values.
  • Allow function-backed values implementing error to be used with WithError, WithField, and WithFields.

Dependency Changes

Full Changelog: https://github.com/sirupsen/logrus/compare/v1.10.0...v1.10.1

v1.10.0

Logrus v1.10.0

This release focuses on substantial performance improvements, concurrency correctness, and better interoperability with modern Go logging APIs.

🚀 Performance

Major improvements across TextFormatter, entry handling, and common logger paths:

  • ~17% lower geomean runtime across the benchmark suite
  • ~27% higher geomean formatter throughput
  • Common enabled logging paths are ~30–44% faster
  • WithError is ~40% faster
  • Chained fields are ~46% faster
  • TextFormatter paths are up to ~40% faster
  • Allocation counts are reduced by ~25–74% across measured TextFormatter cases, with the largest reductions in colored output

The improvements also show up in complete logger paths:

  • Logger + TextFormatter is ~31% faster, with ~24% fewer allocations
  • Logger + JSONFormatter is ~21% faster, with ~10% fewer allocations

JSONFormatter itself remains largely unchanged in runtime performance, with small allocation reductions.

🔄 log/slog interoperability

v1.10 adds bidirectional interoperability between Logrus and Go's log/slog:

  • A Logrus slog hook can forward existing Logrus entries to an slog logger.
  • hooks/slog.NewHandler implements slog.Handler, allowing log/slog records to use an existing Logrus logger and its hooks, formatter, and output.
  • The handler preserves levels, fields, groups, context, record timestamps, and optionally caller information.
  • Caller reporting is configured per handler, without requiring Logrus's logger-wide ReportCaller option.
  • Custom slog levels can be mapped to Logrus levels.

... (truncated)

Changelog

Sourced from github.com/sirupsen/logrus's changelog.

1.10.1

Fixes:

  • Fix a regression introduced in v1.10.0 where TextFormatter could panic when formatting nil or panicking error and fmt.Stringer values.
  • Allow function-backed implementations of error as field values.

1.10.0

Fixes:

  • Fix reentrant logging deadlocks in formatter paths.
  • Fix race conditions in formatter and entry handling.
  • Fix generic Log, Logf, Logln, and LogFn methods unexpectedly panicking when called with PanicLevel. Use the corresponding Panic methods when panic behavior is desired.
  • Improve concurrency safety around formatter and hook access.

Features:

  • Add slog hook for forwarding Logrus entries to log/slog.
  • Add slog.Handler for forwarding log/slog records to a Logrus logger, including levels, fields, groups, context, time, and optional caller reporting. The hook and handler can also be combined to help migrate between Logrus and log/slog.
  • Add minimal, composable logging interfaces for each log level. This enables consumers to depend on narrower interfaces, making it easier to substitute or adapt logging implementations.
  • Allow Entry.Caller to be set explicitly and preserve it across derived entries, enabling custom caller detection without Logrus overwriting caller information when ReportCaller is enabled.

Changed:

  • Raise minimum supported Go version to 1.23.
  • TextFormatter now renders []byte values as raw/quoted strings instead of slice-of-ints.
  • TextFormatter now uses distinct dimmed colors for debug and trace output.
  • TextFormatter now automatically enables colors on Windows terminals with ANSI support, matching the behavior on other platforms.
  • Entry.HasCaller is now deprecated in favor of checking Entry.Caller directly.
  • Deprecated MutexWrap, which was unintentionally exposed as public API. It remains available as an alias for compatibility but should not be used directly.

Performance:

  • Significantly improve TextFormatter performance and reduce allocations.
  • Optimize common Entry and Logger hot paths.
  • Reduce allocations in caller reporting.

title: No aarch64/arm64 release artifacts: v1.5.3 publishes 20 assets, all x86_64/amd64 or source
body:
## What we observed

`v1.5.3` (latest, published 2026-07-21) has 20 release assets and none of them are aarch64/arm64:

```
apptainer-1.5.3-1.el10.x86_64.rpm          apptainer-suid-1.5.3-1.el10.x86_64.rpm
apptainer-1.5.3-1.x86_64.rpm               apptainer-suid-1.5.3-1.x86_64.rpm
apptainer-1.5.3-1.src.rpm                  apptainer-suid-debuginfo-…x86_64.rpm  (×2)
apptainer-1.5.3.tar.gz                     apptainer-suid_1.5.3_amd64.deb
apptainer-debuginfo-…x86_64.rpm    (×2)    apptainer-suid_1.5.3-trixie+_amd64.deb
apptainer-debugsource-…x86_64.rpm  (×2)    apptainer-suid-dbgsym_…_amd64.deb     (×2)
apptainer_1.5.3_amd64.deb                  apptainer-dbgsym_…_amd64.deb          (×2)
apptainer_1.5.3-trixie+_amd64.deb
```

Taken from the releases API, filtered for `arm`/`aarch`: empty.

## Why this is not covered by #2979

[#2979](https://github.com/apptainer/apptainer/issues/2979) ("Build apptainer binaries and packages for more architectures") was closed 2025-09-01 because **the Ubuntu PPA is maintained again and now has arm64**. That resolves the Debian/Ubuntu side, and it is genuinely useful — but the PPA does not help a RHEL-family host, and the RPM side of the release page is still x86_64-only. So the gap for `.rpm` consumers on arm64 outlived the issue that would have covered it.

## The concrete situation it creates

We benchmark identical workloads on Graviton (aarch64) and x86_64 EC2 instances on Amazon Linux 2023, which is RHEL9-adjacent. Findings:

- `dnf install apptainer` on AL2023 fails on **both** arches — Amazon's repos carry no `apptainer` package at all, so this is not an arm-specific packaging gap on their side.
- The release page supplies x86_64 RPMs, so an x86_64 host has a first-party option.
- An aarch64 host has none: no RPM, no tarball binary, only source.

The asymmetry is the awkward part for our use case. Our arm and x86 rows are supposed to differ by ISA and nothing else, so installing an upstream RPM on x86_64 and something else on aarch64 would make the runtime a second variable in the comparison. We ended up using **EPEL9 for both arches** (`apptainer-1.5.3-1.el9.{aarch64,x86_64}.rpm` + the matching `apptainer-suid`), pinned by sha256, which works and installs cleanly on AL2023 with all dependencies resolving from AL2023's own repos. Recording it here because "use EPEL for x86_64 too, even though upstream has it" is not an obvious conclusion and might save someone the same detour.

That EPEL builds the identical spec for aarch64 also suggests the packaging work is largely done — it may be closer to a CI matrix entry than a porting effort.

## Ask

Publish aarch64 RPMs (and ideally an arm64 `.deb`) alongside the x86_64 ones on the release page, or — if that is not planned — state on the [installation page](https://apptainer.org/docs/admin/latest/installation.html#installation-on-linux) that aarch64 RPM users should get packages from EPEL. Either resolves it; the second is nearly free and would have answered our question immediately.

## Environment

- Amazon Linux 2023, aarch64 (Graviton3/4) and x86_64
- Apptainer 1.5.3-1.el9 from EPEL9 (working, both arches)
- Checked against apptainer/apptainer release `v1.5.3`, 2026-08-19

Hi everyone! Today we announce the v0.22.0 release of ebpf-go. We ship Linux 7.1 compatibility, older versions of the library will not work on 7.1 kernels and above, so please upgrade if you are targeting the latest releases of Linux. We also made a breaking change to BTF caching, please read those notes. And of course a few fixes, improvements and minor features.

Kernel 7.1 compatibility

In kernel 7.1 the BTF header was extended to introduce a new feature called BTF layout. This change caused our BTF parser to fail when parsing vmlinux for this kernel. This has been fixed in this latest release, we recommend upgrading to this latest release to avoid breakage on 7.1 and newer kernels.

See cilium/ebpf#2042 for details. Special thanks to @​Capricornus007 for making the bug report that allowed us to fix this in a timely manner.

BPF token support

Some BPF-related actions require the user to have root privileges (CAP_SYS_ADMIN). One example is loading and attaching programs that can inspect kernel memory. In some environments, you may want to permit a known good process to load such BPF programs, but you don't want to grant it CAP_SYS_ADMIN to avoid privilege escalation if that process gets compromised.

BPF tokens are a mechanism that allows a privileged process to delegate fine-grained BPF capabilities to an unprivileged process. The process of delegating is complex and typically handled by a container runtime such as LXC or a process manager like systemd. This part of the handshake is currently out of scope of ebpf-go, as the library is not in charge of process creation where this delegation takes place.

However, the consuming side is what's included in this release. ebpf-go will automatically detect when the current process is running in a namespace where a BPF token is provided, and will automatically try to obtain an use it for interacting with the BPF syscall. Unlike libbpf, this currently requires no extra configuration on behalf of the application.

See cilium/ebpf#1953 for more details.

BTF cache changes

Package btf used to cache kernel (vmlinux) BTF specs globally. This is a significant time gain when loading multiple Collections in a row. However, doing so comes at a fairly significant memory cost (~20 MiB), so users could flush this cache with btf.FlushKernelSpec. Unfortunately, the caching behaviour being opt-out means users would typically discover it while investigating memory usage, and would then have to find an appropriate time during execution to call the flush function. This was always a band-aid for something we didn't have a clear solution to.

With this update, we've removed the global cache and the btf.FlushKernelSpec function, which may slow down subsequent collection loading on busy systems. To opt back in, users can now maintain their own cache object, obtained from btf.NewCache and pass it to NewCollectionWithOptions via CollectionOptions.Cache. Typically, you would put this in a global variable in a bpf-related package in your application, or keep it around in function scope if you load multiple collections in a row.

See cilium/ebpf#1988 for more details. Thank you @​matthyx for these changes.

  • bpf2go: Generate constant names for maps, programs, and variables by @​mattijons in cilium/ebpf#1860
  • Allow link.OpenExecutable for files without executable bit set by @​ti-mo in cilium/ebpf#1982
  • asm: add support for the may_goto insn and JCOND opcode by @​mtardy in cilium/ebpf#1898

This is the first patch release in the 1.5.z release series of runc, and primarily includes a fix for a serious regression on Ubuntu 20.04 kernels.

Release notes

Sourced from github.com/moby/go-archive's releases.

v0.3.3

What's Changed

  • Fix a regression introduced in v0.3.0 that caused archive extraction to reject hardlinks with absolute targets, as produced by some image builders. Absolute hardlink targets are now resolved relative to the extraction root, while paths that escape the root remain rejected. moby/go-archive#100
  • Fix a regression introduced in v0.3.0 that caused archive extraction to fail when applying permissions to device nodes, including nodes on nodev filesystems and dev/ptmx. Device nodes are now referenced without opening the underlying device before applying their mode. moby/go-archive#103
  • Set close-on-exec on file descriptors used by the Linux permission fallback to prevent them from leaking into child processes. moby/go-archive#104

Full Changelog: https://github.com/moby/go-archive/compare/v0.3.2...v0.3.3

v0.3.2

What's Changed

Fix a regression introduced in v0.3.0 that caused archive extraction to fail when paths traversed absolute symlinks inside the destination root, such as var/run -> /run. Absolute symlink targets are now resolved relative to the extraction root while relative symlink escapes remain rejected. moby/go-archive#93

Full Changelog: https://github.com/moby/go-archive/compare/v0.3.1...v0.3.2

v0.3.1

Fixes

This patch release fixes a regression introduced in v0.2.1 where archive extraction could fail when an archive omitted explicit entries for parent directories. For example, extracting etc/dnf/ without a preceding etc/ entry could return mkdirat etc/dnf: no such file or directory.

This prevented affected images from being extracted. Archive extraction now creates implied parent directories for both file and directory entries.

What's Changed

  • archive: create implied parents for directory entries moby/go-archive#92
  • archive: Tarballer.Go: suppress io.ErrClosedPipe logs on close moby/go-archive#94

Full Changelog: https://github.com/moby/go-archive/compare/v0.3.0...v0.3.1

v0.3.0

Security

This release fixes CVE-2026-17106 / GHSA-hfg8-hc9c-6c3h, where a crafted tar archive could use links to cause extraction operations to create or overwrite files outside the intended destination directory.

The issue affected Unpack, UnpackLayer, Untar, UntarUncompressed, and the ApplyLayer helpers. Users should upgrade and avoid extracting untrusted archives with earlier versions.

What's Changed

  • archive: harden tar extraction against path traversal moby/go-archive#45
  • archive: do not follow reparse points in chtimes moby/go-archive#90

Bumps [github.com/buger/jsonparser](https://github.com/buger/jsonparser) from 1.3.1 to 1.6.1.
Release notes

Sourced from github.com/buger/jsonparser's releases.

v1.6.1 — Fastest across all payload sizes (now benchmarks vs gjson + sonic)

🔒 Covered by ReqProof — L3 Assurance (123 requirements, 0 errors, 0 warnings)

Performance — gjson-style fast-skip

Ported gjson's >'\\' single-comparison fast-skip to three hot loops. The trick skips all non-structural bytes (those > 0x5C) in one unsigned comparison per byte, reducing branch overhead.

Payload Before After Change
Small (190B) 382 ns 339 ns -11.3%
Medium (2.4kB) 3,899 ns 3,141 ns -19.4%
Large (24kB) 20,788 ns 20,114 ns -3.2%

Now benchmarks against gjson and sonic

Added tidwall/gjson (15.5k⭐) and bytedance/sonic (9.6k⭐) to the benchmark suite.

Large payload — the definitive ranking:

Library time/op allocs
jsonparser 20,114 ns 0
gjson 22,756 ns 2
easyjson 33,771 ns 134
sonic 41,053 ns 71
ffjson 59,063 ns 144
encoding/json 130,565 ns 147

jsonparser is the fastest across ALL payload sizes and the only zero-allocation parser.

title: feat: Make ldconfig optional for GPU library discovery
body:
Reviewer: @DrDaveD 

## Description of the Pull Request (PR):

Apptainer locates the GPU driver libraries named in nvliblist.conf and rocmliblist.conf by running "ldconfig -p". That fails on systems which do not populate an ld.so cache, or which do not ship ldconfig at all, such as NixOS and Guix, where the driver libraries live in unusual paths. On those hosts --nv and --rocm find nothing to bind.

Add a "gpu library path" option to apptainer.conf, holding a list of directories to search for those libraries. The configured directories are searched first, in order, and the ld.so cache becomes an optional secondary source: when ldconfig cannot be found or run, the configured directories are used on their own instead of the lookup coming up empty.

Entries which do not resolve, such as dangling symlinks, are skipped so that they cannot shadow a working library of the same name found in a lower priority location.

The warning issued when no libraries can be found now names the setting to configure, rather than only reporting that the ld cache is unreadable.

 - Fixes #1894

title: Problems with the `formats` doc
body: There are lots of warnings when generating the apptainer-userdocs that look like ``` /nashome/d/dwd/work/apptainer-userdocs/cli/apptainer_exec.rst:16: WARNING: Inline emphasis start-string without end-string. /nashome/d/dwd/work/apptainer-userdocs/cli/apptainer_exec.rst:18: WARNING: Inline emphasis start-string without end-string. /nashome/d/dwd/work/apptainer-userdocs/cli/apptainer_exec.rst:20: WARNING: Inline emphasis start-string without end-string. ``` That's because there are single asterisks in the `formats` string. Those can be avoided by inserting a backslash ahead of them, or just deleting those asterisks since they're not really required. The backslash shows up in `--help` output so it's probably better to delete them. At the same time, many of the lines in that file are showing up with a bold first part like seen in #3690: That happens whenever a line is continued onto the next line. Turning it into a single long line helps with the doc but then the `--help` output doesn't wrap. The problem is that rst expects related lines to be indented at the same level. There also needs to be some kind of a separator besides a bunch of blank spaces. Probably the thing to do is to take advantage of the formatting and list the format at one level and indent the descriptions.
