title: `python -c "from rattler import *"` continually triggers apptainer hang
body:
### Version of Apptainer

```
$ pixi run -e py314 apptainer --version
apptainer version 1.4.5
```

### Expected behavior

`pixi run -e py314 apptainer exec docker://condaforge/miniforge3:26.3.2-3 python -c "from rattler import *"` should run to completion, so does `pixi run -e py314 apptainer exec --cwd '/tmp/snakemake-test_singularity_conda-da5g1vss' --bind '/tmp':'/tmp' docker://condaforge/miniforge3:26.3.2-3 bash -c 'pip install snakemake-software-deployment-plugin-conda==0.7.0 >&2 && python -c "import snakemake_software_deployment_plugin_conda" '`.

### Actual behavior

The command **intermittently hangs forever**, and then can only be stopped from another terminal with `pkill -9 -f squashfuse_ll`; the panic trace below is what surfaces once the FUSE daemon is killed:

```sh
$ pixi run -e py314 apptainer exec docker://condaforge/miniforge3:26.3.2-3 python -c "from rattler import *"
INFO:    Using cached SIF image
INFO:    fuse2fs not found, will not be able to mount EXT3 filesystems

thread '<unnamed>' (254710) panicked at src/networking/client.rs:62:53:
called `Result::unwrap()` on an `Err` value: reqwest::Error { kind: Builder, source: General("No CA certificates were loaded from the system") }
note: run with `RUST_BACKTRACE=1` environment variable to display a backtrace
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "<string>", line 1, in <module>
  File "$PYTHON/site-packages/rattler/__init__.py", line 50, in <module>
    from rattler.solver import solve, solve_with_sparse_repodata
  File "$PYTHON/site-packages/rattler/solver/__init__.py", line 1, in <module>
    from rattler.solver.solver import solve, solve_with_sparse_repodata
  File "$PYTHON/site-packages/rattler/repo_data/gateway.py", line 155, in __init__
    self._gateway = PyGateway(
pyo3_runtime.PanicException: called `Result::unwrap()` on an `Err` value: reqwest::Error { kind: Builder, source: General("No CA certificates were loaded from the system") }
```

```sh
$ ps -eo pid,ppid,stat,wchan,etime,cmd | grep -E "python" |grep apptainer
 268371  224459 Sl+  futex_       00:31 pixi run -e py314 apptainer exec docker://condaforge/miniforge3:26.3.2-3 python -c from rattler import *
$ pkill -9 -f squashfuse_ll  # triggers `thread '<unnamed>' (254710) panicked at src/networking/client.rs:62:53:` and followings
```

Notably, the "missing" CA file is actually **present and readable** inside the container:

```sh
$ pixi run -e py314 apptainer exec docker://condaforge/miniforge3:26.3.2-3 bash -c 'wc -l /etc/ssl/certs/ca-certificates.crt'
INFO:    Using cached SIF image
INFO:    fuse2fs not found, will not be able to mount EXT3 filesystems
3000
```

Binding the CA bundle in clears the panic, but the run **still hangs**:

```sh
$ pixi run -e py314 apptainer exec --bind /etc/ssl/certs:/etc/ssl/certs docker://condaforge/miniforge3:26.3.2-3 python -c "from rattler import *"
INFO:    Using cached SIF image
INFO:    fuse2fs not found, will not be able to mount EXT3 filesystems
# hangs here
```

Extracting the same image to a plain directory with `apptainer build --sandbox` and running the identical import **completes instantly**:

```sh
$ pixi run -e py314 apptainer exec --cwd '/tmp/snakemake-test_singularity_conda-da5g1vss' /tmp/miniforge3-sandbox bash -c 'python -c "import snakemake_software_deployment_plugin_conda; print(1)"'
1
```

So rattler is failing to read a file that is present and readable, which points at the file-reading layer (squashfs via FUSE, i.e. SIF) rather than the code. `rattler`'s import is a reliable trigger because it does many file reads (large shared libraries + system CA bundle + statx) in a short time window.

### Steps to reproduce this behavior

Requires `pixi` with a `py314` environment containing `apptainer` and the python `rattler` package (both from conda-forge/pypi). Then repeat:

```sh
$ pixi run -e py314 apptainer exec docker://condaforge/miniforge3:26.3.2-3 python -c "from rattler import *"
```

until it hangs (intermittent; roughly one in a few runs in our environment). Once hung, only `pkill -9 -f squashfuse_ll` restores things, after which the panic above surfaces.

### What OS/distro are you running

```sh
$ cat /etc/os-release
PRETTY_NAME="Ubuntu 22.04.4 LTS"
NAME="Ubuntu"
VERSION_ID="22.04"
VERSION="22.04.4 LTS (Jammy Jellyfish)"
VERSION_CODENAME=jammy
ID=ubuntu
ID_LIKE=debian
HOME_URL="https://www.ubuntu.com/"
SUPPORT_URL="https://help.ubuntu.com/"
BUG_REPORT_URL="https://bugs.launchpad.net/ubuntu/"
PRIVACY_POLICY_URL="https://www.ubuntu.com/legal/terms-and-policies/privacy-policy"
UBUNTU_CODENAME=jammy
```

Running under WSL2:

```sh
$ uname -a
Linux Matebook14 6.6.87.2-microsoft-standard-WSL2 #1 SMP PREEMPT_DYNAMIC Thu Jun  5 18:30:46 UTC 2025 x86_64 x86_64 x86_64 GNU/Linux
```

The same hang was also observed in a GitHub Actions CI (native Linux) runner.

### How did you install Apptainer

via pixi from pyproject.toml of snakemake (conda-forge `apptainer` 1.4.5, which pulls `squashfuse 0.6.1` and `squashfs-tools`).

### Additional context

See https://github.com/snakemake/snakemake/pull/3339#issuecomment-5216168878 for the originating snakemake discussion.

Sourced from github.com/opencontainers/runc's releases.

runc v1.5.0 -- "Why do we even have that lever?!"

This is the somewhat-delayed^Wlong-awaited first stable release of the 1.5.z release branch of runc. It contains a handful of fixes for issues found in 1.5.0-rc.3 and an important dependency bump for libpathrs.

This is the third release of runc following our new release and support policy (see RELEASES.md for more details). This means that, as of this release:

  • The runc 1.2.z (and earlier) release branches are now completely unsupported.
  • The runc 1.3.z release branch will now only receive high severity CVE fixes, and will no longer be supported in less than 6 months (end of October 2026).
  • The runc 1.4.z release branch will now only recieve security and "significant" bugfixes.
  • Users are encouraged to plan migrating to runc 1.5.0 as soon as possible.
  • Despite this release being delayed by over a month, users should still expect a runc 1.6.0 release in late October 2026.

Added

  • runc version and runc features now provide version information about libpathrs (when runc is built with the libpathrs build tag). (#5291, #5328)

Fixed

Changed

  • runc (when built with the libpathrs build tag) now depends on libpathrs v0.2.5 or later, and attempting to build with older versions will cause compilation errors. (#5291, #5328)
  • Switched to go-criu v8.3.0, which reduces our binary size from ~16MB to ~14MB. (#5312, #5326)

Release notes

Sourced from github.com/moby/go-archive's releases.

v0.3.2

What's Changed

Fix a regression introduced in v0.3.0 that caused archive extraction to fail when paths traversed absolute symlinks inside the destination root, such as var/run -> /run. Absolute symlink targets are now resolved relative to the extraction root while relative symlink escapes remain rejected. moby/go-archive#93

Full Changelog: https://github.com/moby/go-archive/compare/v0.3.1...v0.3.2

v0.3.1

Fixes

This patch release fixes a regression introduced in v0.2.1 where archive extraction could fail when an archive omitted explicit entries for parent directories. For example, extracting etc/dnf/ without a preceding etc/ entry could return mkdirat etc/dnf: no such file or directory.

This prevented affected images from being extracted. Archive extraction now creates implied parent directories for both file and directory entries.

What's Changed

  • archive: create implied parents for directory entries moby/go-archive#92
  • archive: Tarballer.Go: suppress io.ErrClosedPipe logs on close moby/go-archive#94

Full Changelog: https://github.com/moby/go-archive/compare/v0.3.0...v0.3.1

v0.3.0

Security

This release fixes CVE-2026-17106 / GHSA-hfg8-hc9c-6c3h, where a crafted tar archive could use links to cause extraction operations to create or overwrite files outside the intended destination directory.

The issue affected Unpack, UnpackLayer, Untar, UntarUncompressed, and the ApplyLayer helpers. Users should upgrade and avoid extracting untrusted archives with earlier versions.

What's Changed

But it is.. undocumented [here](https://apptainer.org/docs/user/main/build_a_container.html) or [there](https://apptainer.org/docs/user/main/cli/apptainer_build.html#apptainer-build)?

title: Add --writable-tmpfs-size argument
body:
## Description of the Pull Request (PR):

This PR adds `--writable-tmpfs-size` argument to control the size of the disposable overlay that is created, simialar how #1313 and https://github.com/apptainer/singularity/issues/5718 discussed.


This would be particularly useful for one-line commands. While `--overlay` offers similar functionality, it requires manually running `mkdir /tmp/overlay` (or `apptainer overlay create`), launching Apptainer, and then performing cleanup. The cleanup process is especially tricky with `--fakeroot`, as it can create files owned by sub-UIDs that a standard `rm` cannot delete (I have to do this multiple times a day).

In my experience, increasing the `tmpfs` size to 10GB in `apptainer.conf` was a helpful workaround, but it requires creating a custom configuration file and setting `APPTAINER_CONFIGDIR`.

It would be ideal to have direct control over the size via command-line arguments, especially since everything runs in userspace for non-setuid installations. A feature similar to `docker run --rm` that automatically cleans up leftovers would be incredibly helpful.


### This fixes or addresses the following GitHub issues:

 - Fixes #1313

title: APPTAINER_PULLDIR breaks `pull --name` when destination is an absolute path
body:
### Version of Apptainer

```
$ apptainer --version
apptainer version 1.5.0-1.el9
```
### Expected behavior

When setting APPTAINER_PULLDIR and specifying an absolute output path with --name, I expect Apptainer to write the resulting SIF image to the path provided.

e.g.:

```
export APPTAINER_PULLDIR=/tmp/apptainer-pull
apptainer pull --name /tmp/test.sif docker://alpine
```
should create
```
/tmp/test.sif
```
### Actual behavior

The pull fails when APPTAINER_PULLDIR is set to a non-empty value.

The failure occurs during the stage where the cached SIF image is copied to the requested output location.

### Steps to reproduce this behavior

```
export APPTAINER_PULLDIR=/tmp/pull
mkdir -p $APPTAINER_PULLDIR

apptainer pull --name /tmp/test.sif docker://alpine
# Fails

APPTAINER_PULLDIR= 
apptainer pull --name /tmp/test.sif docker://alpine
# Succeeds
```

### What OS/distro are you running

Rocky Linux 9.8 (Blue Onyx)

### How did you install Apptainer

Installed from RPM package

body:
Bumps [github.com/buger/jsonparser](https://github.com/buger/jsonparser) from 1.2.0 to 1.3.1.
Release notes

Sourced from github.com/buger/jsonparser's releases.

v1.3.1 — Bug fixes + proof strengthening

Bug fixes

  • Fix Set/Delete input-buffer aliasing (#209, #141) — Set and Delete no longer corrupt the caller's input []byte when the slice has spare capacity. The append() call path was writing into the backing array beyond the returned slice. Now all mutation paths allocate a fresh buffer.

  • Fix EachKey array-index inconsistency (#232) — EachKey now descends into terminal array-index paths (e.g. "key", "[0]") consistently with Get. Previously EachKey returned empty where Get succeeded on the same path.

  • Fix benchmark measuring ffjson, not encoding/json (#126) — the benchmark payload types had ffjson-generated MarshalJSON/UnmarshalJSON methods, so the "10x faster than encoding/json" comparison was silently measuring ffjson. Now uses plain types with no generated methods.

Proof strengthening (how these bugs escaped, and the gates that prevent recurrence)

Bug Proof gap New gate
#209/#141 Set aliasing No obligation said "Set must not mutate the input buffer" New obligation no_input_mutation + assertInputUnchanged gate (snapshots input + backing-array capacity before every Set/Delete, verifies unchanged after)
#232 EachKey ≠ Get No obligation said "EachKey must resolve paths identically to Get" New obligation api_consistency + TestApiConsistencyEachKeyMatchesGet gate (random JSON + paths, asserts EachKey result == Get result)
#126 benchmark ffjson Proof didn't cover the benchmark suite Benchmark honesty lint: verifies no benchmark type implements json.Marshaler/json.Unmarshaler

Contributed by codex (gpt-5-codex) via codex exec.

v1.3.0 — Formally verified by ReqProof (L3 Assurance)

🔒 Formally verified by ReqProof

jsonparser v1.3.0 is the first Go library proven to L3 assurance by ReqProof — a git-native requirements-engineering and formal-verification platform. Every public API is traced to a formal requirement, every requirement is tested with 100% MC/DC coverage, and the entire parser is fuzzed by a custom structure-aware JSON fuzzer at 250k inputs/sec.

Release notes

Sourced from github.com/opencontainers/runc's releases.

runc v1.5.0 -- "Why do we even have that lever?!"

This is the somewhat-delayed^Wlong-awaited first stable release of the 1.5.z release branch of runc. It contains a handful of fixes for issues found in 1.5.0-rc.3 and an important dependency bump for libpathrs.

This is the third release of runc following our new release and support policy (see RELEASES.md for more details). This means that, as of this release:

  • The runc 1.2.z (and earlier) release branches are now completely unsupported.
  • The runc 1.3.z release branch will now only receive high severity CVE fixes, and will no longer be supported in less than 6 months (end of October 2026).
  • The runc 1.4.z release branch will now only recieve security and "significant" bugfixes.
  • Users are encouraged to plan migrating to runc 1.5.0 as soon as possible.
  • Despite this release being delayed by over a month, users should still expect a runc 1.6.0 release in late October 2026.

Added

  • runc version and runc features now provide version information about libpathrs (when runc is built with the libpathrs build tag). (#5291, #5328)

Bumps [github.com/buger/jsonparser](https://github.com/buger/jsonparser) from 1.2.0 to 1.3.1.
Release notes

Sourced from github.com/buger/jsonparser's releases.

v1.3.1 — Bug fixes + proof strengthening

Bug fixes

  • Fix Set/Delete input-buffer aliasing (#209, #141) — Set and Delete no longer corrupt the caller's input []byte when the slice has spare capacity. The append() call path was writing into the backing array beyond the returned slice. Now all mutation paths allocate a fresh buffer.

  • Fix EachKey array-index inconsistency (#232) — EachKey now descends into terminal array-index paths (e.g. "key", "[0]") consistently with Get. Previously EachKey returned empty where Get succeeded on the same path.

  • Fix benchmark measuring ffjson, not encoding/json (#126) — the benchmark payload types had ffjson-generated MarshalJSON/UnmarshalJSON methods, so the "10x faster than encoding/json" comparison was silently measuring ffjson. Now uses plain types with no generated methods.

Proof strengthening (how these bugs escaped, and the gates that prevent recurrence)

Bug Proof gap New gate
#209/#141 Set aliasing No obligation said "Set must not mutate the input buffer" New obligation no_input_mutation + assertInputUnchanged gate (snapshots input + backing-array capacity before every Set/Delete, verifies unchanged after)
#232 EachKey ≠ Get No obligation said "EachKey must resolve paths identically to Get" New obligation api_consistency + TestApiConsistencyEachKeyMatchesGet gate (random JSON + paths, asserts EachKey result == Get result)
#126 benchmark ffjson Proof didn't cover the benchmark suite Benchmark honesty lint: verifies no benchmark type implements json.Marshaler/json.Unmarshaler

Contributed by codex (gpt-5-codex) via codex exec.

v1.3.0 — Formally verified by ReqProof (L3 Assurance)

🔒 Formally verified by ReqProof

jsonparser v1.3.0 is the first Go library proven to L3 assurance by ReqProof — a git-native requirements-engineering and formal-verification platform. Every public API is traced to a formal requirement, every requirement is tested with 100% MC/DC coverage, and the entire parser is fuzzed by a custom structure-aware JSON fuzzer at 250k inputs/sec.

The proof review caught 7 real bugs that years of community use, OSS-Fuzz, and standard fuzzing had missed.

Performance

  • parseInt fast-path — 22–37% faster on short integers — @​trevorprater (#285)
  • stringEnd SIMD fast path — 12× faster on no-escape strings

Acknowledgments

Thank you to @​c-tonneslan, @​Solaris-star, @​trevorprater, and OSS-Fuzz for the reports and contributions.

jsonparser v1.3.0 is the first Go library proven to L3 assurance by ReqProof, a git-native requirements-engineering and formal-verification platform. The entire codebase is now covered by:

  • 118 formal requirements (7 stakeholder + 111 system-level), each traced to code via source annotations and verified with FRETish formalization.

title: Auto-detect tmp-on-tmpfs for APPTAINER_TMPDIR
body:
Now that more and more distributions are using the systemd tmpfs for /tmp,
maybe this should be automatically detected to avoid APPTAINER_TMPDIR

Currently the packaging needs an override `APPTAINER_TMPDIR=/var/tmp`,
due to /tmp being mounted with "nodev" (and possible too small, being RAM)

* https://github.com/lima-vm/lima/pull/1085 (fedora)

* https://github.com/lima-vm/lima/pull/5331 (ubuntu)

----

Previously Fedora 18+

https://fedoraproject.org/wiki/Features/tmp-on-tmpfs

Now also Ubuntu 24.10+

https://documentation.ubuntu.com/release-notes/26.04/summary-for-lts-users/#systemd-259


BEFORE (24.04)

```
Filesystem      Size  Used Avail Use% Mounted on
/dev/vda1        96G  1.9G   94G   2% /
```

AFTER (26.04)

```
TARGET SOURCE FSTYPE OPTIONS
/tmp   tmpfs  tmpfs  rw,nosuid,nodev,nr_inodes=1048576,inode64,usrquota

Filesystem      Size  Used Avail Use% Mounted on
tmpfs           2.0G     0  2.0G   0% /tmp
```

Changelog

  • The new GET /images/{name}/attestations endpoint returns in-toto attestation statements (such as SLSA provenance and SPDX SBOM) attached to an image, with optional platform selection, predicate type filtering, and an opt-in statement query parameter for retrieving the verbatim statement bodies.   • Builder: ENTRYPOINT instruction sets a default binary entry point to a container
  • Builder: VOLUME instruction marks a part of the container as persistent data
  • Builder: 'docker build' displays the full output of a build by default
  • Runtime: 'docker login' supports additional options
  • Runtime: Dont save a container's hostname when committing an image.
  • Registry: Fix issues when uploading images to a private registry

  • Runtime: Fix a bug which caused 'docker run -d' to no longer print the container ID.
  • Tests: Fix issues in the test suite

  • Registry: easier push/pull to a custom registry
  • Remote API: the progress bar updates faster when downloading and uploading large files

  • Runtime: improve detection of kernel version
  • Runtime: host directories can be mounted as volumes with 'docker run -b'
  • Runtime: fix an issue when only attaching to stdin

  • Hack: improve test suite and dev environment

0.4.6 (2013-06-22)

  • Runtime: fix a bug which caused creation of empty images (and volumes) to crash.

  • Runtime: 'docker ps -s' optionally prints container size

0.4.4 (2013-06-19)

title: Merge release-1.5 into main after 1.5.3 release
Update golang.org/x/net to v0.55.0 (release-1.5)
body:
Builds in Fedora rawhide are dying with a message 
```
vendor/google.golang.org/grpc/internal/transport/handler_server.go:271:18: undefined: http2.TrailerPrefix
```
which is related to the fact that rawhide is building with golang-1.27-rc2.

However, according to https://repojournal.com/showcase/golang/2026-05-09 that was an early problem with 1.27 but it should have been fixed by the time rc1 was released in June and surely by rc2 in July.  kubernetes/kubernetes#139257 describes the problem fixed by updating to golang.org/x/net v0.55.0 so I'm trying that.

title: Update to `nvliblist.conf` required for NVIDIA Orin Nano developer boards?
body:
### Version of Apptainer

Not from a specific Appptainer version, but I did test apptainer. In [EESSI](https://www.eessi.io/docs/) I use the same `nvliblist.conf` as `apptainer` to know what NVIDIA libraries I should symlink so that the EESSI runtime linker can find them.

<!-- please include command-line output in a code block -->

### Expected behavior

We ship compiled binaries with CUDA capabilities, after symlinking driver libraries based on the contents of `nvliblist.conf`, those binaries should be able to run successfully.

### Actual behavior

I bought a Jetson Orin Nano developer board and expected to work as for other GPUs. The way the GPU works there though seems to be slightly different and there are quite a few additional libraries from NVIDIA. 

After our normal script to link the drivers (based off `nvliblist.conf`) the binaries could not execute. Running `strace` I could see they are trying to load libraries which were not linked. After linking additional drivers the binaries ran successfully.

I tried `apptainer`, running the example at https://apptainer.org/docs/user/latest/gpu.html#example-tensorflow-gpu but that container is `x86_64` only. I tried a simple CUDA container,  but this could not even run `nvidia-smi`.

title: Using encrypted images without SUID installation
body:
TLDR: Is it a hard requirement to have the SUID installation of Apptainer to use encrypted images or is there some other way? We are using it on a HPC cluster and would rather avoid SUID binaries.
Is there documentation about that requirement already?

### Version of Apptainer

`apptainer version 1.5.3`

### Expected behavior

Use of encrypted image works.

### Actual behavior

Error shown:

```
$ singularity shell --pem-path img.key img
INFO:    Detected Singularity user configuration directory
INFO:    Try appending ':ro' to your overlay image or using '--fakeroot'
FATAL:   container creation failed: mount hook function failure: mount /proc/self/fd/10->/var/lib/apptainer/mnt/session/rootfs error: while mounting image /proc/self/fd/10: failed to find loop device: could not attach image file to loop device: failed to attach loop device: could not open /dev/loop0: permission denied
```

### Steps to reproduce this behavior

Run `singularity shell --pem-path img.key img` on an encrypted image

### What OS/distro are you running

Linux Mint 22.3

### How did you install Apptainer

`apt install apptainer`

One can check with:
```
$ apptainer buildcfg | grep -i suid
APPTAINER_SUID_INSTALL=0
```

Bumps [google.golang.org/grpc](https://github.com/grpc/grpc-go) from 1.81.1 to 1.82.1.
Release notes

Sourced from google.golang.org/grpc's releases.

Release 1.82.1

Security

  • server: Stop reading from the connection when flooded by HTTP/2 frames. The default value for this limit is 100 frames, excluding DATA and HEADERS, and may be changed by setting environment variable GRPC_GO_EXPERIMENTAL_CONTROL_BUFFER_THROTTLE_LIMIT.
  • xds/rbac: Support Metadata and RequestedServerName permissions matcher fields. If present in a DENY rule, previously these would be ignored and fail-open.
  • xds/rbac: Fix panic when parsing unsupported fields in NotRule/NotId permissions.
  • xds/rbac: Support the deprecated source_ip principal identifier by treating it as equivalent to direct_remote_ip.

Release 1.82.0

Behavior Changes

  • server: Remove support for GRPC_GO_EXPERIMENTAL_DISABLE_STRICT_PATH_CHECKING environment varibale. Strict incoming RPC path validation (which has been the default since v1.79.3) can no longer be disabled. (#9112)
  • transport: Add environment variable to change the default max header list size from 16MB to 8KB. This may be enabled by setting GRPC_GO_EXPERIMENTAL_ENABLE_8KB_DEFAULT_HEADER_LIST_SIZE=true. This will be enabled by default in a subsequent release. (#9019)
  • balancer: Load Balancing policy registry is now case-sensitive. Set GRPC_GO_EXPERIMENTAL_CASE_SENSITIVE_BALANCER_REGISTRIES=false (and file an issue) to revert to case-insensitive behavior. (#9017)

New Features

  • experimental/stats: Expose a new API, NewContextWithLabelCallback, to register a callback that is invoked when telemetry labels are added. (#8877)
    • Special Thanks: @​seth-epps
  • client: Return a portion of the response body in the error message, when the client receives an unexpected non-gRPC HTTP response, to make debugging easier. (#8929)
    • Special Thanks: @​chengxilo
  • server: Add environment variable GRPC_GO_SERVER_GOROUTINE_LABELS that controls setting runtime/pprof.Labels on goroutines spawned by the server. Set GRPC_GO_SERVER_GOROUTINE_LABELS=grpc.method=true to add the grpc.method label on goroutines spawned to handle incoming requests. (#9082)
    • Special Thanks: @​dfinkel

Bug Fixes

  • xds/server: Fix a memory leak of HTTP filter instances occurring when route configurations are updated in-place during a Route Discovery Service (RDS) update. (#9138)
  • grpc: In the deprecated gzip Compressor (used via the deprecated WithCompressor dial option), enforce the MaxRecvMsgSize limit on the decompressed message buffer, preventing excessive memory allocation from highly compressed payloads. (#9114)
    • Special Thanks: @​evilgensec
  • stats/opentelemetry: Record retry attempts, grpc.previous-rpc-attempts, at the call level and not the attempt level. (#8923)
  • encoding: Ensure Close() is always called on readers returned from Compressor.Decompress if possible. (#9135)
  • channelz: Fix the LastMessageSentTimestamp and LastMessageReceivedTimestamp fields in SocketMetrics to ensure they contain correct timestamp values. (#9109)

Release notes

Sourced from github.com/opencontainers/runc's releases.

runc v1.5.0 -- "Why do we even have that lever?!"

This is the somewhat-delayed^Wlong-awaited first stable release of the 1.5.z release branch of runc. It contains a handful of fixes for issues found in 1.5.0-rc.3 and an important dependency bump for libpathrs.

This is the third release of runc following our new release and support policy (see RELEASES.md for more details). This means that, as of this release:

  • The runc 1.2.z (and earlier) release branches are now completely unsupported.
  • The runc 1.3.z release branch will now only receive high severity CVE fixes, and will no longer be supported in less than 6 months (end of October 2026).
  • The runc 1.4.z release branch will now only recieve security and "significant" bugfixes.
  • Users are encouraged to plan migrating to runc 1.5.0 as soon as possible.
  • Despite this release being delayed by over a month, users should still expect a runc 1.6.0 release in late October 2026.

Added

  • runc version and runc features now provide version information about libpathrs (when runc is built with the libpathrs build tag). (#5291, #5328)

Fixed

Changed

client/0.5.0

0.5.0

Changelog

  • The new GET /images/{name}/attestations endpoint returns in-toto attestation statements (such as SLSA provenance and SPDX SBOM) attached to an image, with optional platform selection, predicate type filtering, and an opt-in statement query parameter for retrieving the verbatim statement bodies. 0.5.0 (2013-07-17)

  • Runtime: List all processes running inside a container with 'docker top'

  • Runtime: Containers can expose public UDP ports (eg, '-p 123/udp')
  • Runtime: Optionally specify an exact public port (eg. '-p 80:4500')
  • Registry: New image naming scheme inspired by Go packaging convention allows arbitrary combinations of registries
  • Builder: ENTRYPOINT instruction sets a default binary entry point to a container
  • Builder: VOLUME instruction marks a part of the container as persistent data
  • Builder: 'docker build' displays the full output of a build by default
  • Runtime: 'docker login' supports additional options
  • Runtime: Dont save a container's hostname when committing an image.
  • Registry: Fix issues when uploading images to a private registry

  • Builder: New build operation ENTRYPOINT adds an executable entry point to the container.
  • Runtime: Fix a bug which caused 'docker run -d' to no longer print the container ID.
  • Tests: Fix issues in the test suite

  • Registry: easier push/pull to a custom registry
  • Remote API: the progress bar updates faster when downloading and uploading large files
  • Remote API: fix a bug in the optional unix socket transport
  • Runtime: improve detection of kernel version
  • Runtime: host directories can be mounted as volumes with 'docker run -b'
  • Runtime: fix an issue when only attaching to stdin
  • Runtime: use 'tar --numeric-owner' to avoid uid mismatch across multiple hosts
  • Hack: improve test suite and dev environment
  • Hack: remove dependency on unit tests on 'os/user'
  • Documentation: add terminology section

0.4.6 (2013-06-22)

  • Runtime: fix a bug which caused creation of empty images (and volumes) to crash.

  • Builder: 'docker build git://URL' fetches and builds a remote git repository
  • Runtime: 'docker ps -s' optionally prints container size
  • Tests: Improved and simplified

  • Builder: fix a regression when using ADD with single regular file.

0.4.4 (2013-06-19)

  • Builder: fix a regression introduced in 0.4.3 which caused builds to fail on new clients.

0.4.3 (2013-06-19)

  • Builder: ADD of a local file will detect tar archives and unpack them
  • Runtime: Remove bsdtar dependency
  • Runtime: Add unix socket and multiple -H support

title: ".singularity.d/libs/fakeroot: getopt: command not found" during container build
body:
Apptainer fails to build containers with fakeroot on AlmaLinux 10.2

### Version of Apptainer

```shell
$ apptainer --version
apptainer version 1.5.2-1.el10_2
```

### Actual behavior

```shell
$ cat test.def
Bootstrap: docker
From: quay.io/almalinuxorg/almalinux:10

%post

    dnf -y install vim

$ apptainer build test.sif test.def
INFO:    User not listed in /etc/subuid, trying root-mapped namespace
INFO:    The %post section will be run under the fakeroot command
INFO:    Starting build...
INFO:    Fetching OCI image...
65.4MiB / 65.4MiB [=============================================================================================] 100 % 0.0 b/s 0s
INFO:    Extracting OCI image...
INFO:    Inserting Apptainer configuration...
INFO:    Running post scriptlet
/.singularity.d/libs/fakeroot: line 46: getopt: command not found
/.singularity.d/libs/fakeroot: line 50: getopt: command not found
fakeroot, create a fake root environment.
   usage: fakeroot [-l|--lib fakerootlib] [-f|--faked fakedbin]
                   [-i file] [-s file] [-u|--unknown-is-real]
		   [-b|--fd-base fd] [-h|--help] [-v|--version]
                   [--] [command]
INFO:    If error was from fakeroot, try --ignore-fakeroot-command and
INFO:      maybe use fakeroot inside the %post section as described at
INFO:      https://apptainer.org/docs/user/latest/fakeroot.html#fakeroot-inside-def
FATAL:   While performing build: while running engine: while running %post section: exit status 1
```

### What OS/distro are you running

```shell
$ uname -a
Linux test 6.12.0-211.30.1.el10_2.x86_64 #1 SMP PREEMPT_DYNAMIC Fri Jul  3 09:07:20 EDT 2026 x86_64 GNU/Linux

$ cat /etc/os-release
```

RPM package from EPEL

Using the workaround mentioned in #1863 (and workaround in #3597), it is possible to build the container:

Updates `github.com/opencontainers/runc` from 1.4.2 to 1.5.0
Release notes

Sourced from github.com/opencontainers/runc's releases.

runc v1.5.0 -- "Why do we even have that lever?!"

This is the somewhat-delayed^Wlong-awaited first stable release of the 1.5.z release branch of runc. It contains a handful of fixes for issues found in 1.5.0-rc.3 and an important dependency bump for libpathrs.

This is the third release of runc following our new release and support policy (see RELEASES.md for more details). This means that, as of this release:

  • The runc 1.2.z (and earlier) release branches are now completely unsupported.
  • The runc 1.3.z release branch will now only receive high severity CVE fixes, and will no longer be supported in less than 6 months (end of October 2026).
  • The runc 1.4.z release branch will now only recieve security and "significant" bugfixes.
  • Users are encouraged to plan migrating to runc 1.5.0 as soon as possible.
  • Despite this release being delayed by over a month, users should still expect a runc 1.6.0 release in late October 2026.

Added

  • runc version and runc features now provide version information about libpathrs (when runc is built with the libpathrs build tag). (#5291, #5328)

Fixed

  • Since runc 1.3.0, the org.opencontainers.runc.version annotation included in runc features contained an extraneous \n, possibly causing issues with tools that parse the output. It is now properly stripped. (#5329, #5330, #5331, #5335)

Changed

  • runc (when built with the libpathrs build tag) now depends on libpathrs v0.2.5 or later, and attempting to build with older versions will cause compilation errors. (#5291, #5328)
  • Switched to go-criu v8.3.0, which reduces our binary size from ~16MB to ~14MB. (#5312, #5326)

Static Linking Notices

The runc binaries distributed with this release are statically linked with the following GNU LGPL-2.1 licensed libraries, with runc acting as a "work that uses the Library":

client/0.5.0

0.5.0

Changelog

  • The new GET /images/{name}/attestations endpoint returns in-toto attestation statements (such as SLSA provenance and SPDX SBOM) attached to an image, with optional platform selection, predicate type filtering, and an opt-in statement query parameter for retrieving the verbatim statement bodies. Changelog

Tools can now retrieve attestation metadata and content directly from the daemon instead of performing additional registry round-trips. moby/moby#52636

0.5.0 (2013-07-17)

  • Runtime: List all processes running inside a container with 'docker top'
  • Runtime: Host directories can be mounted as volumes with 'docker run -v'
  • Runtime: Containers can expose public UDP ports (eg, '-p 123/udp')
  • Runtime: Optionally specify an exact public port (eg. '-p 80:4500')
  • Registry: New image naming scheme inspired by Go packaging convention allows arbitrary combinations of registries
  • Builder: ENTRYPOINT instruction sets a default binary entry point to a container
  • Builder: VOLUME instruction marks a part of the container as persistent data
  • Builder: 'docker build' displays the full output of a build by default
  • Runtime: 'docker login' supports additional options
  • Runtime: Dont save a container's hostname when committing an image.
  • Registry: Fix issues when uploading images to a private registry

0.4.8 (2013-07-01)

  • Builder: New build operation ENTRYPOINT adds an executable entry point to the container.
  • Runtime: Fix a bug which caused 'docker run -d' to no longer print the container ID.
  • Tests: Fix issues in the test suite

0.4.7 (2013-06-28)

  • Registry: easier push/pull to a custom registry
  • Remote API: the progress bar updates faster when downloading and uploading large files
  • Remote API: fix a bug in the optional unix socket transport
  • Runtime: improve detection of kernel version
  • Runtime: host directories can be mounted as volumes with 'docker run -b'
  • Runtime: fix an issue when only attaching to stdin
  • Runtime: use 'tar --numeric-owner' to avoid uid mismatch across multiple hosts
  • Hack: improve test suite and dev environment
  • Hack: remove dependency on unit tests on 'os/user'
  • Documentation: add terminology section

0.4.6 (2013-06-22)

  • Runtime: fix a bug which caused creation of empty images (and volumes) to crash.

0.4.5 (2013-06-21)

  • Builder: 'docker build git://URL' fetches and builds a remote git repository
  • Runtime: 'docker ps -s' optionally prints container size
  • Tests: Improved and simplified
  • Runtime: fix a regression introduced in 0.4.3 which caused the logs command to fail.
  • Builder: fix a regression when using ADD with single regular file.

0.4.4 (2013-06-19)

  • Builder: fix a regression introduced in 0.4.3 which caused builds to fail on new clients.

0.4.3 (2013-06-19)

  • Builder: ADD of a local file will detect tar archives and unpack them
  • Runtime: Remove bsdtar dependency
  • Runtime: Add unix socket and multiple -H support

Updates `github.com/opencontainers/runc` from 1.4.2 to 1.5.0
Release notes

Sourced from github.com/opencontainers/runc's releases.

runc v1.5.0 -- "Why do we even have that lever?!"

This is the somewhat-delayed^Wlong-awaited first stable release of the 1.5.z release branch of runc. It contains a handful of fixes for issues found in 1.5.0-rc.3 and an important dependency bump for libpathrs.

This is the third release of runc following our new release and support policy (see RELEASES.md for more details). This means that, as of this release:

  • The runc 1.2.z (and earlier) release branches are now completely unsupported.
  • The runc 1.3.z release branch will now only receive high severity CVE fixes, and will no longer be supported in less than 6 months (end of October 2026).
  • The runc 1.4.z release branch will now only recieve security and "significant" bugfixes.
  • Users are encouraged to plan migrating to runc 1.5.0 as soon as possible.
  • Despite this release being delayed by over a month, users should still expect a runc 1.6.0 release in late October 2026.

Added

  • runc version and runc features now provide version information about libpathrs (when runc is built with the libpathrs build tag). (#5291, #5328)

Fixed

  • Since runc 1.3.0, the org.opencontainers.runc.version annotation included in runc features contained an extraneous \n, possibly causing issues with tools that parse the output. It is now properly stripped. (#5329, #5330, #5331, #5335)

Changed

  • runc (when built with the libpathrs build tag) now depends on libpathrs v0.2.5 or later, and attempting to build with older versions will cause compilation errors. (#5291, #5328)
  • Switched to go-criu v8.3.0, which reduces our binary size from ~16MB to ~14MB. (#5312, #5326)

Static Linking Notices

The runc binaries distributed with this release are statically linked with the following GNU LGPL-2.1 licensed libraries, with runc acting as a "work that uses the Library":

... (truncated)

Changelog

Sourced from github.com/opencontainers/runc's changelog.

[1.5.0] - 2026-06-19

Why do we even have that lever?!

Added

  • runc version and runc features now provide version information about libpathrs (when runc is built with the libpathrs build tag). (#5291, #5328)

Fixed

  • Since runc 1.3.0, the org.opencontainers.runc.version annotation included in runc features contained an extraneous \n, possibly causing issues with tools that parse the output. It is now properly stripped. (#5329, #5330, #5331, #5335)

Changed

  • runc (when built with the libpathrs build tag) now depends on libpathrs v0.2.5 or later, and attempting to build with older versions will cause compilation errors. (#5291, #5328)
  • Switched to go-criu v8.3.0, which reduces our binary size from ~16MB to ~14MB. (#5312, #5326)

[1.5.0-rc.3] - 2026-06-13

The best way to get a drink out of a Vogon is to stick your finger down his throat.

Security

This release includes a fix for the following low-severity security issue:

  • CVE-2026-41579 allowed a malicious image with a /dev symlink to have limited write access to the host filesystem in ways that our analysis indicates was too limited to be problematic in practice. This bug was very similar to those fixed in [CVE-2025-31133][], [CVE-2025-52565][], [CVE-2025-31133][] and was simply missed at the time when we hardened the rootfs preparation code. We have conducted a deeper audit and not found any other problematic cases.

libcontainer API

  • The cmsg helpers from github.com/opencontainers/runc/libcontainer/utils have been moved to an internal package. We have included wrapper functions but they will be removed in runc 1.6. (#5227, #5231)
  • Added //go:fix inline to ease migration for libcontainer/devices symbols that are deprecated and scheduled for removal in runc 1.6. (#5223, #5225)

Changelog

title: Multiple Apptainer Instances on a single host some randomly fail
body:
(This was originally created as a Slack thread, I'm posting here so it's easier to find in case someone else runs into it)

We are seeing some issues running multiple apptainer instances on compute nodes. On our HPC systems, users can share compute nodes/one user can have multiple jobs on a single node. It's not common, but a user could have 384 single core jobs for example. (Max number of jobs/node = total cores, so smaller cpus have a smaller max jobs)

We are seeing that when someone starts somewhere between 24 to 48+ apptainer instances at a time, some randomly fail with the error:
```
Failed to connect to bus: Connection refused
INFO:    Terminating squashfuse_ll after timeout
INFO:    Timeouts can be caused by a running background process
ERROR:   container cleanup failed: no instance found with name foo-2071440
FATAL:   container creation failed: while applying cgroups config: while creating cgroup manager: failed to connect to dbus (hint: for rootless containers, maybe you need to install dbus-user-session package, see https://github.com/opencontainers/runc/blob/master/docs/cgroup-v2.md): could not execute `busctl --user --no-pager status` (output: "Failed to connect to bus: Connection refused\n"): exit status 1

FATAL:   while executing starter: failed to start instance: while running /apps/local/apptainer/1.4.4/x86_64/libexec/apptainer/bin/starter: exit status 255
```

In our tests, 24 instances at a time succeed, but >= 48 (haven't tested in between 24-48 yet) random instances start to fail. We've been digging into squashfuse_ll timeouts, file system checks (loading the container from /tmp instead of nfs). I figured I'd reach out to see if anyone has any ideas of what could be going on.

I don't think this is an apptainer issue specifically, I think it's likely an our systems thing, but I'm trying to dig into what apptainer is doing behind the scenes to figure out where the issue could be. I've tried launching apptainer with -d for debug, and I definitely got more output, but nothing specifically stood out. I think this is because it's more related to squashfuse, but I'm not sure.

Here's a script we've been modifying and using to test:
```bash
#SBATCH --nodes=1
#SBATCH --cpus-per-task=1
#SBATCH --time=0:05:00

#SBATCH --nodelist=NODE0078
#SBATCH --array=1-192
#SBATCH --ntasks=1
#SBATCH --output=output/%j.out

echo "Job $SLURM_JOB_ID on node $SLURM_NODELIST, task $SLURM_ARRAY_TASK_ID started at $(date)"

module load apptainer
CONTAINER_PATH=/path/to/container.sif
FAILED=
JOB_NAME=foo-$SLURM_JOB_ID

apptainer instance start $CONTAINER_PATH $JOB_NAME || FAILED=1
apptainer instance stop $JOB_NAME || true
if [ -n "$FAILED" ]; then
    echo "ruh roh raggy"
    exit 1
else
    echo "no issue detected"
fi
```

It looks like it might be related to apptainer trying to use systemd cgroups vs slurm controlled cgroups.

In apptainer.conf, I changed the default system cgroups from yes to no and that seemed to eliminate the failures.

```
# SYSTEMD CGROUPS: [BOOL]
# DEFAULT: yes
# Whether to use systemd to manage container cgroups. Required for rootless cgroups
# functionality. 'no' will manage cgroups directly via cgroupfs.
systemd cgroups = no
```
I don't fully know the consequences of changing this. Do you know what changing this might affect? My guess would be that slurm would still control the job's processes in cgroups?

drdaved  [7:01 PM]
I would think you are correct.  I don’t think that apptainer does much with cgroups by default.

Release notes

Sourced from github.com/opencontainers/runc's releases.

runc v1.5.0 -- "Why do we even have that lever?!"

This is the somewhat-delayed^Wlong-awaited first stable release of the 1.5.z release branch of runc. It contains a handful of fixes for issues found in 1.5.0-rc.3 and an important dependency bump for libpathrs.

This is the third release of runc following our new release and support policy (see RELEASES.md for more details). This means that, as of this release:

  • The runc 1.2.z (and earlier) release branches are now completely unsupported.
  • The runc 1.3.z release branch will now only receive high severity CVE fixes, and will no longer be supported in less than 6 months (end of October 2026).
  • The runc 1.4.z release branch will now only recieve security and "significant" bugfixes.
  • Users are encouraged to plan migrating to runc 1.5.0 as soon as possible.
  • Despite this release being delayed by over a month, users should still expect a runc 1.6.0 release in late October 2026.

Added

The best way to get a drink out of a Vogon is to stick your finger down his throat.

This bug was very similar to those fixed in [CVE-2025-31133][], [CVE-2025-52565][], [CVE-2025-31133][] and was simply missed at the time when we hardened the rootfs preparation code. 0.5.0

Changelog

  • The new GET /images/{name}/attestations endpoint returns in-toto attestation statements (such as SLSA provenance and SPDX SBOM) attached to an image, with optional platform selection, predicate type filtering, and an opt-in statement query parameter for retrieving the verbatim statement bodies. Tools can now retrieve attestation metadata and content directly from the daemon instead of performing additional registry round-trips. moby/moby#52636

  • The new GET /images/{name}/attestations endpoint returns in-toto attestation statements (such as SLSA provenance and SPDX SBOM) attached to an image, with optional platform selection, predicate type filtering, and an opt-in statement query parameter for retrieving the verbatim statement bodies. Tools can now retrieve attestation metadata and content directly from the daemon instead of performing additional registry round-trips. moby/moby#52636

Sourced from github.com/moby/moby/client's changelog.

0.5.0 (2013-07-17)

  • Runtime: List all processes running inside a container with 'docker top'

  • Registry: New image naming scheme inspired by Go packaging convention allows arbitrary combinations of registries
  • Builder: ENTRYPOINT instruction sets a default binary entry point to a container
  • Builder: VOLUME instruction marks a part of the container as persistent data
  • Builder: 'docker build' displays the full output of a build by default
  • Runtime: 'docker login' supports additional options
  • Runtime: Dont save a container's hostname when committing an image.
  • Registry: Fix issues when uploading images to a private registry

0.4.8 (2013-07-01)

  • Builder: New build operation ENTRYPOINT adds an executable entry point to the container.
  • Runtime: Fix a bug which caused 'docker run -d' to no longer print the container ID.
  • Tests: Fix issues in the test suite

0.4.7 (2013-06-28)

  • Registry: easier push/pull to a custom registry
  • Remote API: the progress bar updates faster when downloading and uploading large files
  • Remote API: fix a bug in the optional unix socket transport
  • Runtime: improve detection of kernel version
  • Runtime: host directories can be mounted as volumes with 'docker run -b'
  • Runtime: fix an issue when only attaching to stdin
  • Runtime: use 'tar --numeric-owner' to avoid uid mismatch across multiple hosts
  • Hack: improve test suite and dev environment
  • Hack: remove dependency on unit tests on 'os/user'
  • Documentation: add terminology section

0.4.6 (2013-06-22)

  • Runtime: fix a bug which caused creation of empty images (and volumes) to crash.

0.4.5 (2013-06-21)

  • Builder: 'docker build git://URL' fetches and builds a remote git repository
  • Runtime: 'docker ps -s' optionally prints container size
  • Tests: Improved and simplified
  • Runtime: fix a regression introduced in 0.4.3 which caused the logs command to fail.
  • Builder: fix a regression when using ADD with single regular file.

0.4.4 (2013-06-19)

  • Builder: fix a regression introduced in 0.4.3 which caused builds to fail on new clients.

0.4.3 (2013-06-19)

  • Builder: ADD of a local file will detect tar archives and unpack them
  • Runtime: Remove bsdtar dependency
  • Runtime: Add unix socket and multiple -H support
  • Runtime: Prevent rm of running containers

title: Unprivileged build fails with PRoot ptrace(TRACEME) error on RHEL 9.8 when kernel.yama.ptrace_scope = 3
body:
### Version of Apptainer

- 1.5.1-1
- 1.5.2-1


### Expected behavior

```bash
$ cat /etc/redhat-release 
Red Hat Enterprise Linux release 9.6 (Plow)
$ uname -r
5.14.0-570.106.1.el9_6.x86_64

$ cat test_perms.def
BootStrap: docker
From: debian:stable-slim

%post
    echo "Testing user and file creation on a glibc system..."
    # Create a non-root system user (Debian uses useradd)
    useradd -m testuser
    
    # Create a file and change its ownership
    mkdir -p /opt
    touch /opt/testfile.txt
    chown testuser:nogroup /opt/testfile.txt
    chmod 644 /opt/testfile.txt

$ apptainer build perms.sif test_perms.def
INFO:    User not listed in /etc/subuid, trying root-mapped namespace
INFO:    The %post section will be run under the fakeroot command
Build target 'perms.sif' already exists and will be deleted during the build process. Do you want to continue? [y/N] y
INFO:    Starting build...
INFO:    Fetching OCI image...
28.4MiB / 28.4MiB [=====================================================================================================================================================] 100 %0s
INFO:    Extracting OCI image...
2026/06/25 14:46:59  warn xattr{etc/gshadow} ignoring ENOTSUP on setxattr "user.rootlesscontainers"
2026/06/25 14:46:59  warn xattr{/tmp/build-temp-1818254481/rootfs/etc/gshadow} destination filesystem does not support xattrs, further warnings will be suppressed
INFO:    Inserting Apptainer configuration...
INFO:    Running post scriptlet
+ echo Testing user and file creation on a glibc system...
Testing user and file creation on a glibc system...
+ useradd -m testuser
+ mkdir -p /opt
+ touch /opt/testfile.txt
+ chown testuser:nogroup /opt/testfile.txt
+ chmod 644 /opt/testfile.txt
INFO:    Creating SIF file...
[======================================================================================================================================================================] 100 % 0s
INFO:    Build complete: perms.sif
```

### Actual behavior

```bash
$ cat /etc/redhat-release 
Red Hat Enterprise Linux release 9.8 (Plow)
$ uname -r
5.14.0-687.15.1.el9_8.x86_64

$ apptainer build perms.sif test_perms.def
INFO:    User not listed in /etc/subuid, trying root-mapped namespace
INFO:    The %post section will be run under the fakeroot command
INFO:    Starting build...
INFO:    Fetching OCI image...
28.4MiB / 28.4MiB [=====================================================================================================================================================] 100 %0s
INFO:    Extracting OCI image...
INFO:    Inserting Apptainer configuration...
INFO:    Running post scriptlet
+ echo Testing user and file creation on a glibc system...
Testing user and file creation on a glibc system...
+ useradd -m testuser
+ mkdir -p /opt
+ touch /opt/testfile.txt
+ chown testuser:nogroup /opt/testfile.txt
+ chmod 644 /opt/testfile.txt
INFO:    Creating SIF file...
[------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------] 0 % 0s
FATAL:   While performing build: while creating squashfs: /usr/libexec/apptainer/bin/mksquashfs command failed: exit status 1: proot error: ptrace(TRACEME): Operation not permitted
proot error: execve("/usr/libexec/apptainer/bin/mksquashfs"): Operation not permitted
proot info: It seems your kernel contains this bug: https://bugs.launchpad.net/ubuntu/+source/linux/+bug/1202161
To workaround it, set the env. variable PROOT_NO_SECCOMP to 1.
fatal error: see `proot --help`.
```

### Steps to reproduce this behavior

Use apptainer 1.5 under RHEL 9.8 with `kernel.yama.ptrace_scope = 3` set.


### What OS/distro are you running

```
NAME="Red Hat Enterprise Linux"
VERSION="9.8 (Plow)"
ID="rhel"
ID_LIKE="fedora"
VERSION_ID="9.8"
PLATFORM_ID="platform:el9"
PRETTY_NAME="Red Hat Enterprise Linux 9.8 (Plow)"
ANSI_COLOR="0;31"
LOGO="fedora-logo-icon"
CPE_NAME="cpe:/o:redhat:enterprise_linux:9::baseos"
HOME_URL="https://www.redhat.com/"
DOCUMENTATION_URL="https://access.redhat.com/documentation/en-us/red_hat_enterprise_linux/9"
BUG_REPORT_URL="https://issues.redhat.com/"

REDHAT_BUGZILLA_PRODUCT="Red Hat Enterprise Linux 9"
REDHAT_BUGZILLA_PRODUCT_VERSION=9.8
REDHAT_SUPPORT_PRODUCT="Red Hat Enterprise Linux"
REDHAT_SUPPORT_PRODUCT_VERSION="9.8"
```

### How did you install Apptainer

- apptainer 1.5.1-1 was installed as an RPM via EPEL 9.
- apptainer 1.5.2-1 was installed as an RPM from https://github.com/apptainer/apptainer/releases/tag/v1.5.2


### Possible fix

There should probably be a change to Apptainer to have it first verify if it can do ptrace before it attempts to start PRoot, and skip it, probably with an INFO message, if ptrace doesn’t work.

My current work around is to set `APPTAINER_IGNORE_PROOT=1` as an environmental variable.

title: feature - Performance improvements for IO to writeable-tmpfs overlay
body:
> __Short:__
> Remove FUSE-FS based Workaround for Linux-Kernel regression for never not afflicted Kernel versions and add performance relevant mount options (e.g. volatile) for non-persistent overlays.

I would like to be assigned to this issue. Before starting out I would like to know whether this is something that might at all get merged or not or would need to be changed.

A few years back Apptainer added a [workaround](https://github.com/apptainer/apptainer/blob/aee8987c216296761d30ecbd1b77f1c1a3404104/internal/pkg/runtime/engine/apptainer/container_linux.go#L794)  to Address a Linux-Kernel regression introduced in Linux 5.15, which caused problems. The workaround was discussed in [#634](https://github.com/apptainer/apptainer/pull/634#issuecomment-1224233820) and disabled the use of the kernel-based overlay-fs if any underlying file-system is a fuse-based file-system.

The Discussion references the corresponding mail-exchange in the Linux-Kernel mailing list ( [kernel lore](https://lore.kernel.org/lkml/CAJfpegvaUyCUkucNwP0P419hC8v78PEM25pW5mBho94HRCgO3Q@mail.gmail.com/) ). The last mentioned patch for fixing this issue has been merged into the Linux-6.5-release, ( https://github.com/torvalds/linux/commit/6a567e920fd0451bf29abc418df96c3365925770 ). I also have not found any later discussions about a similar issue.

With linux-6.6 the tmpfs file-system gained support for user user_xattr(s). This allows for further improvement in regards to the overlay configuration, which is why I would like to  introduce a Linux-Kernel version check within the mount strategy and handle mounts differently - breaking point being Kernel version 6.6.

Since at least Linux 5.14 overlays can be configured to use user.overlay instead of trusted.overlay ([linux-5.14](https://www.kernel.org/doc/html/v5.14/filesystems/overlayfs.html#user-xattr), [linux-7.1](https://www.kernel.org/doc/html/v7.1/filesystems/overlayfs.html#user-xattr). 

Those user_xattr(s) can then be used to enable the uuid feature of linux overlay-fs [uuid-doc](https://www.kernel.org/doc/html/v7.0/filesystems/overlayfs.html#uuid-and-fsid) to make kernel-based-overlays behave more consistent (e.g. when files are moved from a lower to a upper-directory, that those storage places have different uuid(s)). Assuming there is only a non-persistent-tmpfs overlay mounted the [volatile](https://www.kernel.org/doc/html/v7.0/filesystems/overlayfs.html#durability-and-copy-up) option also be interesting.


Charlieclouds mounting strategy relies on the kernel based overlayfs without issues (at least not for my use-cases, assuming a recent enough kernel). Also some preliminary micro-benchmarking on my end generally showed performance gains, which is inline with my general understanding of how fuse works (this should still be the case after [FUSE Passthrough](https://docs.kernel.org/6.16/filesystems/fuse-passthrough.html) makes the jump to users without `CAP_SYS_ADMIN`). 

I am aware that microbenchmarks are not meaningful when it comes real-world file-io with as many dependencies as we have for overlay-based file systems. Also just because it works for me, it may cause problems for others.

As of this I propose putting this change behind a experimental feature flag that:
    - Links to documentation what this does and if the Kernel version is older than 6.6 explains that the feature cannot be used.
    - In any other case it links to a prepared github-Issue to provide a central hub to discuss potential Probelems.
Apptainer could make it the default in a future release, once it has been reasonable well proven.


There are a few more interesting overlayfs-features, e.g. opaque directories. Though am not sure if too much should be changed at once. It may also require the underlying fileystem (e.g. sqash-fs (/fuse2fs)) to also support user_xattrs and I am not sure implementing them could risk security problems. Depending on how above works out, I may investigate further and report back.

While some distributions may have Back-ported a few of this feature to previous Versions, I don't think it would make sense to instead rely on feature tests as it could lead to difficult to triage error-behavior caused by differences in cherry-picked-backport-patches across Distributions.

title: Include Fedora in CI checks
body:
Update `scripts/ci-rpm-build-test` to include Fedora 44 & 45 and add fedora44 and fedora45 CI checks to the github actions ci.yml. I also suspect that the workaround in dist/rpm/apptainer.spec.in and scripts/download-dependencies for fedora 45 to not build PRoot may need to be extended to Fedora 44 for a CI check, because in my testing of the fedora:44 docker image the same gcc version is used as on Fedora 45 and it fails in the same way.  However, builds for f44 on koji.fedoraproject.org do not fail.

The official source for Fedora containers is quay.io/fedora/fedora-bootc

The best way to irritate him is to feed his grandmother to the Ravenous Bugblatter Beast of Traal.

Security

This release includes a fix for the following low-severity security issue:

  • CVE-2026-41579 allowed a malicious image with a /dev symlink to have limited write access to the host filesystem in ways that our analysis indicates was too limited to be problematic in practice. Sourced from github.com/moby/moby/client's releases.

client/0.5.0

0.5.0

Changelog

  • The new GET /images/{name}/attestations endpoint returns in-toto attestation statements (such as SLSA provenance and SPDX SBOM) attached to an image, with optional platform selection, predicate type filtering, and an opt-in statement query parameter for retrieving the verbatim statement bodies. Tools can now retrieve attestation metadata and content directly from the daemon instead of performing additional registry round-trips. moby/moby#52636

client/v0.5.0-rc.1

0.5.0-rc.1

Changelog

  • The new GET /images/{name}/attestations endpoint returns in-toto attestation statements (such as SLSA provenance and SPDX SBOM) attached to an image, with optional platform selection, predicate type filtering, and an opt-in statement query parameter for retrieving the verbatim statement bodies. Tools can now retrieve attestation metadata and content directly from the daemon instead of performing additional registry round-trips. moby/moby#52636
Changelog

Sourced from github.com/moby/moby/client's changelog.

0.5.0 (2013-07-17)

  • Runtime: List all processes running inside a container with 'docker top'
  • Runtime: Host directories can be mounted as volumes with 'docker run -v'
  • Runtime: Containers can expose public UDP ports (eg, '-p 123/udp')
  • Runtime: Optionally specify an exact public port (eg. '-p 80:4500')
  • Registry: New image naming scheme inspired by Go packaging convention allows arbitrary combinations of registries
  • Builder: ENTRYPOINT instruction sets a default binary entry point to a container
  • Builder: VOLUME instruction marks a part of the container as persistent data
  • Builder: 'docker build' displays the full output of a build by default
  • Runtime: 'docker login' supports additional options
  • Runtime: Dont save a container's hostname when committing an image.
  • Registry: Fix issues when uploading images to a private registry

0.4.8 (2013-07-01)

  • Builder: New build operation ENTRYPOINT adds an executable entry point to the container.
  • Runtime: Fix a bug which caused 'docker run -d' to no longer print the container ID.
  • Tests: Fix issues in the test suite

0.4.7 (2013-06-28)

  • Registry: easier push/pull to a custom registry
  • Remote API: the progress bar updates faster when downloading and uploading large files
  • Remote API: fix a bug in the optional unix socket transport
  • Runtime: improve detection of kernel version
  • Runtime: host directories can be mounted as volumes with 'docker run -b'
  • Runtime: fix an issue when only attaching to stdin
  • Runtime: use 'tar --numeric-owner' to avoid uid mismatch across multiple hosts
  • Hack: improve test suite and dev environment
  • Hack: remove dependency on unit tests on 'os/user'

0.4.6 (2013-06-22)

  • Runtime: fix a bug which caused creation of empty images (and volumes) to crash.

0.4.5 (2013-06-21)

  • Builder: 'docker build git://URL' fetches and builds a remote git repository
  • Runtime: 'docker ps -s' optionally prints container size
  • Tests: Improved and simplified
  • Runtime: fix a regression introduced in 0.4.3 which caused the logs command to fail.
  • Builder: fix a regression when using ADD with single regular file.

0.4.4 (2013-06-19)

  • Builder: fix a regression introduced in 0.4.3 which caused builds to fail on new clients.

0.4.3 (2013-06-19)

  • Builder: ADD of a local file will detect tar archives and unpack them
  • Runtime: Remove bsdtar dependency
  • Runtime: Add unix socket and multiple -H support
  • Runtime: Prevent rm of running containers
  • Runtime: Use go1.1 cookiejar
  • Builder: ADD improvements: use tar for copy + automatically unpack local archives

runc v1.5.0 -- "Why do we even have that lever?!"

This is the somewhat-delayed^Wlong-awaited first stable release of the 1.5.z release branch of runc. It contains a handful of fixes for issues found in 1.5.0-rc.3 and an important dependency bump for libpathrs.

This is the third release of runc following our new release and support policy (see RELEASES.md for more details). This means that, as of this release:

  • The runc 1.2.z (and earlier) release branches are now completely unsupported.
  • The runc 1.3.z release branch will now only receive high severity CVE fixes, and will no longer be supported in less than 6 months (end of October 2026).
  • The runc 1.4.z release branch will now only recieve security and "significant" bugfixes.
  • Users are encouraged to plan migrating to runc 1.5.0 as soon as possible.
  • Despite this release being delayed by over a month, users should still expect a runc 1.6.0 release in late October 2026.

title: Sync writable extfs
body:
Add a sync writable extfs apptainer.conf directive. When enabled, writable ext3 image mounts use the sync mount option, while default behavior remains unchanged.

## Description of the Pull Request (PR):

We want to enable sync for loop devices (specifically writeable overlays). Problem comes from:
- we write to many writeable overlays (ext3 loop devs)
- the lvm the loops live on fills up
- writing processes are in D state, since the loop devs are trying to writeback their dirty pages (huge on a high-mem host), and kernel doesn't propagate ENOSPC - likely a kernel bug
- to get around this, we want the optionality to set sync on the loop devices to be a bit more aggressive during writeback, so that we don't enter this deadlock (there's not as much in dirty pagecache).

### This fixes or addresses the following GitHub issues:

No issue reported. We found this, patched and have seen it solves the problem.

title: `mksquashfs` included in Apptainer 1.5.1 errors on `SIGSEGV` when building
body:
### Version of Apptainer

```sh
$ apptainer --version
apptainer version 1.5.1

$ /usr/libexec/apptainer/bin/mksquashfs -version | head -n 1
mksquashfs version 4.7.5 (2026/03/01)   # failing binary

$ mksquashfs -version | head -n 1
mksquashfs version 4.5.1 (2022/03/17)   # workaround binary
```

### Expected behavior

`apptainer build sct.sif ...` should deterministically complete and produce a SIF image.

### Actual behavior

Build fails intermittently during squashfs creation with:

```text
FATAL: While performing build: while creating squashfs: /usr/libexec/apptainer/bin/mksquashfs command failed: exit status 139
```

The failure point is nondeterministic (e.g. sometimes around ~29%, sometimes elsewhere).

Important observations:
- This happens in a VS Code devcontainer setup (nested/containerized environment).
- Direct `mksquashfs` over the same exported rootfs can complete successfully.
- Replacing Apptainer helper `mksquashfs` with system `mksquashfs` 4.5.1 makes `apptainer build` succeed reliably.

### Steps to reproduce this behavior

1. Use a VS Code devcontainer on Debian 12 (Docker-outside-of-Docker), with Apptainer installed via devcontainer feature.

   Environment details relevant to nested Apptainer:
   - Devcontainer `securityOpt` includes:
     - `seccomp=unconfined`
     - `systempaths=unconfined`
     - `apparmor=unconfined`
   - Devcontainer `capAdd` includes:
     - `SYS_PTRACE`
   - Devcontainer `runArgs` includes:
     - `--device=/dev/fuse`
   - `privileged` set to `false`

2. Run:

```sh
apptainer build sct.sif docker://neuropoly/sct:demo-7.4
```

3. Observe intermittent failure during squashfs stage with exit status 139.

Workaround (reliable):

```sh
sudo apt-get update
sudo apt-get install -y squashfs-tools
sudo cp /usr/libexec/apptainer/bin/mksquashfs /usr/libexec/apptainer/bin/mksquashfs.bundled-4.7.5
sudo ln -sf /usr/bin/mksquashfs /usr/libexec/apptainer/bin/mksquashfs

apptainer build sct.sif docker:neuropoly/sct:demo-7.4
```

### What OS/distro are you running

```sh
$ cat /etc/os-release
PRETTY_NAME="Debian GNU/Linux 12 (bookworm)"
NAME="Debian GNU/Linux"
VERSION_ID="12"
VERSION="12 (bookworm)"
VERSION_CODENAME=bookworm
ID=debian
HOME_URL="https://www.debian.org/"
SUPPORT_URL="https://www.debian.org/support"
BUG_REPORT_URL="https://bugs.debian.org/"
```

### How did you install Apptainer

Installed via VS Code devcontainer feature:

- `ghcr.io/miguelrodo/devcontainerfeatures/apptainer:1.1.4`

(inside a VS Code devcontainer, with Docker-outside-of-Docker)

title: ECL: ValidateConfig runs unconditionally, even when activated = false, causing lockout if a dirpath directory is removed
body:
## Version

Reproduced on `apptainer 1.4.5-3.el9` (Rocky Linux 9).

## Summary

`ecl.ValidateConfig()` is invoked on every SIF `apptainer exec`/`run`/`shell` **before** the `Activated` flag is consulted. The validator calls `filepath.EvalSymlinks()` on each `[[execgroup]].dirpath` (which underneath does an `lstat()`). If a referenced directory has been removed while the execgroup still lists it, every subsequent SIF invocation fails with:

```
FATAL: while validating ECL configuration: lstat <path>: no such file or directory
```

This effectively locks the host out of running any SIF until the stale execgroup is hand-removed from `/etc/apptainer/ecl.toml`. Setting `activated = false` does **not** avoid the lockout because validation runs first.

## Steps to reproduce

```bash
# Apptainer 1.4.5-3.el9, Rocky Linux 9, root-owned ecl.toml
sudo mkdir -p /opt/prod
sudo cp myimage.sif /opt/prod/

sudo tee /etc/apptainer/ecl.toml > /dev/null <<TOML
activated = true
legacyinsecure = false

[[execgroup]]
  tagname = "prod"
  mode = "whitelist"
  dirpath = "/opt/prod"
  keyfp = ["<a 40-char fingerprint>"]
TOML

# Disable ECL and remove the directory (in either order)
sudo sed -i 's/activated = true/activated = false/' /etc/apptainer/ecl.toml
sudo rm -rf /opt/prod

# Try to run ANY SIF, even outside /opt/prod
apptainer exec ~/some-other.sif true
# FATAL: while validating ECL configuration: lstat /opt/prod: no such file or directory
```

## Expected behavior

When `activated = false`, ECL config validation should be skipped (or at minimum, missing `dirpath` directories should be a warning, not a fatal). Currently `activated = false` cannot be relied upon as a "disable + safely clean up" mechanism.

## Actual behavior

Validation runs on every SIF exec regardless of activation state, and any missing `dirpath` makes the entire host unable to execute SIF images.

## Source

Call site — `internal/pkg/runtime/engine/apptainer/prepare_linux.go` (around line 1337):

```go
ecl, err := syecl.LoadConfig(buildcfg.ECL_FILE)
if err == nil {
    if err = ecl.ValidateConfig(); err != nil {            // ← runs unconditionally
        return fmt.Errorf("while validating ECL configuration: %s", err)
    }

    // ...
    if ecl.Activated {                                     // ← Activated checked AFTER validation
        // load keyring, run ShouldRunFp, etc.
    }
}
```

Validator — `internal/pkg/syecl/syecl.go` (around line 85), the relevant lines:

```go
func (ecl *EclConfig) ValidateConfig() error {
    // ...
    for _, v := range ecl.ExecGroups {
        // ...
        if v.DirPath != "" {
            path, err := filepath.EvalSymlinks(v.DirPath)    // ← lstat under the hood
            if err != nil {
                return err
            }
            // ...
        }
    }
    return nil
}
```

## Suggested fix

Move the `if !ecl.Activated { return true, nil }` early-exit into `ValidateConfig` (or check `ecl.Activated` in the caller before invoking `ValidateConfig`). Either approach restores the property that `activated = false` is a clean "turn off and clean up later" switch.

A softer alternative: change the `EvalSymlinks` failure on a missing directory from a fatal error into a logged warning, and skip the affected execgroup.

## Impact

- Surprising lockout for admins who follow what reads as the obvious safe order (`activated = false` → remove directory).
- No clean automation path for tearing down an ECL deployment.
- Discovered while preparing training material; pretty easy for any new ECL user to hit.

Happy to open a PR for whichever of the two fixes the maintainers prefer.

title: mksquashfs fails under proot in Apptainer 1.5.1 with Parabricks image; succeeds with APPTAINER_IGNORE_PROOT=1
body:
### Version of Apptainer

```bash
$ apptainer --version
apptainer version 1.5.1
```

### Expected behavior

The build should complete successfully with default options, or Apptainer should fall back safely if `mksquashfs` fails under `proot`.

### Actual behavior

`mksquashfs` crashes or hits `FATAL ERROR: Bug in orderer` when invoked through Apptainer's bundled `proot`.

Observed failures are nondeterministic. I have seen both:

```text
FATAL:   While performing build: while creating squashfs:
/usr/libexec/apptainer/bin/mksquashfs command failed: exit status 139
```

and:

```text
FATAL:   While performing build: while creating squashfs:
/usr/libexec/apptainer/bin/mksquashfs command failed: exit status 1:
FATAL ERROR: Bug in orderer
```

With `--debug`, Apptainer invokes:

```text
Executing /usr/libexec/apptainer/bin/proot -S / /usr/libexec/apptainer/bin/mksquashfs \
  /tmp/build-temp-.../rootfs /tmp/bundle-temp-.../squashfs-... -noappend -comp gzip

Parallel mksquashfs: Using 32 processors
```

The same build succeeds if I disable the new proot path:

```bash
APPTAINER_IGNORE_PROOT=1 apptainer build pb.sif docker://nvcr.io/nvidia/clara/clara-parabricks:4.7.0-1
```

Successful debug line:

```text
Executing /usr/libexec/apptainer/bin/mksquashfs ... -noappend -comp gzip -all-root
Parallel mksquashfs: Using 32 processors
Build complete
```

Also, limiting mksquashfs processors works around it:

```bash
apptainer build --mksquashfs-args '-processors 1' \
  pb.sif docker://nvcr.io/nvidia/clara/clara-parabricks:4.7.0-1
```

### Steps to reproduce this behavior

Run:

```bash
apptainer build pb.sif docker://nvcr.io/nvidia/clara/clara-parabricks:4.7.0-1
```

The failure happens during SIF creation / squashfs creation.

For comparison, this succeeds:

```bash
APPTAINER_IGNORE_PROOT=1 apptainer build pb.sif docker://nvcr.io/nvidia/clara/clara-parabricks:4.7.0-1
```

This suggests the issue is specifically in the 1.5.x `proot` path used for invoking `mksquashfs`.

### What OS/distro are you running

```sh
$ cat /etc/os-release
PRETTY_NAME="Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS"
NAME="Ubuntu"
VERSION_ID="24.04"
VERSION="24.04.4 LTS (Noble Numbat)"
VERSION_CODENAME=noble
ID=ubuntu
ID_LIKE=debian
HOME_URL="https://www.ubuntu.com/"
SUPPORT_URL="https://help.ubuntu.com/"
BUG_REPORT_URL="https://bugs.launchpad.net/ubuntu/"
PRIVACY_POLICY_URL="https://www.ubuntu.com/legal/terms-and-policies/privacy-policy"
UBUNTU_CODENAME=noble
LOGO=ubuntu-logo
```

Additional host info:

```bash
$ nproc
32
```

### How did you install Apptainer

Installed from the Apptainer Ubuntu PPA:

```bash
$ dpkg -l | grep apptainer
ii  apptainer  1.5.1-1~noble  amd64  container platform focused on supporting "Mobility of Compute" formerly known as Singularity
```

### Notes

This appears related to the 1.5.x change that runs `mksquashfs` through `proot` to preserve OCI ownership metadata.

It may be related to, but not fully fixed by:

- #3486
- #3535

This reproduces on Apptainer 1.5.1, with default gzip compression, not xz.

Fixed

  • ExecLabel was using an incorrect path (regression in v1.13.0). (opencontainers/selinux#253)

Deprecated

  • CategoryRange is deprecated; use SetCategoryRange instead. (opencontainers/selinux#262)
  • KVMContainerLabels is deprecated; use KVMContainerLabel instead. (opencontainers/selinux#262)

  • ReserveLabel is deprecated; use ReserveLabelV2 instead. (opencontainers/selinux#262)
  • ROFileLabel is deprecated; if you use it, open a new issue. (opencontainers/selinux#262)
  • ContainerLabels is deprecated, if you use it, open a new issue. (opencontainers/selinux#262)

Added

  • CheckLabel. (opencontainers/selinux#250)
  • SetCategoryRange, KVMContainerLabel, InitContainerLabel, ReserveLabelV2. (opencontainers/selinux#262)

Changed

  • Switch to Go 1.22 as the minimally supported version (opencontainers/selinux#256)
  • Update GetDefaultContextWithLevel to fall back to failsafe context (opencontainers/selinux#232)

title: Merge release-1.5 into main after 1.5.1 release
fix: limit container paths using path prefix, not string prefix (release-1.5)
body:
The Image.AuthorizedPath function, which is passed the values of the 'limit container paths' apptainer.conf directive, previously used plain tring prefix matching. This meant an image in a sibling directory, e.g. /tmp/foobar would be allowed when the directive was set to /tmp/foo.

Because of explicit and implicit filepath.Clean it's also not possible to match on /tmp/foo/ as the final slash will be stripped by the Clean.

Modify the code to evaluate the relative path of the image from each limit path, and assess based on this.

Imported to Apptainer from https://github.com/sylabs/singularity/security/advisories/GHSA-wqcr-7rf3-f64m

title: Enable extglob for %files section

## Description of the Pull Request (PR):

I noticed that the path expansion in the %files section was done by executing a script with mvdan.cc/sh, which struck me as unnecessarily unsafe. Instead, we can use the mvdan.cc/sh/v3/expand package that is used by the package internally as well, and skip the rest of the shell, reducing the possibility of unexpected command injections via the %files section.

title: Nested container start failing with apptainer version 1.5.0
body:
Starting a container within container fails with apptainer version 1.5.0 in the outer container.  While starting a container within a container with apptainer version 1.4.5 works fine
### Version of Apptainer

apptainer version 1.5.0-1.el8

### Expected behavior

> export APPTAINER_BINDPATH=/etc/pki/ca-trust,/cvmfs,/tmp,/data,/var/run/user,/run/user,/cvmfs/grid.cern.ch/etc/grid-security:/etc/grid-security,/cvmfs/grid.cern.ch/etc/grid-security/vomses:/etc/vomses,/home,/data
> apptainer -s exec /cvmfs/unpacked.cern.ch/registry.hub.docker.com/cmssw/el8:x86_64-d20260519 bash
Singularity> apptainer --version
apptainer version 1.4.5-3.el8
Singularity> apptainer -s exec /cvmfs/unpacked.cern.ch/registry.hub.docker.com/cmssw/el7:x86_64 sh -c 'echo OK'
OK

### Actual behavior

> export APPTAINER_BINDPATH=/etc/pki/ca-trust,/cvmfs,/tmp,/data,/var/run/user,/run/user,/cvmfs/grid.cern.ch/etc/grid-security:/etc/grid-security,/cvmfs/grid.cern.ch/etc/grid-security/vomses:/etc/vomses,/home,/data
> apptainer -s exec /cvmfs/unpacked.cern.ch/registry.hub.docker.com/cmssw/el8:x86_64 bash
Singularity> apptainer --version
apptainer version 1.5.0-1.el8
Singularity> apptainer -s exec /cvmfs/unpacked.cern.ch/registry.hub.docker.com/cmssw/el7:x86_64 sh -c 'echo OK'
FATAL:   container creation failed: mount hook function failure: mount /etc/vomses->/etc/vomses error: while mounting /etc/vomses: destination /etc/vomses doesn't exist in container

### Steps to reproduce this behavior

Starting a container with apptainer 1.5.0-1.el8 and then within it start an other container. Things work fine when we had apptainer version 1.4.5 in the outer container but with aptainer version 1.5.0 in outer container the inner container fails with mount issue. Note that `/etc/vomses ` does exists in both containers

### What OS/distro are you running

almalinux9

### How did you install Apptainer

cmssw/el8:x86_64-d20260519 (with apptainer version 1.4.5) and cmssw/el8:x86_64-d20260530 (with apptainer version 1.5.0) containers are unpacked on /cvmfs/unpacked.cern.ch repository by CERN CVMFS team.

  • Use math/rand/v2 rather than crypto/rand for MCS label generation (opencontainers/selinux#257)
