title: Panic updating progress bars during image pull
body:
### Version of Apptainer

`apptainer version 1.5.0`

### Expected behavior

Successful pull of image from cache during image build:

`apptainer build foo.sif foodef`

xxx.def:
```
Bootstrap: docker
From: ros:{{ ros_distro }}
Stage: build_interfaces

%arguments
  ros_distro=kilted

...
```

### Actual behavior

Panic when updating progress bars.

```
panic: runtime error: index out of range [7] with length 7

goroutine 1 [running]:
github.com/apptainer/apptainer/internal/pkg/client.(*RoundTripper).ProgressComplete(...)
        github.com/apptainer/apptainer/internal/pkg/client/progress_roundtrip.go:75
github.com/apptainer/apptainer/internal/pkg/ociimage.FetchToLayout({0xaaaacb8dc968, 0x7db11c2ca3c0}, 0x7db11c2a8240, 0x7db11c3aa930, {0x7db11c194be8?, 0x13?}, {0x7db11c49d2c0, 0x19})
        github.com/apptainer/apptainer/internal/pkg/ociimage/fetch.go:143 +0xb7c
github.com/apptainer/apptainer/internal/pkg/build/sources.(*OCIConveyorPacker).Get(0x7db11c1523c0, {0xaaaacb8dc968, 0x7db11c2ca3c0}, 0x7db11c318808)
        github.com/apptainer/apptainer/internal/pkg/build/sources/conveyorPacker_oci.go:206 +0x80c
github.com/apptainer/apptainer/internal/pkg/build.(*Build).Full(0x7db11c5f6a00, {0xaaaacb8dc968, 0x7db11c2ca3c0})
        github.com/apptainer/apptainer/internal/pkg/build/build.go:302 +0x358
github.com/apptainer/apptainer/cmd/internal/cli.runBuildLocal({0xaaaacb8dc968, 0x7db11c2ca3c0}, 0xaaaacb95da80, {0xffffc687d59e, 0x14}, {0xffffc687d5b3, 0x14}, {0x0, 0x0})
        github.com/apptainer/apptainer/cmd/internal/cli/build_linux.go:421 +0x1194
github.com/apptainer/apptainer/cmd/internal/cli.runBuild(0xaaaacb95da80, {0x7db11c55c1c0?, 0x2?, 0x2?})
        github.com/apptainer/apptainer/cmd/internal/cli/build_linux.go:241 +0x5c8
github.com/spf13/cobra.(*Command).execute(0xaaaacb95da80, {0x7db11c1920e0, 0x2, 0x2})
        github.com/spf13/cobra@v1.10.2/command.go:1019 +0x7fc
github.com/spf13/cobra.(*Command).ExecuteC(0xaaaacb95d4c0)
        github.com/spf13/cobra@v1.10.2/command.go:1148 +0x350
github.com/spf13/cobra.(*Command).Execute(...)
        github.com/spf13/cobra@v1.10.2/command.go:1071
github.com/spf13/cobra.(*Command).ExecuteContext(...)
        github.com/spf13/cobra@v1.10.2/command.go:1064
github.com/apptainer/apptainer/cmd/internal/cli.ExecuteApptainer()
        github.com/apptainer/apptainer/cmd/internal/cli/apptainer.go:700 +0x1b0
main.main()
        github.com/apptainer/apptainer/cmd/apptainer/cli.go:22 +0x38
```

### Steps to reproduce this behavior

Was unable to reproduce, subsequent runs of same command had no issues.

On examination it appears that if a `ProgressComplete` call is made between [`internal/pkg/client/progress_roundtrip.go:64`](https://github.com/apptainer/apptainer/blob/main/internal/pkg/client/progress_roundtrip.go#L64) and the following line, `t.bars` would be one longer than `t.sizes` potentially leading to this panic. `ProgressComplete` uses `range` on `t.bars` and uses that index to access `t.sizes`.

Swapping the order of those lines would avoid this.

```go
func (t *RoundTripper) RoundTrip(req *http.Request) (*http.Response, error) {
	if t.p == nil || req.Method != http.MethodGet {
		return t.inner.RoundTrip(req)
	}

	resp, err := t.inner.RoundTrip(req)
	if resp != nil && resp.Body != nil && resp.ContentLength >= contentSizeThreshold {
		bar := t.p.AddBar(resp.ContentLength, defaultOption...)
		t.bars = append(t.bars, bar)
                // Here t.bars is one longer than t.sizes
		t.sizes = append(t.sizes, resp.ContentLength)
		resp.Body = bar.ProxyReader(resp.Body)
	}
	return resp, err
}
```

v1.15.0

This release adds a new function, SetProcessKind, which is to be used instead of KVMProcessLabel[s] and InitProcessLabel[s] in case the user only wants to change the type of the existing label, not generate a new one. It also fixes an CI issue and optimizes label.InitLabels for a few common cases.

v1.14.1

This release mostly fixes label.InitLabels regression introduced in v1.14.0.

What's Changed

  • README: rm travis, add gha badge by @​kolyshkin in opencontainers/selinux#268
  • Fix label.InitLabels regression in v1.14.0; amend ReserveLabelV2 doc by @​kolyshkin in opencontainers/selinux#267

Full Changelog: https://github.com/opencontainers/selinux/compare/v1.14.0...v1.14.1

v1.14.0

This release fixes a regression in ExecLabel, bumps the minimal Go version to 1.22, and deprecates several functions in favor of improved API.

Fixed

  • ExecLabel was using an incorrect path (regression in v1.13.0). (opencontainers/selinux#253)

Deprecated

  • CategoryRange is deprecated; use SetCategoryRange instead. (opencontainers/selinux#262)
  • KVMContainerLabels is deprecated; use KVMContainerLabel instead. (opencontainers/selinux#262)
  • InitContainerLabels is deprecated; use InitContainerLabel instead. (opencontainers/selinux#262)
  • ReserveLabel is deprecated; use ReserveLabelV2 instead. (opencontainers/selinux#262)
  • ROFileLabel is deprecated; if you use it, open a new issue. (opencontainers/selinux#262)
  • ContainerLabels is deprecated, if you use it, open a new issue. (opencontainers/selinux#262)

Added

  • SEUserByName. (opencontainers/selinux#232, opencontainers/selinux#251)
  • CheckLabel. (opencontainers/selinux#250)
  • SetCategoryRange, KVMContainerLabel, InitContainerLabel, ReserveLabelV2. (opencontainers/selinux#262)

Changed

  • Switch to Go 1.22 as the minimally supported version (opencontainers/selinux#256)
  • Update GetDefaultContextWithLevel to fall back to failsafe context (opencontainers/selinux#232)
  • Use math/rand/v2 rather than crypto/rand for MCS label generation (opencontainers/selinux#257)

Miscellaneous

  • MAINTAINERS: add Aleksa as a maintainer. (opencontainers/selinux#243)
  • Assorted CI bumps and related fixes. (opencontainers/selinux#255)
  • Remove intToMcs. (opencontainers/selinux#259)
  • Use Cut more. (opencontainers/selinux#254)
  • Simplify getSelinuxMountPoint. (opencontainers/selinux#258)
  • Simplify/remove some code. (opencontainers/selinux#261)

title: squashfuse_ll crash for apptainer-in-docker older images
body:
### Version of Apptainer

What version of Apptainer (or Singularity) are you using? Run

`apptainer --version` (or `singularity --version`).

`apptainer version 1.5.0`

### Expected behavior


### Actual behavior

I had a working setup where I would run apptainer image in a alpine docker container (CI job).
It would work with docker container being passed `--device /dev/fuse --security-opt "apparmor:unconfined" --security-opt "seccomp:unconfined"` 
I a now having a weird bug where `squashfuse_ll` crashes at some point when a process tries to access files, it might only be in a forked subprocess. That issue seems to have been triggered by recent host kernel and OS updates, as the docker image had not changed when it first happened, though the examples above are with an updated image as I tried first updating apptainer using an alpine:edge image to get potential fixes.

The relevant part of the traceback is:

The files indeed exist,

### Steps to reproduce this behavior

Due to the convoluted setup this is pretty complex to reproduce, I cannot for now find a simpler reproducing case. 

I am mainly looking into cues to debug what is happening with `squashfuse` as there are no message as to what causes the crash. Is there any way to fork `squashfuse_ll` in apptainer with higher verbosity?

### What OS/distro are you running

title: Fix incorrect propagation of APPTAINER_BINDPATH inside the container
body:
Add a `nonested` flag for `--mount` bind specifications that prevents individual mounts from being propagated to nested containers via `APPTAINER_BIND`. Example: `--mount type=bind,source=/data,destination=/mnt,nonested`. This gives users fine-grained control over which binds are inherited by nested Apptainer commands, without having to manually edit `APPTAINER_BIND` inside the container.

Also clarifies in the documentation that unlike in Singularity, `APPTAINER_BIND` and `APPTAINER_BINDPATH` are equivalent aliases in Apptainer — both propagate to nested containers. Removes a stale code comment that incorrectly claimed `--mount` binds were not exported for nested containers, and updates the user docs to reflect the current behavior and point users to `nonested` as the proper way to prevent propagation.

### This fixes or addresses the following GitHub issues:

 - Fixes #3500

title: APPTAINER_BINDPATH doesn't work as documented
body:
### Version of Apptainer

**What version of Apptainer (or Singularity) are you using? Run**

`apptainer --version` (or `singularity --version`).

```sh
apptainer version 1.4.1-1.el8
```

### Expected behavior

**What did you expect to see when you do...?**

The documentation states:
https://apptainer.org/docs/user/main/bind_paths_and_mounts.html
> Inside an Apptainer container all the paths that were bound in are set in the $APPTAINER_BIND variable. That means they will be automatically bound in again by default if another apptainer command is run nested inside the first container. You can change that variable if you choose before that point, but if you want to avoid interfering with nested containers it’s better to use $APPTAINER_BINDPATH.

`APPTAINER_BINDPATH=/s3 apptainer exec --containall /path/to/image.sif printenv | egrep 'SING|APPT'` shouldn't display /s3


### Actual behavior

**What actually happened? Why was it incorrect?**

```
$  APPTAINER_BINDPATH=/s3 apptainer exec --containall /path/to/image.sif printenv | egrep 'SING|APPT'

APPTAINER_APPNAME=
APPTAINER_BIND=/s3
APPTAINER_COMMAND=exec
APPTAINER_CONTAINER=/path/to/image.sif
APPTAINER_ENVIRONMENT=/.singularity.d/env/91-environment.sh
APPTAINER_NAME=image.sif
SINGULARITY_BIND=/s3
SINGULARITY_CONTAINER=/path/to/image.sif
SINGULARITY_ENVIRONMENT=/.singularity.d/env/91-environment.sh
SINGULARITY_NAME=image.sif
```

With `APPTAINER_BINDPATH`, it shouldn't propagate /s3 to APPTAINER_BIND inside the container.

### Steps to reproduce this behavior

**How can others reproduce this issue/problem?**

Run the command, it's a minimal reproducible example. Any image will work. All the apptainer versions are affected 

### What OS/distro are you running

```sh
$ cat /etc/os-release

PRETTY_NAME="Ubuntu 22.04.5 LTS"
NAME="Ubuntu"
VERSION_ID="22.04"
VERSION="22.04.5 LTS (Jammy Jellyfish)"
VERSION_CODENAME=jammy
ID=ubuntu
ID_LIKE=debian
HOME_URL="https://www.ubuntu.com/"
SUPPORT_URL="https://help.ubuntu.com/"
BUG_REPORT_URL="https://bugs.launchpad.net/ubuntu/"
PRIVACY_POLICY_URL="https://www.ubuntu.com/legal/terms-and-policies/privacy-policy"
UBUNTU_CODENAME=jammy
```

### How did you install Apptainer

Not relevant

### Timeline of the bug

I tried to trace back to find how this happened, as if it's documented somewhere, there are high chances it was implemented initially, then was missed from a big refactor.

Indeed, that's actually happened:

- **2016–2018 (C/shell Singularity):** Only `SINGULARITY_BINDPATH` existed. The `--bind` flag set it, the C code processed it, then **unset it** (`unsetenv("SINGULARITY_BINDPATH")`) — it was never propagated into the container.

- **Sep 2018 ( f93309041 ):** Go rewrite introduced env-var-to-flag binding. `SINGULARITY_BINDPATH` and a new `SINGULARITY_BIND` alias were both mapped to the same variable (`EnvKeys: []string{"BINDPATH", "BIND"}`). **The distinction was lost from day one of the Go port — they were never handled separately.**

- **Oct 2020 ( 84360fca7 ):** Propagation of `SINGULARITY_BIND` was added into the container (fixing #5599), so containers could inspect which binds were active. But since `BIND` and `BINDPATH` were already merged into the same variable, **all** binds from both env vars (plus `--bind`) got propagated as `SINGULARITY_BIND` inside the container.

- **Jul 2022 ( 088b9c57b ):** @DrDaveD added `--mount` and fakeroot bind support to `setBinds`. **The propagation still used a separate `bindPaths` string slice, so `--mount` and fakeroot binds were correctly excluded from `APPTAINER_BIND` inside the container.** Currently you can find a leftover comment `Note that these do not get exported for nested containers`, that was accurate at that point, but not now.

- **Jan 2023 ( 7ae4a07cde ):** @DrDaveD refactored propagation in "Fix nested bind lists" to derive destinations from the merged `binds` slice (to fix a comma/colon parsing bug). This inadvertently started propagating `--mount` and fakeroot binds too, making the "do not get exported" comment stale.

- **Present:** Two bugs: (1) `APPTAINER_BINDPATH` behaves identically to `APPTAINER_BIND` — never implemented in Go. (2) `--mount` binds are propagated as `APPTAINER_BIND` — regressed in Jan 2023.

title: Experiment with shorthand flags for squashfs compression
body: When you use the `gzip` command, it has some simple flags like `--fast` and `--best`. It would be nice with something similar for apptainer build, even beyond legacy gzip... Currently there is a `--mksquashfs-args` generic option, that can do anything/nothing. https://apptainer.org/docs/user/main/build_a_container.html#alternative-compressors The assumption is that both compress **and** decompress can be up to 5x faster than now*. \* by switching the default compressor from gzip to zstd, before any levels or comp flags. Follow-up from: * #2785 ----- According to my own experiments, lz4 is the fast and zstd is the best compression. But note also that lz4 has the _worst_ size, and for instance xz has the _worst_ speed: _the type of image also impacts the result, so need to test with several more of them_ Switching the default from `gzip -9` to `zstd -9` has a good impact on both, though. The compression/decompression speed is faster, but the image size is still smaller... ----- Compression | `mksquashfs-args` --- | --- None | `-no-compression # -noI -noD -noF -noX` _Legacy options:_ | Fastest |`-comp lzo` Fast |`-comp gzip -Xcompression-level 1` Default |`-comp gzip # -Xcompression-level 9` Best | `-comp xz` _Modern options:_ | Fastest | `-comp lz4` Fast | `-comp zstd -Xcompression-level 1` Default | `-comp zstd -Xcompression-level 9` Best |`-comp zstd # -Xcompression-level 15` Higher levels of zstd are exponentially more expensive to compress, same as with xz. They also have a performance penalty for decompress, high with xz - less with zstd.

title: Add concept of overlay container images
body:
My community has a desire to separately distribute common base containers maintained by projects from specific code added by individuals.  The base containers would be distributed by the projects in one CVMFS repository and be relatively permanent, and the specific code would be distributed in a separate CVMFS repository that gets updated more quickly and which automatically cleans out the code after a period of time of no use.

My plan to address this is the following:
- Add an `--overlay` option to `apptainer build` which will by default produce a SIF file containing a squashfs partition that is in overlayfs upper layer format, on top of the `From:` part on which it is building.  The metadata will include a hash representing the container on which it is built.  That hash will also be stored in the partition for the purpose of converting to sandbox, in a file under a `/.singularity.d` directory.
- Add a `--basepath` action command option (and APPTAINER_BASEPATH environment variable) that is a colon-separated list of paths. If someone attempts to run one of these overlay containers, attempt to discover the corresponding base container by searching through that path.  If the path directly contains a SIF or sandbox, use it.  Otherwise if a path is a directory, look in the directory for the hash which could be the SIF or sandbox, and also for a directory containing the first two characters of the hash and then the hash inside that directory (for distributions of large numbers of these containers).  If a match is not found in one path component, continue to search through the basepath.   When a match is found, use it as a base container image and add the given image as an overlay layer.
- Additionally, it will work for the existing action command `--overlay` option to accept the overlay SIF or sandbox that was built by `apptainer build --overlay`, defaulting to read-only.

body:
The packages for Ubuntu 26.04 LTS are missing from the PPA:

```
Reading package lists...
E: The repository 'https://ppa.launchpadcontent.net/apptainer/ppa/ubuntu resolute Release' does not have a Release file.
Repository: 'Types: deb

This PPA contains stable releases of Apptainer.

Bug report https://github.com/apptainer/apptainer/issues
More info: https://launchpad.net/~apptainer/+archive/ubuntu/ppa
Adding repository.
```

This causes the installation script to fail, even if there is a package:

https://packages.ubuntu.com/search?keywords=apptainer

```
questing (25.10) (admin): container platform focused on supporting "Mobility of Compute" [universe]
1.4.0-6: amd64 arm64 armhf ppc64el riscv64 s390x
resolute (26.04LTS) (admin): container platform focused on supporting "Mobility of Compute" [universe]
1.4.5-1: amd64 arm64 armhf ppc64el riscv64 s390x
stonking (admin): container platform focused on supporting "Mobility of Compute" [universe]
1.4.5-1: amd64 arm64 armhf ppc64el riscv64 s390x
```

Since the Apptainer 1.5.0 release was a bit late, it missed the LTS but:

`apptainer/resolute,now 1.4.5-1 arm64 [installed]`

However, the deb is missing a couple of important dependencies:

```
Installing:                     
  apptainer

Installing dependencies:
  containernetworking-plugins
```

```
INFO:    squashfuse not found, will not be able to mount SIF or other squashfs files
INFO:    fuse2fs not found, will not be able to mount EXT3 filesystems
INFO:    gocryptfs not found, will not be able to use gocryptfs
INFO:    Converting SIF file to temporary sandbox...
```

It is possible to install them manually, and then it works OK:

Need to have: (depends)
```
Installing:                     
  squashfuse

Installing dependencies:
  libsquashfuse0
```

Nice to have: (recommends)
```
Installing:                     
  fuse2fs  gocryptfs

Suggested packages:
  fido2-tools
```

But they should be added to the ubuntu package, as dependencies?

The `squashfs-tools`  does have support for all decompressors, though.

    https://ppa.launchpadcontent.net/apptainer/ppa/ubuntu/

Release notes

Sourced from github.com/opencontainers/selinux's releases.

v1.14.0

This release fixes a regression in ExecLabel, bumps the minimal Go version to 1.22, and deprecates several functions in favor of improved API.

Fixed

  • ExecLabel was using an incorrect path (regression in v1.13.0). (opencontainers/selinux#253)

Deprecated

  • CategoryRange is deprecated; use SetCategoryRange instead. (opencontainers/selinux#262)
  • KVMContainerLabels is deprecated; use KVMContainerLabel instead. (opencontainers/selinux#262)
  • InitContainerLabels is deprecated; use InitContainerLabel instead. (opencontainers/selinux#262)
  • ReserveLabel is deprecated; use ReserveLabelV2 instead. (opencontainers/selinux#262)
  • ROFileLabel is deprecated; if you use it, open a new issue. (opencontainers/selinux#262)
  • ContainerLabels is deprecated, if you use it, open a new issue. (opencontainers/selinux#262)

Added

  • SEUserByName. (opencontainers/selinux#232, opencontainers/selinux#251)
  • CheckLabel. (opencontainers/selinux#250)
  • SetCategoryRange, KVMContainerLabel, InitContainerLabel, ReserveLabelV2. (opencontainers/selinux#262)

Changed

  • Switch to Go 1.22 as the minimally supported version (opencontainers/selinux#256)
  • Update GetDefaultContextWithLevel to fall back to failsafe context (opencontainers/selinux#232)
  • Use math/rand/v2 rather than crypto/rand for MCS label generation (opencontainers/selinux#257)

Miscellaneous

  • MAINTAINERS: add Aleksa as a maintainer. (opencontainers/selinux#243)
  • Assorted CI bumps and related fixes. (opencontainers/selinux#255)
  • Remove intToMcs. (opencontainers/selinux#259)
  • Use Cut more. (opencontainers/selinux#254)

title: Merge release-1.5 into main after 1.5.0
Relax validation on architecture and add variant information
body:
Currently we convert the arch and variant into a combined "buildarch".

But this _only_ happens for arm64v8 (and the legacy arm32 buildarch).

And v8 is the _only_ (current) alternative for arm64, so it is not used.

Instead, we should go back to just "arm64" - and record the variant...

----

The arm32 buildarches for the "arm" arch will be kept as-is, for compability.

But the arm32v7 buildarch can be changed to "arm" arch, it is the default.

buildarch | platform
--- | ---
arm32v5 | `linux/arm/v5`
arm32v6 | `linux/arm/v6`
arm32v7 | `linux/arm/v7`

Drop support for arm32v3 through arm32v4, since they are now obsolete.

The arm64v8 buildarch has been changed to "arm64" arch, like the "amd64".

* #2894 - commit 66c8e3ae5f635eef72d226504278112768d784c7

buildarch | platform
--- | ---
arm64v8 | `linux/arm64/v8`

There will be no validation on the variants, to allow for `v8.1` and newer too.
Similar to the other (*64) platforms, the variant is just recorded as metadata.

* #3460

https://github.com/opencontainers/image-spec/blob/v1.1.1/image-index.md#platform-variants

ISA/ABI	| architecture	| variant | variable | notes
--- | --- | --- | --- | ---
ARM 32-bit	| arm	| v5, v6, v7	| GOARM | validated
ARM 64-bit	| arm64	| v8, v8.1, …	| GOARM64 |
POWER8+	| ppc64le	| power8, power9, …	| GOPPC64 |
RISC-V	| riscv64	| rva20u64, …	| GORISCV64 |
x86-64	| amd64	| v1, v2, v3, …	| GOAMD64 |

Currently the container registries are **not** recording variants, causing issues.
That is, there are some `amd64/v3` containers that are mislabeled as `amd64` (v1).

title: Allow searching in oras registry or repository
body:
## Description of the Pull Request (PR):

Allow searching images from oras registries, in addition to library.

Maybe more like "listing" than searching, but that's what is there...

Doesn't seem to be any repository descriptions available either?

registry
https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/google/go-containerregistry@v0.21.3/pkg/name#Registry
```console
$ oras repo ls localhost:5000
artifact
bar/alpine
foo/alpine
$ apptainer search oras://localhost:5000
Found 4 container images for amd64 matching "localhost:5000":

	oras://localhost:5000/artifact:latest

	oras://localhost:5000/bar/alpine:latest

	oras://localhost:5000/foo/alpine:v1

	oras://localhost:5000/foo/alpine:v2
```

repository (in a registry)
https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/google/go-containerregistry@v0.21.3/pkg/name#Repository
```console
$ oras repo tags localhost:5000/foo/alpine
v1
v2
$ apptainer search oras://localhost:5000/foo/alpine
Found 2 container images for amd64 matching "localhost:5000/foo/alpine":

	oras://localhost:5000/foo/alpine:v1

	oras://localhost:5000/foo/alpine:v2
```

title: Update the metadata from label-schema to opencontainers.image
body:
Currently using the old labels from `org.label-schema`, and without verification.
Should be updated to `org.opencontainers.image` and follow the specification.

https://github.com/opencontainers/image-spec/blob/main/annotations.md#back-compatibility-with-label-schema

https://github.com/opencontainers/image-spec/blob/main/annotations.md#pre-defined-annotation-keys

```
org.label-schema.build-arch: amd64
org.label-schema.build-date: Tuesday_21_April_2026_12:35:10_CEST
org.label-schema.schema-version: 1.0
org.label-schema.usage.apptainer.version: 1.5.0-rc.2+67-gbbd29005a
org.label-schema.usage.singularity.deffile.bootstrap: docker
org.label-schema.usage.singularity.deffile.from: alpine
```

```
org.opencontainers.image.architecture: amd64
org.opencontainers.image.base.digest: sha256:5b10f432ef3da1b8d4c7eb6c487f2f5a8f096bc91145e68878dd4a5019afde11
org.opencontainers.image.base.name: docker.io/library/alpine:latest
org.opencontainers.image.created: 2026-04-21T12:35:10+02:00
```

The old build-date is not following the specification, and is hard to parse.
See <https://xkcd.com/1179/>, it is supposed to follow RFC3339/ISO8601

```
	RFC3339     = "2006-01-02T15:04:05Z07:00"
	RFC3339Nano = "2006-01-02T15:04:05.999999999Z07:00"
```

This will help with implementing the ORAS "created" reporting and with variants.
Currently only the old ARM variants are supported, but 1.1.1 adds new variants.

* https://github.com/opencontainers/image-spec/blob/v1.1.0/spec.md

ISA/ABI	| architecture	| variant| Old arch | Old var
--- | --- | --- | --- | ---
ARM 32-bit, v6	| arm	| v6 | arm32v6 | 6
ARM 32-bit, v7	| arm	| v7 | arm32v7 | 7 
ARM 32-bit, v8	| arm	| v8 | arm32v8 | 8
ARM 64-bit, v8	| arm64	| v8 | arm64v8 | 8 (aarch64)

* https://github.com/opencontainers/image-spec/blob/v1.1.1/spec.md

ISA/ABI	| architecture	| variant	| Go analog
--- | --- | --- | ---
ARM 32-bit	| arm	| v6, v7, v8	| GOARM
ARM 64-bit	| arm64	| v8, v8.1, …	| GOARM64
POWER8+	| ppc64le	| power8, power9, …	| GOPPC64
IBM z/Arch | s390x | |
RISC-V	| riscv64	| rva20u64, …	| GORISCV64
x86-64	| amd64	| v1, v2, v3, …	| GOAMD64
LoongArch | loong64 | |

It uses `org.opencontainers.image.variant`, if it has been set in buildarch.
The old arm32 variants v3-v4 can be removed, they are not used anywhere.

Note: this issue is just for the metadata

For compatibility reasons, it can use both

title: Prepare for 1.5.0-rc.2
Allow deleting from oras registry if supported
body:
## Description of the Pull Request (PR):

Not all registries support deleting images or manifests.

Also add a NormalizeRef function for showing nice names.

Before
```
FATAL:   unsupported protocol scheme "oras" for delete
```

After
```
$ apptainer delete oras://localhost:5000/alpine
Are you sure you want to delete localhost:5000/alpine:latest (amd64) [y/N] y
FATAL:   Unable to delete image from oci registry: DELETE http://localhost:5000/v2/alpine/manifests/latest: UNSUPPORTED: The operation is unsupported.
```

Some registries do allow deleting images, like Zot

```
$ apptainer delete oras://localhost:5000/alpine
Are you sure you want to delete localhost:5000/alpine:latest (amd64) [y/N] y
INFO:    Image localhost:5000/alpine:latest (amd64) deleted.
```

Release notes

Sourced from google.golang.org/grpc's releases.

Release 1.79.3

Security

  • server: fix an authorization bypass where malformed :path headers (missing the leading slash) could bypass path-based restricted "deny" rules in interceptors like grpc/authz. Any request with a non-canonical path is now immediately rejected with an Unimplemented error. (#8981)

Release 1.79.2

Bug Fixes

  • stats: Prevent redundant error logging in health/ORCA producers by skipping stats/tracing processing when no stats handler is configured. (grpc/grpc-go#8874)

Release 1.79.1

Bug Fixes

  • grpc: Remove the -dev suffix from the User-Agent header. (grpc/grpc-go#8902)

Release 1.79.0

API Changes

  • mem: Add experimental API SetDefaultBufferPool to change the default buffer pool. (#8806)
    • Special Thanks: @​vanja-p
  • experimental/stats: Update MetricsRecorder to require embedding the new UnimplementedMetricsRecorder (a no-op struct) in all implementations for forward compatibility. (#8780)

Behavior Changes

  • balancer/weightedtarget: Remove handling of Addresses and only handle Endpoints in resolver updates. (#8841)

New Features

  • experimental/stats: Add support for asynchronous gauge metrics through the new AsyncMetricReporter and RegisterAsyncReporter APIs. (#8780)
  • pickfirst: Add support for weighted random shuffling of endpoints, as described in gRFC A113.
    • This is enabled by default, and can be turned off using the environment variable GRPC_EXPERIMENTAL_PF_WEIGHTED_SHUFFLING. (#8864)
  • xds: Implement :authority rewriting, as specified in gRFC A81. (#8779)
  • balancer/randomsubsetting: Implement the random_subsetting LB policy, as specified in gRFC A68. (#8650)
    • Special Thanks: @​marek-szews

Bug Fixes

  • credentials/tls: Fix a bug where the port was not stripped from the authority override before validation. (#8726)
    • Special Thanks: @​Atul1710
  • xds/priority: Fix a bug causing delayed failover to lower-priority clusters when a higher-priority cluster is stuck in CONNECTING state. (#8813)
  • health: Fix a bug where health checks failed for clients using legacy compression options (WithDecompressor or RPCDecompressor). (#8765)
    • Special Thanks: @​sanki92
  • transport: Fix an issue where the HTTP/2 server could skip header size checks when terminating a stream early. (#8769)
    • Special Thanks: @​joybestourous
  • server: Propagate status detail headers, if available, when terminating a stream during request header processing. (#8754)
    • Special Thanks: @​joybestourous

Performance Improvements

  • credentials/alts: Optimize read buffer alignment to reduce copies. (#8791)
  • mem: Optimize pooling and creation of buffer objects. (#8784)
  • transport: Reduce slice re-allocations by reserving slice capacity. (#8797)

title: feat: add loong64 architecture
body:
## Description of the Pull Request (PR):
Add loong(arch)64 support.
The sif support already merged in https://github.com/apptainer/sif/pull/297 .

Due to non-technical reasons ( https://github.com/docker-library/official-images/issues/16404 ), there is no official linux/loong64 docker image, so I didn't add loong64 support in dist/docker/*

For the similar reason, I disabled `internal/pkg/build/source/conveyorPacker_library_test.go#TestLibraryPacker` on some architectures.
Command for checking sycloud alpine image architectures support:

```bash
for arch in "arm" "arm64" "amd64" "386" "ppc64le" "s390x" "riscv64" "loong64"; do
    curl --fail -s -o /dev/null "https://library.production.sycloud.io/v1/images/alpine:latest?arch=$arch" && echo "support $arch"
done

# outputs:
# support arm64
# support amd64
# support ppc64le
```

Test platform:
- Machine: Loongson-3B6000x1-7A2000x1-EVB
- Distro: Alpine linux 3.24.0_alpha20260127
- Kernel:  6.18.16-0-lts
- Go: go1.26.1 linux/loong64

`make -C builddir test` outputs:
[apptainer-test.log](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/25993724/apptainer-test.log)

The reason of test failures:
- TestGet:
  In Alpine Linux, the cat command is a symlink to `/bin/coreutils` or `/bin/busybox`.
  coreutils/busybox binaries use argv[0] to determine which applet to run.
  Modify argv[0] cause the binary will fail to recognize the intended command and won't know which function to execute.
- TestEncrypt: **I have no idea, seems like it's the problem of cryptsetup or udev (I use libudev-zero)**
- TestLdCache: musl `ldconfig` has different command flags compare to glibc
- TestResolve: `libc.so` only belong to glibc
- TestFromSif: no `e2e/testdata/busybox_loong64.sif` file

Bumps the opencontainers group with 1 update: [github.com/opencontainers/runc](https://github.com/opencontainers/runc). Updates `github.com/opencontainers/runc` from 1.4.0 to 1.4.1
Changelog

Sourced from github.com/opencontainers/runc's changelog.

[1.4.1] - 2026-03-12

La guerre n'est pas une aventure. La guerre est une maladie. Comme le typhus.

Deprecated

  • libcontainer/configs.MPOL_* constants added in runc [1.4.0][]. (#5110, #5055)

Added

  • Preliminary loong64 support. (#5062, #4938)

Fixed

  • libct: fix panic in initSystemdProps when processing certain systemd properties in the OCI spec. (#5161, #5133)
  • libct: fix several file descriptor leaks on error paths. (#5168, #5009)
  • Remove unnecessary crypto/tls dependency by open-coding the systemd socket activation logic, allowing us to more easily avoid false positive CVE warnings. (#5093, #5057)
  • Remove legacy os.Is* error usage, improving error type detection to make our error fallback paths more robust. (#5162, #5061)
  • Go 1.26 has started enforcing a restriction of os/exec.Cmd which caused issues with our usage of CLONE_INTO_CGROUP (on newer kernels). This has now been resolved. (#5116, #5091)
  • Recursive atime-related mount flags (rrelatime et al.) are now applied properly. (#5114, #5098)
  • Fix a regression in runc exec due to CLONE_INTO_CGROUP in the (inadvisable) scenario where a container is configured without cgroup namespaces and with /sys/fs/cgroup mounted rw. (#5117, #5101)
  • On machines with more than 1024 CPU cores, our logic for resetting the CPU affinity will now correctly reset the affinity onto all available cores (not just the first 1024). (#5149, #5025)
  • PR #4757 caused a regression that resulted in spurious cannot start a container that has stopped errors when running runc create and has thus been reverted. (#5157, #5153, #5151, #4645, #4757)

Changed

  • Previously we made an attempt to make our runc.armhf release binaries work with ARMv6 (which would allow runc to work on the original Raspberry Pi). Unfortunately, this has effectively always been broken (because we cross-compile libseccomp within a Debian container and statically link to it) and so we are now officially matching the Debian definition of armhf (that is, ARMv7). (#5167, #5103)
  • Minor signing keyring updates. (#5147, #5139, #5144, #5148)

This adds a bundled, modified (by the rootless-containers project) PRoot around mksquashfs in order to preserve the file owner and group information that is stored by umoci in `rootlesscontainers` extended attributes. title: Race condition with APPTAINER_SHARENS=true when multiple srun tasks start simultaneously
body:
## Version of Apptainer ```bash $ apptainer --version apptainer version 1.4.5-3.el9 ``` ## Version of Slurm ```bash $ srun --version slurm 25.11.3 ``` ## Linux OS distro ```bash NAME="Rocky Linux" VERSION="9.7 (Blue Onyx)" ID="rocky" ID_LIKE="rhel centos fedora" VERSION_ID="9.7" PLATFORM_ID="platform:el9" PRETTY_NAME="Rocky Linux 9.7 (Blue Onyx)" ANSI_COLOR="0;32" LOGO="fedora-logo-icon" CPE_NAME="cpe:/o:rocky:rocky:9::baseos" HOME_URL="https://rockylinux.org/" VENDOR_NAME="RESF" VENDOR_URL="https://resf.org/" BUG_REPORT_URL="https://bugs.rockylinux.org/" SUPPORT_END="2032-05-31" ROCKY_SUPPORT_PRODUCT="Rocky-Linux-9" ROCKY_SUPPORT_PRODUCT_VERSION="9.7" REDHAT_SUPPORT_PRODUCT="Rocky Linux" REDHAT_SUPPORT_PRODUCT_VERSION="9.7" ``` ## Kernel ```bash $ uname -r 5.14.0-611.27.1.el9_7.x86_64 ``` ## Expected behaviour When running a Slurm job with multiple tasks per node and `APPTAINER_SHARENS=true ` set in the environment, all tasks should successfully execute inside the container. Specifically, with --ntasks-per-node=N, with `2<= N <=N_MAX` all tasks should run properly the executable like ` hostname` and exit cleanly. ## Actual observed behaviour As soon as one `srun --tasks-per-node >=2`, tasks fail with namespace and proc directory errors. Only one task per node works correctly; with two or more tasks per node , they crash with: ```bash ERROR : Failed to enter in user namespace: No such process FATAL: could not open proc directory /proc/849066: no such file or directory FATAL: could not open proc directory /proc/849066: no such file or directory srun: error: ccexe0167: tasks 0,2: Exited with exit code 255 srun: error: ccexe0167: task 1: Exited with exit code 1 ``` This is incorrect because APPTAINER_SHARENS=true is designed to enable MPI across nodes by putting all processes in the same user namespace alloying accordingly advanced IPC techniques (posix shm, cma ), and should work regardless of if the process is MPI or not, and regardless of how many tasks start simultaneously via `srun`. ## Reproduce behaviour ```bash #!/bin/bash #SBATCH --nodes=1 #SBATCH --ntasks-per-node=2 #SBATCH --partition=long #SBATCH --cpus-per-task=1 #SBATCH --time=00:20:00 #SBATCH --output=test_%j.out #SBATCH --error=test_%j.err # Environment export CONT=my_ompi_container.sif export APPTAINER_BINDPATH=/lustre/username export APPTAINER_SHARENS=true export APPTAINER_CONFIGDIR=/tmp/$USER # launch via srun srun --export=ALL apptainer exec $CONT hostname ``` Submission via `sbatch`. ## Test Results | Configuration | Command | Result | Error Message | |--------------|---------|--------|---------------| | 1 task per node | `srun --ntasks-per-node=1 apptainer exec $CONT hostname` | ✅ Success | None | | 2 tasks per node | `srun --ntasks-per-node=2 apptainer exec $CONT hostname` | ❌ Failure | `ERROR : Failed to enter in user namespace: No such process`
`FATAL: could not open proc directory /proc/849066: no such file or directory`
`srun: error: ccexe0167: tasks 0,2: Exited with exit code 255`
`srun: error: ccexe0167: task 1: Exited with exit code 1` | | 2 tasks per node with sleep delay | `srun --ntasks-per-node=2 apptainer exec $CONT bash -c "sleep 1 && hostname"` | ✅ Success | None | ## Possible explanation ? This behaviour can be dued to a race condition in namespace creation/joining when multiple `srun` launched tasks start simultaneously with `APPTAINER_SHARENS=true` Without `APPTAINER_SHARENS=true` the race condition problem does not exists. Note that i have notice the same behaviour with an older version of apptainer `1.3` and older Linux OS RL8.10 with cgroups v1 with the same errors.

title: Subuid fakeroot with suid mode fails to import passwd and group files
body:
### Version of Apptainer

1.4.5-3.el8

### Expected behavior

I expect that subuid fakeroot mode works when apptainer-suid is used

### Actual behavior

Prints warnings about missing `passwd` and `group` file and they are missing.

### Steps to reproduce this behavior

After installing apptainer-suid and with /etc/sub[ug]id set up:

```
$ apptainer exec -f docker://busybox ls -l /etc/passwd
INFO:    Using cached SIF image
WARNING: passwd file doesn't exist in container, not updating
WARNING: group file doesn't exist in container, not updating
-rw-r--r--    1 3382     9767           340 Sep 26  2024 /etc/passwd
```

But it works when apptainer-suid is not installed or when simulating that with `-u`:
```
$ apptainer exec -f -u docker://busybox ls -l /etc/passwd
INFO:    Using cached SIF image
-rw-r--r--    1 root     root           340 Mar  9 15:46 /etc/passwd
```

It also works with the fakeroot command based fakeroot (where that works):
```
$ apptainer exec -f --ignore-subuid docker://ubuntu:22.04 ls -l /etc/passwd
INFO:    Using cached SIF image
INFO:    User not listed in /etc/subuid, trying root-mapped namespace
INFO:    Using cached SIF image
INFO:    Using fakeroot command combined with root-mapped namespace
-rw-r--r-- 1 root root 922 Mar  9 15:51 /etc/passwd
```

Rocky 8

EPEL

title: Add more detailed documentation for the new features in 1.5.0
body:
https://hpsf.io/blog/2026/charting-the-future-of-high-performance-software-hpsf-year-in-review-and-whats-ahead/#apptainer

> In 2026 we plan to release the 1.5.x series.  New feature highlights planned are support for Container Device Interface (CDI) descriptors for generic handling of new hardware devices, a new buildkit bootstrap for building Apptainer containers directly from Dockerfile descriptors, an option for building completely reproducible SIF containers, and the ability to download SIF files using an InterPlanetary File System (IPFS) gateway.

From the CHANGELOG:

- Add support for Container Device Interface (CDI) through new
  `--device` and `--cdi-dirs` run/shell/exec options.

- Add new bootstrap `buildkit:` (and `buildkit:` URL) for building SIF images
  directly from Dockerfile, without having to use Docker/Podman but only BuildKit.
  The full buildkit log file is included in the image, for traceability.
  _EDIT: Should also mention the `dockerfile:` compatibility alias, and `docker`?_
  
 - Create reproducible SIF images, if the environment variable `SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH`
   has been set (it is a Unix timestamp given as seconds, in the UTC timezone).
  Add `--reproducible` flag (_and env_) to build and pull, from `oras://` sources.
  This sets SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH automatically from the image "created" time.

- Add support for downloading SIF images from an IPFS peer-to-peer cluster using
  a HTTP gateway (similar to the existing support for IPFS in the `curl` tool).
  The location of the address can set in the `IPFS_GATEWAY` environment variable,

title: Find an alternative to wiping the global Go build cache
body:
Currently when you build all of Apptainer, it will clear out the Go cache (for **all** projects)

This means that your next builds will be slow again, because the cache has been wiped.

It would be nice if there was a better (less intrusive) way to do this?

Like setting a special GOCACHE only for "starter", or maybe disabling it.

----

I was trying with the `go build -a` flag, maybe that would be enough.

```diff
index 1184a40c7..40d3f6d8f 100644
--- a/mlocal/frags/build_runtime.mk
+++ b/mlocal/frags/build_runtime.mk
@@ -13,19 +13,13 @@ $(starter_deps): $(GO_MODFILES)
 starter_CSOURCE := $(wildcard $(SOURCEDIR)/cmd/starter/c/*.c)
 starter_CSOURCE += $(wildcard $(SOURCEDIR)/cmd/starter/c/include/*.h)
 
-$(BUILDDIR_ABSPATH)/.clean-starter: $(starter_CSOURCE)
-       @echo " GO clean -cache"
-       -$(V)$(GO) clean -cache 2>/dev/null
-       $(V)touch $@
-
-
 # starter
 # Look at dependencies file changes via starter_deps
 # because it means that a module was updated.
 starter := $(BUILDDIR_ABSPATH)/cmd/starter/c/starter
-$(starter): $(BUILDDIR_ABSPATH)/.clean-starter $(apptainer_build_config) $(starter_deps) $(starter_SOURCE)
+$(starter): $(apptainer_build_config) $(starter_deps) $(starter_SOURCE)
        @echo " GO" $@
-       $(V)cd $(SOURCEDIR) && $(GO) build $(GO_MODFLAGS) $(GO_BUILDMODE) \
+       $(V)cd $(SOURCEDIR) && $(GO) build -a $(GO_MODFLAGS) $(GO_BUILDMODE) \
                $(GO_GCFLAGS) $(GO_LDFLAGS) -tags "$(GO_TAGS)" \
                -o $@ cmd/starter/main_linux.go
 ```

This is related to not rebuilding when only C code is modified: 7c6073ced91b8cf91de6f8d1da4189f783670d41

Maybe `GOCACHE=$(mktemp -d)`

title: Create the GitHub Actions cache from the base branch
body:
If you create a cache in a PR, it **only** applies to that particular PR (any further update).

`refs/pull/1234/merge`

https://github.com/apptainer/apptainer/actions/caches

To be able to use the cache also in other PR, it needs to be on the main (or rel) branch.

`refs/heads/main`

See [https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/dependency-caching](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/dependency-caching#restrictions-for-accessing-a-cache)

`main`

```yaml
name: ci
on:
  pull_request:

```

`release-1.4` (etc)

```yaml
name: release
on:

    tags:

```

Bumps [github.com/samber/lo](https://github.com/samber/lo) from 1.49.1 to 1.53.0.
Release notes

Sourced from github.com/samber/lo's releases.

v1.53.0

Announcing the latest release of lo with lots of good gifts! 🎁

🌊 First, a big thanks to @​d-enk for making lots of performance improvements in the recent weeks.

🧪 Second, this release introduces a new simd experimental package. If you run on an amd64 architecture and a recent CPU, you can perform very fast operations thanks to SIMD CPU instructions. -> Documentation: https://lo.samber.dev/docs/experimental/simd

💥 Third, this version adds *Err variants of many lo helpers (like MapErr, FlatMapErr, ReduceErr, etc.) whose callbacks can return an error and short-circuit execution when one occurs.

[!NOTE] The simd sub-package is considered not stable. We might break the initial API based on developers' feedback in the coming months.

Features & improvements

  • feat: adding SIMD helpers by @​samber in samber/lo#801
  • feat: adding Error variants: MapErr, FlatMapErr, ReduceErr... by @​samber in samber/lo#823
  • feat: support for buffer iterator by @​mimol91 in samber/lo#824
  • feat: add Take, TakeWhile, FilterTake, Window, and Sliding functions by @​juliazadorozhnaya in samber/lo#760

  • feat: add iterator slice helpers by @​juliazadorozhnaya in samber/lo#791
  • feat(it): adding loit.Concat by @​samber in samber/lo#722
  • feat: Allow Union/Intersect to take many lists by @​frankywahl in samber/lo#181
  • feat: Add Clone function to return shallow copy of slice collections by @​quexer in samber/lo#732
  • feat: IntersectBy by @​ghosx in samber/lo#653
  • feat: Support Custom Assert by @​RelicOfTesla in samber/lo#755
  • feat: Must support Custom error handler. by @​RelicOfTesla in samber/lo#752
  • feat: WithoutNth handle non-comparable types by @​urisimchoni in samber/lo#774
  • refactor: remove unnecessary type arguments in NewThrottle by @​d-enk in samber/lo#773
  • refactor: lo.IntersectBy + adding loit.IntersectBy + adding doc by @​samber in samber/lo#739
  • fix: rename IsSortedByKey to IsSortedBy by @​NathanBaulch in samber/lo#735
  • fix(iter/tuples): support break iteration over Zip[By] seq by @​d-enk in samber/lo#757
  • fix(it.Mode): align behavior with lo.Mode and ensure consistent slice… by @​intojhanurag in samber/lo#711
  • fix: improve Clone function to preserve nilness and avoid liveness issues by @​quexer in samber/lo#740
  • fix: reset n counter per iteration in it.Replace by @​LikimiaD in samber/lo#799
  • fix: make Ellipsis operate on runes instead of bytes to prevent Unicode truncation by @​veeceey in samber/lo#796
  • fix: correct DropByIndex handling of negative indices out of bounds by @​d-enk in samber/lo#778

Deprecation

  • refactor: remove helpers deprecated for more than 3y by @​samber in samber/lo#810

Performance improvements

  • feat: Optimize UniqMap to reduce unnecessary slice preallocation by @​ivolkoff in samber/lo#710
  • refactor(it): simplify DropLast, TrimSuffix, TrimPrefix and use range loops by @​d-enk in samber/lo#782

Bumps the opencontainers group with 3 updates: [github.com/opencontainers/runc](https://github.com/opencontainers/runc), [github.com/opencontainers/runtime-spec](https://github.com/opencontainers/runtime-spec) and [github.com/opencontainers/umoci](https://github.com/opencontainers/umoci). Updates `github.com/opencontainers/runc` from 1.2.8 to 1.4.0
Release notes

Sourced from github.com/opencontainers/runc's releases.

runc v1.4.0 -- "路漫漫其修远兮，吾将上下而求索！"

This is the first release of the 1.4.z release branch of runc. It contains a few fixes for issues found in 1.4.0-rc.3. This version of runc supports runtime-spec v1.3 (see [docs/spec-conformance.md][] for the few features that are still missing).

This is the second release of runc following our new release and support policy (see [RELEASES.md][] for more details). This means that, as of this release:

  • The runc 1.2.z release branch will now only receive high severity CVE fixes, and will no longer be supported in less than 6 months (end of April 2026).
  • The runc 1.3.z release branch will now only receive security and "significant" bugfixes.
  • Users are encouraged to plan migrating to runc 1.4.0 as soon as possible.
  • Despite this release being delayed by a month, users should still expect a runc 1.5.0 release in late April 2026.

Deprecated

  • Deprecate cgroup v1. (#4956)
  • Deprecate CleanPath, StripRoot, WithProcfd, and WithProcfdFile from libcontainer/utils. (#4985)

Breaking

  • The handling of pids.limit has been updated to match the newer guidance from the OCI runtime specification. In particular, now a maximum limit value of 0 will be treated as an actual limit (due to limitations with systemd, it will be treated the same as a limit value of 1). We only expect users that explicitly set pids.limit to 0 will see a behaviour change. opencontainers/cgroups#48#4949)

Fixed

  • opencontainers/cgroups#43
  • cgroups: retry DBus connection when it fails with EAGAIN. opencontainers/cgroups#45
  • cgroups: improve cpuacct.usage_all resilience when parsing data from opencontainers/cgroups#46 opencontainers/cgroups#50)
  • libct: close child fds on prepareCgroupFD error. (#4936)
  • libct: fix mips compilation. (#4962, #4967)
  • When configuring a tmpfs mount, only set the mode= argument if the target path already existed. This fixes a regression introduced in our [CVE-2025-52881][] mitigation patches. (#4971, #4976)
  • Fix various file descriptor leaks and add additional tests to detect them as comprehensively as possible. (#5007, #5021, #5034)
  • The "hallucination" helpers added as part of the [CVE-2025-52881][] mitigation have been made more generic and now apply to all of our pathrs helper functions, which should ensure we will not regress dangling symlink

Updates `github.com/opencontainers/umoci` from 0.4.7 to 0.6.0
Release notes

Sourced from github.com/opencontainers/umoci's releases.

umoci 0.5.1 -- "🖤 Yuki (2021-2025)"

This is a fairly minor update to umoci, containing a few bugfixes for some potential issues, as well as finally removing the requirement for oci-image-tool validation. We still do not support the latest image-spec release, but decoupling for oci-image-tool is a very important first step.

Fixed

  • For images with an empty index.json, umoci will no longer incorrectly set the manifests entry to null (which was technically a violation of the specification, though such images cannot be pushed or interacted with outside of umoci).
  • Based on some recent developments in the image-spec, umoci will now produce an error if it encounters descriptors with a negative size (this was a potential DoS vector previously) as well as a theoretical attack where an attacker would endlessly write to a blob (this would not be generally exploitable for images with descriptors).

Changed

  • We now use go:embed to fill the version information of umoci --version, allowing for users to get a reasonable binary with go install. However, we still recommend using our official binaries, using distribution binaries, or building from source with make.

  • Rather than using oci-image-tool validate for validating images in our tests, we now make use of some hand-written smoke tests as well as the jq-based validators maintained in docker-library/meta-scripts.

    This is intended to act as a stop-gap until umoci validate is implemented (and after that, we may choose to keep the jq-based validators as a double-check that our own validators are working correctly).

Thanks to the following contributors who made this release possible:

  • Adam Korcz Adam@adalogics.com
  • Akhil Mohan akhilerm@gmail.com
  • Aleksa Sarai cyphar@cyphar.com

This release is dedicated to our cat Yuki who sadly passed away on Friday. Most of the code I've written in the past four years was written with him purring away on my chest, and he was the most loving cat I've ever met. Rest in peace, little buddy. I hope you enjoyed your time with us, and I'll always keep you in my heart. 🖤

Changelog

Sourced from github.com/opencontainers/umoci's changelog.

[0.6.0] - 2025-10-15

Please mind the gap between the train and the platform.

This update to umoci includes support for v1.1.1 of the OCI image specification. For the most part, this mostly involves supporting reading new features added to the specification (such as embedded-data descriptors and subject references used by OCI artifact images), but at the moment umoci does not yet support creating images utilising these features.

In addition, umoci also now supports generating config.json blobs that are compliant with v1.2.1 of the OCI runtime specification. Note that we do not explicitly use any of the newer features, this is mostly a quality-of-life update to move away from our ancient pinned version of the runtime-spec.

Breaking

  • github.com/opencontainers/umoci/oci/config/generate.Generator has had the following breaking API changes made to it:
    • The existing ConfigExposedPorts and ConfigVolumes methods now return a sorted []string instead of a map.
    • The (Set)OS and (Set)Architecture methods have been renamed to have a Platform prefix (to match image-spec v1.1's organisational changes). They now read as (Set)PlatformOS and (Set)PlatformArchitecture respectively.

Added

  • umoci stat now includes information about the manifest and configuration of the image, both in the regular and JSON-formatted outputs.

  • umoci now has [SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH][source-date-epoch] support, to attempt to make it easier to create reproducible images. Our behaviour is modelled after tar --clamp-mtime, meaning that SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH will only be used to modify the timestamps of files newer than SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH.

    As umoci repack works based on diffs, this also means that only files that were modified (and will thus be usually be included in the new layer) will have their timestamps rewritten.

    --history.created and umoci config --created will also now default to SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH (if set).

    With this change, umoci should be fairly compliant with reproducible builds. Please let us know if you find any other problematic areas in umoci (we are investigating some other possible causes of instability such as Go map iteration).

  • In order to avoid the need for a [patched gomtree package][obs-gomtree] that supports rootless mode, umoci now has a umoci raw mtree-validate subcommand that implements the key gomtree validate features we need for our integration tests.

    Note that this subcommand is not intended for wider use outside of our tests (and it is hidden from the help pages for a reason). Most users are probably

title: libsubid.so.3 missing when executing run-help in unprivileged installation
body:
### Version of Apptainer
1.4.3

### Expected behavior

I am attempting an unprivileged installation of Apptainer on an Ubuntu system. The required packages curl,  rpm2cpio, cpio are installed and the installation command according to the documentation is executed successfully. Now ```apptainer run-help test.sif``` is executed for a test image. Expected is the output from the %help section of the image.

### Actual behavior
```
/opt/apptainer/app/x86_64/bin/apptainer: /opt/apptainer/app/x86_64/utils/lib/libselinux.so.1: no version information available (required by /opt/apptainer/lib/libsubid.so.3)
/opt/apptainer/app/x86_64/bin/apptainer: /opt/apptainer/app/x86_64/utils/lib/libselinux.so.1: no version information available (required by /lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libsemanage.so.2)
/opt/apptainer/app/x86_64/bin/apptainer: error while loading shared libraries: libsubid.so.3: cannot open shared object file: No such file or directory
FATAL:   While getting run-help: exit status 127
```
libsubid.so.3 has been manually installed and is recognized by ldd.
```
>ldd /opt/apptainer/app/x86_64/bin/apptainer 
	linux-vdso.so.1 (0x00007ffd02f76000)
	libsubid.so.3 => /opt/apptainer/lib/libsubid.so.3 (0x00007094807ab000)
	libpthread.so.0 => /lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libpthread.so.0 (0x00007094807a4000)
	libdl.so.2 => /lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libdl.so.2 (0x000070948079f000)
	libresolv.so.2 => /lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libresolv.so.2 (0x000070948078b000)
	libseccomp.so.2 => /lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libseccomp.so.2 (0x000070948076b000)
	libc.so.6 => /lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libc.so.6 (0x000070947d000000)
	libaudit.so.1 => /lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libaudit.so.1 (0x000070948073b000)
	libselinux.so.1 => /lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libselinux.so.1 (0x000070948070f000)
	libsemanage.so.2 => /lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libsemanage.so.2 (0x00007094806ce000)
	libcrypt.so.2 => /opt/apptainer/lib/libcrypt.so.2 (0x0000709480694000)
	libacl.so.1 => /lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libacl.so.1 (0x000070948068a000)
	libattr.so.1 => /lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libattr.so.1 (0x0000709480680000)
	/lib64/ld-linux-x86-64.so.2 (0x00007094807eb000)
	libcap-ng.so.0 => /lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libcap-ng.so.0 (0x0000709480678000)
	libpcre2-8.so.0 => /lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libpcre2-8.so.0 (0x000070947d369000)
	libsepol.so.2 => /lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libsepol.so.2 (0x000070947d2b8000)
	libbz2.so.1.0 => /lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libbz2.so.1.0 (0x0000709480665000)
```

### Steps to reproduce this behavior

For reproducibility, I created an image on a system with a privileged installation. In the image, an unprivileged installation is performed. The missing libraries libsubid.so.3 and libcrypt.so.2 are manually added.
```
Bootstrap: docker
From: ubuntu:22.04

%post
    apt update
    apt install curl -y
    apt install rpm2cpio -y
    apt install cpio -y
    apt clean
    
    mkdir -p /opt/apptainer/app /opt/apptainer/lib
    curl -s https://raw.githubusercontent.com/apptainer/apptainer/main/tools/install-unprivileged.sh | \
    bash -s - /opt/apptainer/app
    
    # https://rhel.pkgs.org/9/red-hat-ubi-baseos-x86_64/shadow-utils-subid-4.9-15.el9.x86_64.rpm.html
    curl https://cdn-ubi.redhat.com/content/public/ubi/dist/ubi9/9/x86_64/baseos/os/Packages/s/shadow-utils-subid-4.9-15.el9.x86_64.rpm | \
    rpm2cpio -| cpio -idum -D /opt/apptainer/lib
    find /opt/apptainer/lib/ -name libsubid.so.3 -exec cp  {} /opt/apptainer/lib/ \;
    rm -r /opt/apptainer/lib/usr
    
    # https://rhel.pkgs.org/9/red-hat-ubi-baseos-x86_64/libxcrypt-4.4.18-3.el9.x86_64.rpm.html
    curl https://cdn-ubi.redhat.com/content/public/ubi/dist/ubi9/9/x86_64/baseos/os/Packages/l/libxcrypt-4.4.18-3.el9.x86_64.rpm | \
    rpm2cpio -| cpio -idum -D /opt/apptainer/lib
    find /opt/apptainer/lib/ -name libcrypt.so.2 -exec cp  {} /opt/apptainer/lib/ \;
    rm -r /opt/apptainer/lib/usr
    
%environment
    export PATH=/opt/apptainer/app/bin:$PATH
    export LD_LIBRARY_PATH=/opt/apptainer/lib:$LD_LIBRARY_PATH
    export LC_ALL=C
```
The container was always started with ```apptainer shell -c --bind ./test:/mnt --writable-tmpfs --fakeroot ApptainerUnprivileged.sif```
In ./test was a test image, which was mounted under /mnt. For that image, the command ```apptainer run-help /mnt/test.sif``` should have been executed.

The test image:
```
Bootstrap: docker
From: alpine:3.23.3

%help
    Success! 
```
Please let me know if I make an obvious mistake here. Thanks for your time.

runc v1.4.0 -- "路漫漫其修远兮，吾将上下而求索！"

This is the second release of runc following our new release and support policy (see [RELEASES.md][] for more details). This means that, as of this release:

  • The runc 1.2.z release branch will now only receive high severity CVE fixes, and will no longer be supported in less than 6 months (end of April 2026).
  • The runc 1.3.z release branch will now only receive security and "significant" bugfixes.
  • Users are encouraged to plan migrating to runc 1.4.0 as soon as possible.

Updates `github.com/opencontainers/umoci` from 0.4.7 to 0.6.0
Release notes

Sourced from github.com/opencontainers/umoci's releases.

umoci 0.5.1 -- "🖤 Yuki (2021-2025)"

This is a fairly minor update to umoci, containing a few bugfixes for some potential issues, as well as finally removing the requirement for oci-image-tool validation. We still do not support the latest image-spec release, but decoupling for oci-image-tool is a very important first step.

Fixed

  • For images with an empty index.json, umoci will no longer incorrectly set the manifests entry to null (which was technically a violation of the specification, though such images cannot be pushed or interacted with outside of umoci).
  • Based on some recent developments in the image-spec, umoci will now produce an error if it encounters descriptors with a negative size (this was a potential DoS vector previously) as well as a theoretical attack where an attacker would endlessly write to a blob (this would not be generally exploitable for images with descriptors).

Changed

  • We now use go:embed to fill the version information of umoci --version, allowing for users to get a reasonable binary with go install. However, we still recommend using our official binaries, using distribution binaries, or building from source with make.

  • Rather than using oci-image-tool validate for validating images in our tests, we now make use of some hand-written smoke tests as well as the jq-based validators maintained in docker-library/meta-scripts.

    This is intended to act as a stop-gap until umoci validate is implemented (and after that, we may choose to keep the jq-based validators as a double-check that our own validators are working correctly).

Thanks to the following contributors who made this release possible:

  • Adam Korcz Adam@adalogics.com
  • Akhil Mohan akhilerm@gmail.com
  • Aleksa Sarai cyphar@cyphar.com

This release is dedicated to our cat Yuki who sadly passed away on Friday. Most of the code I've written in the past four years was written with him purring away on my chest, and he was the most loving cat I've ever met. Rest in peace, little buddy. I hope you enjoyed your time with us, and I'll always keep you in my heart. 🖤

... (truncated)

Changelog

Sourced from github.com/opencontainers/umoci's changelog.

[0.6.0] - 2025-10-15

Please mind the gap between the train and the platform.

This update to umoci includes support for v1.1.1 of the OCI image specification. For the most part, this mostly involves supporting reading new features added to the specification (such as embedded-data descriptors and subject references used by OCI artifact images), but at the moment umoci does not yet support creating images utilising these features.

In addition, umoci also now supports generating config.json blobs that are compliant with v1.2.1 of the OCI runtime specification. Note that we do not explicitly use any of the newer features, this is mostly a quality-of-life update to move away from our ancient pinned version of the runtime-spec.

Breaking

  • github.com/opencontainers/umoci/oci/config/generate.Generator has had the following breaking API changes made to it:
    • The existing ConfigExposedPorts and ConfigVolumes methods now return a sorted []string instead of a map.
    • The (Set)OS and (Set)Architecture methods have been renamed to have a Platform prefix (to match image-spec v1.1's organisational changes). They now read as (Set)PlatformOS and (Set)PlatformArchitecture respectively.

Added

  • umoci stat now includes information about the manifest and configuration of the image, both in the regular and JSON-formatted outputs.

  • umoci now has [SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH][source-date-epoch] support, to attempt to make it easier to create reproducible images. Our behaviour is modelled after tar --clamp-mtime, meaning that SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH will only be used to modify the timestamps of files newer than SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH.

    As umoci repack works based on diffs, this also means that only files that were modified (and will thus be usually be included in the new layer) will have their timestamps rewritten.

    --history.created and umoci config --created will also now default to SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH (if set).

    With this change, umoci should be fairly compliant with reproducible builds. Please let us know if you find any other problematic areas in umoci (we are investigating some other possible causes of instability such as Go map iteration).

  • In order to avoid the need for a [patched gomtree package][obs-gomtree] that supports rootless mode, umoci now has a umoci raw mtree-validate subcommand that implements the key gomtree validate features we need for our integration tests.

    Note that this subcommand is not intended for wider use outside of our tests (and it is hidden from the help pages for a reason). Most users are probably

title: Username is changed inside Apptainer container
body:
### Version of Apptainer

What version of Apptainer (or Singularity) are you using? Run

    apptainer version 1.4.5

### Expected behavior

When running in userns mode as user `me`, both `id` and `echo $USER` point to `me` user.

### Actual behavior

I start a container off of `docker://ubuntu:noble` . This OCI image [contains user `ubuntu` with UID 1000](https://askubuntu.com/questions/1513927/ubuntu-24-04-docker-images-now-includes-user-ubuntu-with-uid-gid-1000).

My host has user `me` with UID 1000.

When I go into the image, I get to this situation:

```
$ echo $USER
me
$ id
uid=1000(ubuntu) gid=1000(ubuntu) groups=1000(ubuntu),65534(nogroup)
$ id $USER
id: ’me’: no such user
```

### Steps to reproduce this behavior

    apptainer run docker://ubuntu:noble

### What OS/distro are you running

```sh
$ cat /etc/os-release
NAME="Ubuntu"
VERSION="20.04.6 LTS (Focal Fossa)"
ID=ubuntu
ID_LIKE=debian
PRETTY_NAME="Ubuntu 20.04.6 LTS"
VERSION_ID="20.04"
HOME_URL="https://www.ubuntu.com/"
SUPPORT_URL="https://help.ubuntu.com/"
BUG_REPORT_URL="https://bugs.launchpad.net/ubuntu/"
PRIVACY_POLICY_URL="https://www.ubuntu.com/legal/terms-and-policies/privacy-policy"
VERSION_CODENAME=focal
UBUNTU_CODENAME=focal
```

### How did you install Apptainer

Official PPA

### Other comments

If I understand https://github.com/vzokay/apptainer/blob/552e81a45df7904e18fe76f739d02e48a584fc79/internal/pkg/util/fs/files/passwd.go#L91 and https://github.com/apptainer/apptainer/pull/1561 correctly, this is kind of intended behavior.

Yet I find it highly confusing.

What is the reason why username and group is not overwritten in the image? Is it possible to fix this? I could send the PR, but I don't know if it's reasonable or not.

title: No config media type or layer media type for non-sif artifacts in oras
body:
When pushing a sif image as oras, there are some custom media types:

`application/vnd.sylabs.sif.config.v1+json`
`application/vnd.sylabs.sif.layer.v1.sif`

But there are no media types registered for squashfs, that can be used...

Note: All media types must have a vendor, and may be registered with IANA

----

There is also a new "artifact type" in 1.1, but it is NOT supported by go-containerregistry

See https://github.com/opencontainers/artifacts/blob/main/artifact-authors.md

* https://github.com/google/go-containerregistry/issues/1537

* https://github.com/google/go-containerregistry/issues/1832

Currently the squashfs OCI artifacts are pushed with empty config and generic binary:

`application/vnd.unknown.config.v1+json`
`application/octet-stream`

It works OK with the registries I have tested so far, but the artifacts are anonymous...

* https://github.com/apptainer/apptainer/pull/3356

i.e. there is nothing (but the file magic) saying they are squashfs

The URI gives no hints about the file name, just like OCI images.

Updates `github.com/opencontainers/umoci` from 0.4.7 to 0.6.0
Release notes

Sourced from github.com/opencontainers/umoci's releases.

umoci 0.5.1 -- "🖤 Yuki (2021-2025)"

This is a fairly minor update to umoci, containing a few bugfixes for some potential issues, as well as finally removing the requirement for oci-image-tool validation. We still do not support the latest image-spec release, but decoupling for oci-image-tool is a very important first step.

Fixed

  • For images with an empty index.json, umoci will no longer incorrectly set the manifests entry to null (which was technically a violation of the specification, though such images cannot be pushed or interacted with outside of umoci).
  • Based on some recent developments in the image-spec, umoci will now produce an error if it encounters descriptors with a negative size (this was a potential DoS vector previously) as well as a theoretical attack where an attacker would endlessly write to a blob (this would not be generally exploitable for images with descriptors).

Changed

  • We now use go:embed to fill the version information of umoci --version, allowing for users to get a reasonable binary with go install. However, we still recommend using our official binaries, using distribution binaries, or building from source with make.

  • Rather than using oci-image-tool validate for validating images in our tests, we now make use of some hand-written smoke tests as well as the jq-based validators maintained in docker-library/meta-scripts.

    This is intended to act as a stop-gap until umoci validate is implemented (and after that, we may choose to keep the jq-based validators as a double-check that our own validators are working correctly).

Thanks to the following contributors who made this release possible:

  • Adam Korcz Adam@adalogics.com
  • Akhil Mohan akhilerm@gmail.com
  • Aleksa Sarai cyphar@cyphar.com

This release is dedicated to our cat Yuki who sadly passed away on Friday. Most of the code I've written in the past four years was written with him purring away on my chest, and he was the most loving cat I've ever met. Rest in peace, little buddy. I hope you enjoyed your time with us, and I'll always keep you in my heart. 🖤

Changelog

Sourced from github.com/opencontainers/umoci's changelog.

[0.6.0] - 2025-10-15

Please mind the gap between the train and the platform.

This update to umoci includes support for v1.1.1 of the OCI image specification. For the most part, this mostly involves supporting reading new features added to the specification (such as embedded-data descriptors and subject references used by OCI artifact images), but at the moment umoci does not yet support creating images utilising these features.

In addition, umoci also now supports generating config.json blobs that are compliant with v1.2.1 of the OCI runtime specification. Note that we do not explicitly use any of the newer features, this is mostly a quality-of-life update to move away from our ancient pinned version of the runtime-spec.

Breaking

  • github.com/opencontainers/umoci/oci/config/generate.Generator has had the following breaking API changes made to it:
    • The existing ConfigExposedPorts and ConfigVolumes methods now return a sorted []string instead of a map.
    • The (Set)OS and (Set)Architecture methods have been renamed to have a Platform prefix (to match image-spec v1.1's organisational changes). They now read as (Set)PlatformOS and (Set)PlatformArchitecture respectively.

Added

  • umoci stat now includes information about the manifest and configuration of the image, both in the regular and JSON-formatted outputs.

  • umoci now has [SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH][source-date-epoch] support, to attempt to make it easier to create reproducible images. Our behaviour is modelled after tar --clamp-mtime, meaning that SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH will only be used to modify the timestamps of files newer than SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH.

    As umoci repack works based on diffs, this also means that only files that were modified (and will thus be usually be included in the new layer) will have their timestamps rewritten.

    --history.created and umoci config --created will also now default to SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH (if set).

    With this change, umoci should be fairly compliant with reproducible builds. Please let us know if you find any other problematic areas in umoci (we are investigating some other possible causes of instability such as Go map iteration).

  • In order to avoid the need for a [patched gomtree package][obs-gomtree] that supports rootless mode, umoci now has a umoci raw mtree-validate subcommand that implements the key gomtree validate features we need for our integration tests.

    Note that this subcommand is not intended for wider use outside of our tests (and it is hidden from the help pages for a reason). Most users are probably

title: fusermount3 issue on RHEL 8
body:
### Version of Apptainer
`1.4.5-2.el8`

### Expected behavior
Ubuntu runs on Apptainer.

### Actual behavior
```
INFO:    A fusermount error may indicate that the kernel is too old
INFO:    The --unsquash option may work around it
FATAL:   container creation failed: image driver mount failure: image driver squashfuse_ll instance exited with error: squashfuse_ll exited: fusermount3: mountpoint /dev/fuse is not a directory or a regular file
```

### Steps to reproduce this behavior

```sh
apptainer run ubuntu_latest.sif
```

### What OS/distro are you running

```sh
$ cat /etc/os-release
NAME="Red Hat Enterprise Linux"
VERSION="8.4 (Ootpa)"
ID="rhel"
ID_LIKE="fedora"
VERSION_ID="8.4"
PLATFORM_ID="platform:el8"
PRETTY_NAME="Red Hat Enterprise Linux 8.4 (Ootpa)"
ANSI_COLOR="0;31"
CPE_NAME="cpe:/o:redhat:enterprise_linux:8.4:GA"
HOME_URL="https://www.redhat.com/"
DOCUMENTATION_URL="https://access.redhat.com/documentation/red_hat_enterprise_linux/8/"
BUG_REPORT_URL="https://bugzilla.redhat.com/"

REDHAT_BUGZILLA_PRODUCT="Red Hat Enterprise Linux 8"
REDHAT_BUGZILLA_PRODUCT_VERSION=8.4
REDHAT_SUPPORT_PRODUCT="Red Hat Enterprise Linux"
REDHAT_SUPPORT_PRODUCT_VERSION="8.4"
```

### How did you install Apptainer

```
$ dnf install apptainer
apptainer.x86_64                                   1.4.5-2.el8                                                  @epel
apptainer-suid.x86_64                              1.4.5-2.el8                                                  @epel
```

### Additional info

```sh
$ fuse-overlayfs --version
fuse-overlayfs: version 1.13-dev
FUSE library version 3.2.1
using FUSE kernel interface version 7.26
fusermount3 version: 3.2.1

$uname -srv
Linux 4.18.0-348.20.1.el8_5.x86_64 #1 SMP Tue Mar 8 12:56:54 EST 2022

$ ls -l /dev/fuse
crw-rw-rw- 1 root root 10, 229 Feb 16 01:10 /dev/fuse
```

According to https://apptainer.org/docs/admin/1.4/installation.html#system-requirements , I believe that our 4.18.0 kernel should be well supported. However on another Oracle Linux device running on UEK (5.15.0) things are going smoothly. I wonder if I am missing something else during the setup process, or if apptainer really require a more up-to-date linux kernel that RHEL8 does not have.

title: Fix FIPS support in EL builds
body: For [bugzilla 2437258](https://bugzilla.redhat.com/show_bug.cgi?id=2437258) the EPEL/Fedora packaging was updated to enable FIPS support.  Import that change to do `export GODEBUG=fips140=on` near the beginning of the %build step.

title: Add `{PRE|AP}PEND_LD_LIBRARY_PATH` support
body:
This adds support for `PREPEND_LD_LIBRARY_PATH` and `APPEND_LD_LIBRARY_PATH` environment variables.

One of the benefits is that this gives a way to go back to the previous behavior from before #3293 of searching `/.singularity.d/libs` before a container's default library paths.

Updates `github.com/opencontainers/umoci` from 0.4.7 to 0.6.0
Release notes

Sourced from github.com/opencontainers/umoci's releases.

umoci 0.5.1 -- "🖤 Yuki (2021-2025)"

This is a fairly minor update to umoci, containing a few bugfixes for some potential issues, as well as finally removing the requirement for oci-image-tool validation. We still do not support the latest image-spec release, but decoupling for oci-image-tool is a very important first step.

Fixed

  • For images with an empty index.json, umoci will no longer incorrectly set the manifests entry to null (which was technically a violation of the specification, though such images cannot be pushed or interacted with outside of umoci).
  • Based on some recent developments in the image-spec, umoci will now produce an error if it encounters descriptors with a negative size (this was a potential DoS vector previously) as well as a theoretical attack where an attacker would endlessly write to a blob (this would not be generally exploitable for images with descriptors).

Changed

  • We now use go:embed to fill the version information of umoci --version, allowing for users to get a reasonable binary with go install. However, we still recommend using our official binaries, using distribution binaries, or building from source with make.

  • Rather than using oci-image-tool validate for validating images in our tests, we now make use of some hand-written smoke tests as well as the jq-based validators maintained in docker-library/meta-scripts.

    This is intended to act as a stop-gap until umoci validate is implemented (and after that, we may choose to keep the jq-based validators as a double-check that our own validators are working correctly).

Thanks to the following contributors who made this release possible:

  • Adam Korcz Adam@adalogics.com
  • Akhil Mohan akhilerm@gmail.com
  • Aleksa Sarai cyphar@cyphar.com

This release is dedicated to our cat Yuki who sadly passed away on Friday. Most of the code I've written in the past four years was written with him purring away on my chest, and he was the most loving cat I've ever met. Rest in peace, little buddy. I hope you enjoyed your time with us, and I'll always keep you in my heart. 🖤

Please mind the gap between the train and the platform.

This update to umoci includes support for v1.1.1 of the OCI image specification. For the most part, this mostly involves supporting reading new features added to the specification (such as embedded-data descriptors and subject references used by OCI artifact images), but at the moment umoci does not yet support creating images utilising these features.

In addition, umoci also now supports generating config.json blobs that are compliant with v1.2.1 of the OCI runtime specification. Note that we do not explicitly use any of the newer features, this is mostly a quality-of-life update to move away from our ancient pinned version of the runtime-spec.

Breaking

  • github.com/opencontainers/umoci/oci/config/generate.Generator has had the following breaking API changes made to it:
    • The existing ConfigExposedPorts and ConfigVolumes methods now return a sorted []string instead of a map.
    • The (Set)OS and (Set)Architecture methods have been renamed to have a Platform prefix (to match image-spec v1.1's organisational changes). They now read as (Set)PlatformOS and (Set)PlatformArchitecture respectively.

Added

  • umoci stat now includes information about the manifest and configuration of the image, both in the regular and JSON-formatted outputs.

  • umoci now has [SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH][source-date-epoch] support, to attempt to make it easier to create reproducible images. Our behaviour is modelled after tar --clamp-mtime, meaning that SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH will only be used to modify the timestamps of files newer than SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH.

    As umoci repack works based on diffs, this also means that only files that were modified (and will thus be usually be included in the new layer) will have their timestamps rewritten.

    --history.created and umoci config --created will also now default to SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH (if set).

    With this change, umoci should be fairly compliant with reproducible builds. Please let us know if you find any other problematic areas in umoci (we are investigating some other possible causes of instability such as Go map iteration).

  • In order to avoid the need for a [patched gomtree package][obs-gomtree] that supports rootless mode, umoci now has a umoci raw mtree-validate subcommand that implements the key gomtree validate features we need for our integration tests.

    Note that this subcommand is not intended for wider use outside of our tests (and it is hidden from the help pages for a reason). Most users are probably

This is the first release of the 1.4.z release branch of runc. It contains a few fixes for issues found in 1.4.0-rc.3. This version of runc supports runtime-spec v1.3 (see [docs/spec-conformance.md][] for the few features that are still missing).

This is the second release of runc following our new release and support policy (see [RELEASES.md][] for more details). This means that, as of this release:

  • The runc 1.2.z release branch will now only receive high severity CVE fixes, and will no longer be supported in less than 6 months (end of April 2026).
  • The runc 1.3.z release branch will now only receive security and "significant" bugfixes.
  • Users are encouraged to plan migrating to runc 1.4.0 as soon as possible.
  • Despite this release being delayed by a month, users should still expect a runc 1.5.0 release in late April 2026.
