title: Prepare for 1.4.2 release
Add generation of debugsource rpms
body:
This updates the rpm spec and the Makefile to generate useful `debugsource` rpms.  It also cleans up some unnecessary go build options and adds the use of `GO_GCFLAGS` so when debug options are set they actually get used.

There turned out to be multiple impediments to generating the debugsource rpms.  The ones that I confirmed were:
1. The missing `-ldflags="-linkmode=external` build option resulted in no go sources recognized.
2. The use of `$CGO_CFLAGS` instead of `$CGO_CPPFLAGS` resulted in no go sources recognized.
3. The `-trimpath` exported in `$GOFLAGS` resulted in no go sources recognized.  On the other hand this option is needed for compiling plugins, so this is removed only when building an rpm.  Plugins aren't useful with rpms anyway because they have to be compiled in the same source directory as the binaries were compiled in.
4. We deliberately disabled generation of the debugsource rpms because the above problems resulted in zero source files and caused it to fail, even though later on when we added bundled dependencies sources from them would have made made the debugsource rpms be successfully created, but only with those sources and not go sources.

Since it's so easy to stop including the go sources, I added a line to the ci check to make sure there's at least one included.

title: Building container fails at configuring openssh-client - using subuid/subgid
body:
### Version of Apptainer

What version of Apptainer (or Singularity) are you using? Run

```
$ apptainer version
1.4.1
```

<!-- please include command-line output in a code block -->

### Expected behavior

Build an Nvidia/CUDA container from a Docker bootstrap image:

```
Bootstrap: docker
From: nvidia/cuda:11.8.0-devel-ubuntu20.04
 
%post
    # Prevent interactive prompts
    export DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive

    # Update & install only necessary packages
    apt-get update
	apt-get install -y openssh-client
	apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends python3 python3-pip libopenmpi-dev openmpi-bin
	
    # Clean up APT cache to save space
    apt-get clean && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/* /tmp/* /var/tmp/*

    # Install only required Python packages
    pip3 install --no-cache-dir numpy
 
%environment
    export PATH=/usr/bin:$PATH
    export LD_LIBRARY_PATH=/usr/lib:$LD_LIBRARY_PATH
```

Run with:

```
$ apptainer build container.sif container.def
```

### Actual behavior

The image components are downloaded, the OCI image extracted and the post-installation commands are run:

```
$ apptainer build container.sif container.def
INFO:    Starting build...
INFO:    Fetching OCI image...
83.9KiB / 83.9KiB [=====================================================================================================================================] 100 % 0.0 b/s 0s
26.2MiB / 26.2MiB [=====================================================================================================================================] 100 % 0.0 b/s 0s
2.3GiB / 2.3GiB [=======================================================================================================================================] 100 % 0.0 b/s 0s
1.3GiB / 1.3GiB [=======================================================================================================================================] 100 % 0.0 b/s 0s
7.6MiB / 7.6MiB [=======================================================================================================================================] 100 % 0.0 b/s 0s
53.6MiB / 53.6MiB [=====================================================================================================================================] 100 % 0.0 b/s 0s
INFO:    Extracting OCI image...
INFO:    Inserting Apptainer configuration...
INFO:    Running post scriptlet
+ export DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive
+ apt-get update
```

The post install commands try to update several components (python, openmpi, openssh-client) and fail after attempting to configure openssh-client.

```
Setting up openssh-client (1:8.2p1-4ubuntu0.13) ...
chgrp: changing group of '/usr/bin/ssh-agent': Operation not permitted
dpkg: error processing package openssh-client (--configure):
 installed openssh-client package post-installation script subprocess returned error exit status 1
Setting up libxext6:amd64 (2:1.3.4-0ubuntu1) ...
Setting up xauth (1:1.1-0ubuntu1) ...
Processing triggers for libc-bin (2.31-0ubuntu9.12) ...
Errors were encountered while processing:
 openssh-client
W: chown to _apt:root of directory /var/cache/apt/archives/partial failed - SetupAPTPartialDirectory (1: Operation not permitted)
W: chown to _apt:root of directory /var/lib/apt/lists/auxfiles failed - SetupAPTPartialDirectory (1: Operation not permitted)
W: Download is performed unsandboxed as root as file '/var/cache/apt/archives/partial/libbsd0_0.10.0-1_amd64.deb' couldn't be accessed by user '_apt'. - pkgAcquire::Run (13: Permission denied)
W: chown to root:adm of file /var/log/apt/term.log failed - OpenLog (1: Operation not permitted)
E: Sub-process /usr/bin/dpkg returned an error code (1)
FATAL:   While performing build: while running engine: while running %post section: exit status 100
```

Image build process then terminates.

User namespaces are enabled, and my account has a unique address range in both /etc/subuid and /etc/subgid:

```
$ grep my_name /etc/sub*
/etc/subgid:my_name:1100000:65536
/etc/subuid:my_name:1100000:65536
```

Apptainer is *not* installed setuid and is using `libexec/bin/starter`

The newuidmap and newgidmap binaries are *not* setuid:

```
$ ls -l /usr/bin/new*map
-rwxr-xr-x 1 root root 43136 Nov  5  2024 /usr/bin/newgidmap
-rwxr-xr-x 1 root root 39016 Nov  5  2024 /usr/bin/newuidmap
```

### Steps to reproduce this behavior

Use the container definition listed above. Add entry to /etc/subuid and /etc/subgid for the current user, ensure current user is not in sudoers.

### What OS/distro are you running

We are running Apptainer on the head nodes of a large Slurm cluster which is currently being implemented. The intention is to allow (unprivileged) users to create images on the head nodes before launching those containers on compute resources. Hence the the use of subuid and subgid.

```
NAME="Red Hat Enterprise Linux"
VERSION="9.4 (Plow)"
ID="rhel"
ID_LIKE="fedora"
VERSION_ID="9.4"
PLATFORM_ID="platform:el9"
PRETTY_NAME="Red Hat Enterprise Linux 9.4 (Plow)"
ANSI_COLOR="0;31"
LOGO="fedora-logo-icon"
CPE_NAME="cpe:/o:redhat:enterprise_linux:9::baseos"
HOME_URL="https://www.redhat.com/"
DOCUMENTATION_URL="https://access.redhat.com/documentation/en-us/red_hat_enterprise_linux/9"
BUG_REPORT_URL="https://issues.redhat.com/"

REDHAT_BUGZILLA_PRODUCT="Red Hat Enterprise Linux 9"
REDHAT_BUGZILLA_PRODUCT_VERSION=9.4
REDHAT_SUPPORT_PRODUCT="Red Hat Enterprise Linux"
REDHAT_SUPPORT_PRODUCT_VERSION="9.4"
```

### How did you install Apptainer

I believe our hardware vendor did the install from a current easybuild community recipe.

I've seen a few references to openssh-client being problematic, but this appeared to relate to not using user namespaces, which to the best of my knowledge is in place and working.

What I'm not 100% sure of is the combination of the _apptainer_, _starter_ and _newuidmap_ and _newgidmap_ binaries needing to be setuid, the value of the "use setuid" config parameter, and/or if the starter wrapper needs to be compiled with the --use-uidmap flag.

Our main user filestore is a Lustre mount - so the above is happening in that location. Access to local drives is extremely limited.

title: `--containall` does not isolate unix domain sockets
body:
Apptainer version 1.4.0-1.el9

It seems that `--containall` doesn't isolate unix domain sockets from the host. Is this the expected behavior? I discovered this when I was trying to start a virtual X server in the container via `Xvfb`, but it kept complaining that a server is already running (which turned out to be an X server running on the host).

__Minimal demo__:
```
$ nc -lU /tmp/leaky.sock &         # Create a unix domain socket
$ apptainer build ubuntu.sif docker://ubuntu
$ apptainer shell --containall --cleanenv --no-mount hostfs --fakeroot ubuntu.sif
Apptainer> grep leaky /proc/net/unix
0000000000000000: 00000002 00000000 00010000 0001 01 489641041 /tmp/leaky.sock
```

In general, what options should we use to achieve maximum isolation from the host? Even with `--containall`, `--cleanenv`, `--no-mount hostfs`, Apptainer still attempts to bind certain things like `/etc/localtime` from the host into the container. I wonder what else is Apptainer doing behind the scenes that might break reproducibility (relevant discussion: #64)


### What OS/distro are you running

AlmaLinux 9.5 (RHEL compatible)

title: DRAFT: two approaches in one: Debian packaging with and without network
body:
## Description of the Pull Request (PR):

This is the culmination of my investigations and coding efforts in #3070, and meant to replace it as another "eternal draft" (once again I forgot to sign off my commit..)

- Fixes #3069

Two approaches in one:
(1) `prepare-withnetwork` will prepare the debian/ tree for building with networking **enabled** (`pbuilder` option `--use-network yes`), by providing suitable `control`, `rules` and (empty) `source/include-binaries`.
(2) `prepare-withoutnetwork` will prepare the debian/ tree for building with networking **disabled** (`pbuilder` without `--use-network`), by providing suitable `control`, `rules` and `source/include-binaries`. Tarballs for go and dependencies must be provided!

Both approaches have been tested on amd64 Ubuntu 24.04 ("Noble").
Make sure to provide a `go` version >= 1.20.6!

Again, comment, ignore, steal or reject :)

Release notes

Sourced from mvdan.cc/sh/v3's releases.

v3.12.0

  • The mvdan-sh JS package is discontinued in favor of sh-syntax - #1145
  • cmd/shfmt
    • Support the "simplify" and "minify" flags via EditorConfig - #819
    • --simplify and --minify are now formatting options, disabling the use of EditorConfig
    • Do not allow --write to replace non-regular files - #843
  • interp
    • Add IsBuiltin to check if a command name is a shell built-in - #1164
    • Add HandlerContext.Builtin to allow ExecHandlerFunc to call built-ins
    • Initial support for $! and wait PID - #221
    • Return non-fatal ExecHandlerFunc errors via the Runner.Run API
    • Add HandlerContext.Pos to provide handlers with source positions
    • Deprecate NewExitStatus and IsExitStatus in favor of ExitStatus
    • Fix wait to always return the status of the last given job
    • Copy all env vars for background subshells to avoid data races
    • Support reading random numbers via $RANDOM and $SRANDOM
    • Set $BASH_REMATCH when matching regular expressions via =~
    • Support modifying local vars from the parent calling function
  • expand
    • Adjust which backslash sequences are expanded in here-docs - #1138
    • Tweak tilde expansions to match Bash semantics
  • pattern
    • Remove the flawed and broken Braces mode; use syntax.SplitBraces instead
    • Tweak ** to only act as "globstar" when alone as a path element - #1149
    • Tweak * and ** to not match leading dots in basenames
    • Add a NoGlobStar mode to match the POSIX semantics
  • fileutil
    • Treat all non-regular files as definitely not shell scripts - #1089

Consider becoming a sponsor if you benefit from the work that went into this release!

Binaries built on go version go1.24.4 linux/amd64 with:

CGO_ENABLED=0 go build -trimpath -ldflags="-w -s -X=main.version=v3.12.0"

v3.11.0

This release drops support for Go 1.22 and includes many enhancements.

  • cmd/shfmt
    • Support -l=0 and -f=0 to split filenames with null bytes - #1096
  • syntax
    • New iterator API: Parser.WordsSeq
    • Fix Parser.Incomplete and IsIncomplete to work well with Parser.Words - #937
    • Initial support for parsing incomplete shell via RecoverErrors
    • Expand LangError to include which language was used when parsing
  • interp

This pulls in sylabs PR
* sylabs/singularity#3533

The original PR description was:
> Bump Go version used in CI to latest 1.24.0
> 
> Clarify requirement for >=1.23.4
> 
> Bump golangci-lint and fix much newly reported lint.
> 
> Most of the lint is related to the Go `os.XXX` routines giving `int` uid/gid/modes, while lower level calls, 3rd party things we call, and structs we use, use `uint32` - which is actually what uid/gid are on Linux. Singularity code has a mix of using `int` and `uint32` to bridge between the worlds.
> 
> Unfortunately dependencies are pulling in a patch version above 1.23.0 at this time.

_Note: in the original PR, `golangci-lint` version was initially bumped to 1.64.5, then later changed to 1.64. This was skipped with the commit https://github.com/apptainer/apptainer/commit/09af41852c0af67bdb467e983faa46ec9a2e0841 ._

title: Download failure of apptainer v1.4.1
body:
**Describe the problem**
The module checksum for v1.4.1 in this repository does not match the checksum recorded in Go's checksum database. This might indicate that the module has been retagged or the source code has been modified after the initial release.

When trying to download the module directly from github, the following error occurs:
```
$ GOPROXY=direct go get github.com/apptainer/apptainer@v1.4.1
go: downloading github.com/apptainer/apptainer v1.4.1
go: github.com/apptainer/apptainer@v1.4.1: verifying module: checksum mismatch
        downloaded: h1:S4PGY1ZYbgG/fhx3Q/Y3pE1PhmKja6kyflUJebUXHWo=
        sum.golang.org: h1:rkify3P3kwgkAbD1sEI04ZOPvatROgSH/wqr8EFGwZY=

SECURITY ERROR
This download does NOT match the one reported by the checksum server.
The bits may have been replaced on the origin server, or an attacker may
have intercepted the download attempt.

For more information, see 'go help module-auth'
```

**Possible causes**
- The tag  was deleted and recreated pointing to different commits
- Source code was modified after the tag was created
- Repository was force-pushed affecting the tagged commit
- 
**Proposed solution**
- If legitimate, release a new version to resolve the issue
- Avoid retagging existing versions to maintain checksum integrity

title: New PID namespace option run new process which has the same PGID as the parent process.
body:
Dear Apptainer developers.

In the system we use, "an agent" runs the analytics program with the 'apptainer run -C' option for several jobs. 

However, we have noticed that in certain cases, the program sends a SIGKILL signal to kill its own child process, but due to a bug, it sometimes executes "kill -9 0" (SIGKILL to the same PGID processes).

The problem is that when that signal is raised, not only is the child process killed, but also the parent process, "the agent", receives the SIGKILL. 

We believe this is because the agent and the child process have the same PGID.

In the case of podman, PID namespace isolation is the default, so the newly created process has a different PGID than the agent, and this process does not receive all signals from the child.

I'm posting this on the GitHub issue page, as I've been told that this topic needs more discussion on the Google discussion page.

Could you add a PID namespace isolation option to Apptainer, along with the new PID namespace option?

The existing option has the advantage of having the same PGIDs, allowing us to concatenate structures with pstree or a similar tool. However, the nature of our job requires isolation to minimize issues.

Test Code: [pid_namespace_test](https://github.com/geonmo/pid_namespace_test)

title: Apptainer not functional on Arch - version GLIBC_* not found
body:
Hi

I built an [OpenRV](https://github.com/AcademySoftwareFoundation/OpenRV) Apptainer on Rocky 9 which works fine on Rocky 9 (RHEL) itself as well as Ubuntu 22.04 (Debian).

Run command:
```
$ apptainer exec --nv --bind /run/user/$UID OpenRV.sif /opt/OpenRV/bin/rv -version
3.0.0
```

Apptainer version on Rocky:
```
$ apptainer --version
apptainer version 1.4.1-1.el9
```

However, the very same `sif` throws an error on Manjaro (Arch):
(I tried in both standard shell `zsh` and `bash`)
```
$ apptainer exec --nv --bind /run/user/$UID OpenRV.sif /opt/OpenRV/bin/rv -version
/opt/OpenRV/bin/rv.bin: /opt/OpenRV/lib/libc.so.6: version `GLIBC_ABI_DT_RELR' not found (required by /.singularity.d/libs/libGLX.so.0)
/opt/OpenRV/bin/rv.bin: /opt/OpenRV/lib/libc.so.6: version `GLIBC_2.38' not found (required by /.singularity.d/libs/libGLX.so.0)
/opt/OpenRV/bin/rv.bin: /opt/OpenRV/lib/libc.so.6: version `GLIBC_ABI_DT_RELR' not found (required by /.singularity.d/libs/libOpenGL.so.0)
/opt/OpenRV/bin/rv.bin: /opt/OpenRV/lib/libc.so.6: version `GLIBC_ABI_DT_RELR' not found (required by /.singularity.d/libs/libGL.so.1)
/opt/OpenRV/bin/rv.bin: /opt/OpenRV/lib/libc.so.6: version `GLIBC_ABI_DT_RELR' not found (required by /.singularity.d/libs/libGLdispatch.so.0)
/opt/OpenRV/bin/rv.bin: /opt/OpenRV/lib/libc.so.6: version `GLIBC_2.38' not found (required by /.singularity.d/libs/libGLdispatch.so.0)
```

Apptainer version on Manjaro:
```
$ apptainer --version
apptainer version 1.4.0
```

I must admit I'm not familiar with the scope of how cross platform compatible Apptainers generally are and I'm aware of the different versions - `1.4.0` is the latest available on the `extra` Arch repository.

Any chance of getting this Apptainer to play nicely on my targeted platforms?

Cheers,
Michael

Changelog

Sourced from github.com/opencontainers/runc's changelog.

[1.2.6] - 2025-03-17

Hasta la victoria, siempre.

Fixed

  • Fix a stall issue that would happen if setting O_CLOEXEC with CloseExecFrom failed (#4647).
  • runc now properly handles joining time namespaces (such as with runc exec). Previously we would attempt to set the time offsets when joining, which would fail. (#4635, #4649)
  • Handle EINTR retries correctly for socket-related direct golang.org/x/sys/unix system calls. (#4650)
  • We no longer use F_SEAL_FUTURE_WRITE when sealing the runc binary, as it turns out this had some unfortunate bugs in older kernel versions and was never necessary in the first place. (#4651, #4640)

Removed

  • Remove Fexecve helper from libcontainer/system. Runc 1.2.1 removed runc-dmz, but we forgot to remove this helper added only for that. (#4646)

Changed

  • Use Go 1.23 for official builds, run CI with Go 1.24 and drop Ubuntu 20.04 from CI. We need to drop Ubuntu 20.04 from CI because Github Actions announced it's already deprecated and it will be discontinued soon. (#4648)

Create automated builds for ubuntu PPA


### This fixes or addresses the following GitHub issues:

 - Fixes #2869


#### Before submitting a PR, make sure you have done the following:

- [ ] Read the [Guidelines for Contributing](https://github.com/apptainer/apptainer/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md), and this PR conforms to the stated requirements.
- [ ] Make sure all commits are signed-off with `git commit -s`, see the [Guidelines for Contributing](https://github.com/apptainer/apptainer/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
- [ ] Added changes to the [CHANGELOG](https://github.com/apptainer/apptainer/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md), if necessary according to the [Guidelines for Contributing](https://github.com/apptainer/apptainer/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
- [ ] Added tests to validate this PR, linted with `make check`  and tested this PR locally with a `make test`, and `make testall` if possible (see the [Guidelines for Contributing](https://github.com/apptainer/apptainer/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md)).
- [ ] Based this PR against the appropriate branch according to the [Guidelines for Contributing](https://github.com/apptainer/apptainer/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
- [ ] Added myself as a contributor to the [Contributors File](https://github.com/apptainer/apptainer/blob/main/CONTRIBUTORS.md).

## Description:

The `workflow_dispatch` is only triggered on `main` branch. so it'll be unavailable on the actions tab until this PR gets merged.

![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/8105f38e-4ef5-4b6a-bef9-db2a09fff2ce)

1. `apptaienr published tag (e.g. 1.4.1)` => Fill in the already published apptainer tag (e.g. 1.4.1, this tag is used for downloading the apptainer-{tag}.tar.gz file from github)
2. `publish ppa, ppa:apptainer/ppa => prod, others => test` => Choose the published ppa. (we need to set the proper gpg private_key and private_key_passphrase on the github settings, as well as the Ubuntu PPA launchpad settings)
3. `publish revision number (default: 1)` => Publish revision number, no need to change unless previous builds failed, then we need to change the revision number and the following `new_tag` to overwrite the `.orig.tar.gz` file
4. `publish tag, this will rename the published apptainer tag (e.g. 1.4.1-unofficial)` => Use together with the above field, if previous builds failed and you need to test changes. (can write anything, this would change the name of the .orig.tar.gz file). 

## Attention:
Following file changes:
```
scripts/ci-deb-bulld-test
dist/debian/changelog
dist/debian/rules
```
and other build-related file changes might corrupt the PPA builds, as the script heavily modifies existing builds scripts and changes might result in the corruption.

title: Conda activate returns CondaError with Apptainer container
body:
Hi! I encountered `CondaError` when I tried to create and activate a conda environment `tmp_env` inside an Apptainer container. This may be related to #2912.

The `.sif` file was created as follows:

I created `my_container.def`
```
Bootstrap: docker
From: ubuntu:22.04

%post
    apt-get -y update
    apt-get -y upgrade
    apt-get install -y build-essential \
        less man vim bzip2 curl wget git ca-certificates iputils-ping net-tools locales
    
    # timezone
    export DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive 
    export TZ=Asia/Tokyo
    apt-get install -y tzdata
    ln -fs /usr/share/zoneinfo/$TZ /etc/localtime
    dpkg-reconfigure --frontend noninteractive tzdata
    
    apt-get -y clean
    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

    locale-gen en_US.UTF-8
    update-locale LANG=en_US.UTF-8

    # PS1
    echo "export PS1=\"\[\e[0;32m\]Apptainer|\W> \[\e[m\]\"" >> /opt/init.sh

    # Install Miniforge
    wget https://github.com/conda-forge/miniforge/releases/latest/download/Miniforge3-Linux-x86_64.sh
    /bin/sh Miniforge3-Linux-x86_64.sh -bfp /opt/miniforge3
    rm Miniforge3-Linux-x86_64.sh

    /opt/miniforge3/bin/conda shell.bash hook > /opt/miniforge3/conda_init.sh
    . /opt/miniforge3/conda_init.sh

    echo ". /opt/miniforge3/conda_init.sh" >> /opt/init.sh

    conda update -y -n base -c defaults conda
    
    conda create -n tmp_env -y
    conda activate tmp_env
    conda install python -y
    
%runscript
    echo "Hello, Ubuntu. from runscript"

%startscript
    echo "Hello, Ubuntu. from startscript"

%environment
    . /opt/init.sh    

```

built `sif`  
```
apptainer build my_container.sif my_container.def
```

and entered the Apptainer shell  
```
apptainer shell my_container.sif
```

There were two envs and it seemed that the `base` env was active
```
(base) Apptainer|~> conda env list

# conda environments:
#
base                 * /opt/miniforge3
tmp_env                /opt/miniforge3/envs/tmp_env


(base) Apptainer|~> which python
/opt/miniforge3/bin/python
```

I tried to activate the other env and got an CondaError:
```
(base) Apptainer|~> conda activate tmp_env
CondaError: Run 'conda init' before 'conda activate'
```

This was solved by manually running
```
(base) Apptainer|~> eval "$(/opt/miniforge3/bin/conda shell.bash hook)"
(base) Apptainer|~> conda activate tmp_env
(tmp_env) Apptainer|~> 
```
after entering the shell.


So I inserted this block into `/opt/init.sh` or `/environment` hoping to make this take effect on entering the shell, which did not solve the problem. Is it possible to avoid the CondaError automatically? 

Thanks.



```
host: WSL version 2.5.9.0

$ cat /etc/os-release 
PRETTY_NAME="Debian GNU/Linux 12 (bookworm)"

$ apptainer --version
apptainer version 1.3.6
```

Bumps the opencontainers group with 1 update: [github.com/opencontainers/runc](https://github.com/opencontainers/runc). Updates `github.com/opencontainers/runc` from 1.2.5 to 1.2.6
Changelog

Sourced from github.com/opencontainers/runc's changelog.

[1.2.6] - 2025-03-17

Hasta la victoria, siempre.

Fixed

  • Fix a stall issue that would happen if setting O_CLOEXEC with CloseExecFrom failed (#4647).
  • runc now properly handles joining time namespaces (such as with runc exec). Previously we would attempt to set the time offsets when joining, which would fail. (#4635, #4649)
  • Handle EINTR retries correctly for socket-related direct golang.org/x/sys/unix system calls. (#4650)
  • We no longer use F_SEAL_FUTURE_WRITE when sealing the runc binary, as it turns out this had some unfortunate bugs in older kernel versions and was never necessary in the first place. (#4651, #4640)

Removed

  • Remove Fexecve helper from libcontainer/system. Runc 1.2.1 removed runc-dmz, but we forgot to remove this helper added only for that. (#4646)

Changed

  • Use Go 1.23 for official builds, run CI with Go 1.24 and drop Ubuntu 20.04 from CI. We need to drop Ubuntu 20.04 from CI because Github Actions announced it's already deprecated and it will be discontinued soon. (#4648)

Changelog

Sourced from github.com/opencontainers/runc's changelog.

[1.2.6] - 2025-03-17

Hasta la victoria, siempre.

Fixed

  • Fix a stall issue that would happen if setting O_CLOEXEC with CloseExecFrom failed (#4647).
  • runc now properly handles joining time namespaces (such as with runc exec). Previously we would attempt to set the time offsets when joining, which would fail. (#4635, #4649)
  • Handle EINTR retries correctly for socket-related direct golang.org/x/sys/unix system calls. (#4650)
  • We no longer use F_SEAL_FUTURE_WRITE when sealing the runc binary, as it turns out this had some unfortunate bugs in older kernel versions and was never necessary in the first place. (#4651, #4640)

Removed

  • Remove Fexecve helper from libcontainer/system. Runc 1.2.1 removed runc-dmz, but we forgot to remove this helper added only for that. (#4646)

Changed

  • Use Go 1.23 for official builds, run CI with Go 1.24 and drop Ubuntu 20.04 from CI. We need to drop Ubuntu 20.04 from CI because Github Actions announced it's already deprecated and it will be discontinued soon. (#4648)

  • Handle EINTR retries correctly for socket-related direct golang.org/x/sys/unix system calls. (#4650)
  • We no longer use F_SEAL_FUTURE_WRITE when sealing the runc binary, as it turns out this had some unfortunate bugs in older kernel versions and was never necessary in the first place. (#4651, #4640)

Removed

Changed

  • Use Go 1.23 for official builds, run CI with Go 1.24 and drop Ubuntu 20.04 from CI. We need to drop Ubuntu 20.04 from CI because Github Actions announced it's already deprecated and it will be discontinued soon. (#4648)

title: apptainer build fails if APPTAINER_TMPDIR points to directory with secondary group sticky bit writable
body:
We have a Rocky 8.10 box with apptainer-1.3.2-1.el8.x86_64 that has two local volumes as such:

```
# egrep '( /home |polgar)' /etc/mtab
/dev/nvme0n1p3 /home ext4 rw,seclabel,relatime 0 0
/dev/sda1 /local_mount/space/polgar/1 ext4 rw,seclabel,relatime 0 0
```

When APPTAINER_TMPDIR=/local_mount/space/polgar/1/apptainer/tmp  and one tries to build it fails with

```
$ apptainer build --fakeroot freesurfer-8.0.0.sif./fs-docker/freesurfer/Singularityfile.8.0.0
INFO:    Starting build...
Copying blob 9088cdb84e39 skipped: already exists
Copying config c79048e50f done   |
Writing manifest to image destination
FATAL:   While performing build: packer failed to pack: while unpacking tmpfs: error unpacking rootfs: mkdir rootfs: mkdir
/local_mount/space/polgar/1/apptainer/tmp/build-temp-2566909101/rootfs: no such file or directory

```
Looking at /local_mount/space/polgar/1/apptainer/tmp it is empty but definitely writable by the user. When not writable there is a totally different and clear error about nothing being able to create "build-temp-..." there.  Which is very confusing since when it is writable it still doesn't create it and gives the error above.

However, if we set APPTAINER_TMPDIR=/home/apptainer/tmp the build works fine!!!

```
$ apptainer build --fakeroot freesurfer-8.0.0.sif ./fs-docker/freesurfer/Singularityfile.8.0.0
INFO:    Starting build...
Copying blob 9088cdb84e39 skipped: already exists
Copying config c79048e50f done   |
Writing manifest to image destination
2025/06/09 21:38:14  info unpack layer: sha256:9088cdb84e397c480d4c5f1675d1aa6928c3e8b5b30c57b68a756d5d1fda4d80
INFO:    Running post scriptlet
+ dnf -y update
...
...
+ rm fs8_updates.sh
INFO:    Adding environment to container
INFO:    Creating SIF file...
INFO:    Build complete: freesurfer-8.0.0.sif
```

The only difference between the two volume I can think of (beside the name and one is SSD and the other HDD) is that /local_mount/space/polgar/1  is NFS exported and /home is not.  

APPTAINER_CACHEDIR works just fine on both volumes.

Changelog

Sourced from github.com/opencontainers/umoci's changelog.

[0.5.0] - 2025-05-21

A wizard is never late, Frodo Baggins. Nor is he early; he arrives precisely when he means to.

This version of umoci requires Go 1.23 to build.

Security

  • A security flaw was found in the OCI image-spec, where it is possible to cause a blob with one media-type to be interpreted as a different media-type. As umoci is not a registry nor does it handle signatures, this vulnerability had no real impact on umoci but for safety we implemented the now-recommended media-type embedding and verification. CVE-2021-41190

Breaking

  • The method of configuring the on-disk format and MapOptions in RepackOptions and UnpackOptions has been changed. The on-disk format is now represented with the OnDiskFormat interface, with DirRootfs and OverlayfsRootfs as possible options to use. MapOptions is now configured inside the OnDiskFormat setting, which will require callers to adjust their usage of the main umoci APIs. In particular, examples like

    unpackOptions := &layer.UnpackOptions{
    MapOptions: mapOptions,
    WhiteoutMode: layer.StandardOCIWhiteout, // or layer.OverlayFSWhiteout
}
err := layer.UnpackManifest(ctx, engineExt, bundle, manifest, unpackOptions)

    will have to now be written as

    unpackOptions := &layer.UnpackOptions{
    OnDiskFormat: layer.DirRootfs{ // or layer.OverlayfsRootfs
        MapOptions: mapOptions,
    },
}
err := layer.UnpackManifest(ctx, engineExt, bundle, manifest, unpackOptions)

    and similarly

    repackOptions := &layer.RepackOptions{
    MapOptions: mapOptions,
    TranslateOverlayWhiteouts: false, // or true
}
layerRdr, err := layer.GenerateLayer(path, deltas, repackOptions)

title: The `--contain` flag and `mount dev = minimal` do not mount `/dev/shm`
body:
According to the [apptainer.conf docs](https://apptainer.org/docs/admin/1.4/configfiles.html):

> `mount dev`: Should be set to “YES”, if you want Apptainer to automatically bind mount a complete `/dev` tree within the container. If set to minimal, then only `/dev/null`, `/dev/zero`, `/dev/random`, `/dev/urandom`, and `/dev/shm` will be included.

Further, `--contain` appears to be equivalent to `mount dev = minimal`, from the help text:

```
  -c, --contain                       use minimal /dev and empty other
                                      directories (e.g. /tmp and $HOME)
                                      instead of sharing filesystems from
                                      your host
```

and the comments in the default `apptainer.conf`:

```ini
# MOUNT DEV: [yes/no/minimal]
# DEFAULT: yes
# Should we automatically bind mount /dev within the container? If 'minimal'
# is chosen, then only 'null', 'zero', 'random', 'urandom', and 'shm' will
# be included (the same effect as the --contain options)
mount dev = yes
```

However, in practice, `/dev/shm` is only mounted from the host when `mount dev = yes` and `--contain` is not passed. All other permutations of `mount dev` and `--contain` (or not) result in a container-local `/dev/shm`.

Is this a discrepancy in the documentation or the implementation of `minimal`/`--contain`? What is the intended behavior with respect to `/dev/shm`?

Changelog

Sourced from github.com/opencontainers/runc's changelog.

[1.3.0] - 2025-04-30

Mr. President, we must not allow a mine shaft gap!

Fixed

  • Removed preemptive "full access to cgroups" warning when calling runc pause or runc unpause as an unprivileged user without --systemd-cgroups. Now the warning is only emitted if an actual permission error was encountered. (#4709)
  • Several fixes to our CI, mainly related to AlmaLinux and CRIU. (#4670, #4728, #4736)

Changed

  • In runc 1.2, we changed our mount behaviour to correctly handle clearing flags. However, the error messages we returned did not provide as much information to users about what clearing flags were conflicting with locked mount flags. We now provide more diagnostic information if there is an error when in the fallback path to handle locked mount flags. (#4734)
  • Upgrade our CI to use golangci-lint v2.0. (#4692)
  • runc version information is now filled in using //go:embed rather than being set through Makefile. This allows go install or other non-make builds to contain the correct version information. Note that make EXTRA_VERSION=... still works. (#418)
  • Remove exclude directives from our go.mod for broken cilium/ebpf versions. v0.17.3 resolved the issue we had, and exclude directives are incompatible with go install. (#4748)

[1.3.0-rc.2] - 2025-04-10

Eppur si muove.

Fixed

  • Use the container's /etc/passwd to set the HOME env var. After a refactor for 1.3, we were setting it reading the host's /etc/passwd file instead. (#4693, #4688)
  • Override HOME env var if it's set to the empty string. This fixes a regression after the same refactor for 1.3 and aligns the behavior with older versions of runc. (#4711)
  • Add time namespace to container config after checkpoint/restore. CRIU since version 3.14 uses a time namespace for checkpoint/restore, however it was not joining the time namespace in runc. (#4705)

[1.3.0-rc.1] - 2025-03-04

No tengo miedo al invierno, con tu recuerdo lleno de sol.

libcontainer API

Changelog

Sourced from github.com/opencontainers/umoci's changelog.

[0.5.0] - 2025-05-21

A wizard is never late, Frodo Baggins. Nor is he early; he arrives precisely when he means to.

This version of umoci requires Go 1.23 to build.

Security

  • A security flaw was found in the OCI image-spec, where it is possible to cause a blob with one media-type to be interpreted as a different media-type. As umoci is not a registry nor does it handle signatures, this vulnerability had no real impact on umoci but for safety we implemented the now-recommended media-type embedding and verification. CVE-2021-41190

Breaking

  • The method of configuring the on-disk format and MapOptions in RepackOptions and UnpackOptions has been changed. The on-disk format is now represented with the OnDiskFormat interface, with DirRootfs and OverlayfsRootfs as possible options to use. MapOptions is now configured inside the OnDiskFormat setting, which will require callers to adjust their usage of the main umoci APIs. In particular, examples like

    unpackOptions := &layer.UnpackOptions{
    MapOptions: mapOptions,
    WhiteoutMode: layer.StandardOCIWhiteout, // or layer.OverlayFSWhiteout
}
err := layer.UnpackManifest(ctx, engineExt, bundle, manifest, unpackOptions)

    will have to now be written as

    unpackOptions := &layer.UnpackOptions{
    OnDiskFormat: layer.DirRootfs{ // or layer.OverlayfsRootfs
        MapOptions: mapOptions,
    },
}
err := layer.UnpackManifest(ctx, engineExt, bundle, manifest, unpackOptions)

    and similarly

    repackOptions := &layer.RepackOptions{
    MapOptions: mapOptions,
    TranslateOverlayWhiteouts: false, // or true
}
layerRdr, err := layer.GenerateLayer(path, deltas, repackOptions)

Bumps the moby group with 2 updates: [github.com/docker/docker](https://github.com/docker/docker) and [github.com/docker/cli](https://github.com/docker/cli). Updates `github.com/docker/docker` from 27.5.1+incompatible to 28.2.1+incompatible
Release notes

Sourced from github.com/docker/docker's releases.

28.2.1

Packaging updates

  • Fix packaging regression in v28.2.0 which broke creating the docker group/user on fresh installations. docker-ce-packaging#1209

28.2.0

For a full list of pull requests and changes in this release, refer to the relevant GitHub milestones:

  • docker/cli, 28.2.0 milestone
  • moby/moby, 28.2.0 milestone
  • Deprecated and removed features, see Deprecated Features.
  • Changes to the Engine API, see API version history.

[!NOTE] RHEL packages are currently not available and will be released later.

New

  • Add {{.Platform}} as formatting option for docker ps to show the platform of the image the container is running. docker/cli#6042
  • Add support for relative parent paths (../) on bind mount sources when using docker run/create with -v/--volume or --mount type=bind options. docker/cli#4966
  • CDI is now enabled by default. moby/moby#49963
  • Show discovered CDI devices in docker info. docker/cli#6078
  • docker image rm: add --platform option to remove a variant from multi-platform images. docker/cli#6109
  • containerd image store: Initial BuildKit support for building Windows container images on Windows (requires an opt-in with DOCKER_BUILDKIT=1). moby/moby#49740

Bug fixes and enhancements

  • Add a new log option for fluentd log driver (fluentd-write-timeout), which enables specifying write timeouts for fluentd connections. moby/moby#49911
  • Add support for DOCKER_AUTH_CONFIG for the experimental --use-api-socket option. docker/cli#6019
  • Fix docker exec waiting for 10 seconds if a non-existing user or group was specified. moby/moby#49868
  • Fix docker swarm init ignoring cacert option of --external-ca. docker/cli#5995
  • Fix an issue where the CLI would not correctly save the configuration file (~/.docker/config.json) if it was a relative symbolic link. docker/cli#5282
  • Fix containers with --restart always policy using CDI devices failing to start on daemon restart. moby/moby#49990
  • Fix shell-completion to only complete some flags once, even though they can be set multiple times. docker/cli#6030
  • Fix the plugin does not implement PluginAddr interface error for Swarm CSI drivers. moby/moby#49961
  • Improve docker login error messages for invalid options. docker/cli#6036
  • Make sure the terminal state is restored if the CLI is forcefully terminated. docker/cli#6058
  • Update the default seccomp profile to match the libseccomp v2.6.0. The new syscalls are: listmount, statmount, lsm_get_self_attr, lsm_list_modules, lsm_set_self_attr, mseal, uretprobe, riscv_hwprobe, getxattrat, listxattrat, removexattrat, and setxattrat. This prevents containers from receiving EPERM errors when using them. moby/moby#50077
  • docker inspect: add shell completion, improve flag-description for --type and improve validation. docker/cli#6052
  • containerd image store: Enable BuildKit garbage collector by default. moby/moby#49899
  • containerd image store: Fix docker build not persisting overridden images as dangling. moby/moby#49702
  • containerd image store: Fix docker system df reporting a negative reclaimable space amount. moby/moby#49707
  • containerd image store: Fix duplicate PUT requests when pushing a multi-platform image. moby/moby#49949

Packaging updates

  • Drop Ubuntu 20.04 "Focal" packages as it reached end of life. docker/docker-ce-packaging#1200
  • Fix install location for RPM-based docker-ce man-pages. docker/docker-ce-packaging#1203

28.2.1

Packaging updates

  • Fix packaging regression in v28.2.0 which broke creating the docker group/user on fresh installations. docker-ce-packaging#1209

28.2.0

For a full list of pull requests and changes in this release, refer to the relevant GitHub milestones:

  • docker/cli, 28.2.0 milestone
  • moby/moby, 28.2.0 milestone
  • Deprecated and removed features, see Deprecated Features.
  • Changes to the Engine API, see API version history.

[!NOTE] RHEL packages are currently not available and will be released later.

New

  • Add {{.Platform}} as formatting option for docker ps to show the platform of the image the container is running. docker/cli#6042
  • Add support for relative parent paths (../) on bind mount sources when using docker run/create with -v/--volume or --mount type=bind options. docker/cli#4966
  • CDI is now enabled by default. moby/moby#49963
  • Show discovered CDI devices in docker info. docker/cli#6078
  • docker image rm: add --platform option to remove a variant from multi-platform images. docker/cli#6109
  • containerd image store: Initial BuildKit support for building Windows container images on Windows (requires an opt-in with DOCKER_BUILDKIT=1). moby/moby#49740

Bug fixes and enhancements

  • Add a new log option for fluentd log driver (fluentd-write-timeout), which enables specifying write timeouts for fluentd connections. moby/moby#49911
  • Add support for DOCKER_AUTH_CONFIG for the experimental --use-api-socket option. docker/cli#6019
  • Fix docker exec waiting for 10 seconds if a non-existing user or group was specified. moby/moby#49868
  • Fix docker swarm init ignoring cacert option of --external-ca. docker/cli#5995
  • Fix an issue where the CLI would not correctly save the configuration file (~/.docker/config.json) if it was a relative symbolic link. docker/cli#5282
  • Fix containers with --restart always policy using CDI devices failing to start on daemon restart. moby/moby#49990
  • Fix shell-completion to only complete some flags once, even though they can be set multiple times. docker/cli#6030
  • Fix the plugin does not implement PluginAddr interface error for Swarm CSI drivers. moby/moby#49961
  • Improve docker login error messages for invalid options. docker/cli#6036
  • Make sure the terminal state is restored if the CLI is forcefully terminated. docker/cli#6058
  • Update the default seccomp profile to match the libseccomp v2.6.0. The new syscalls are: listmount, statmount, lsm_get_self_attr, lsm_list_modules, lsm_set_self_attr, mseal, uretprobe, riscv_hwprobe, getxattrat, listxattrat, removexattrat, and setxattrat. This prevents containers from receiving EPERM errors when using them. moby/moby#50077
  • docker inspect: add shell completion, improve flag-description for --type and improve validation. docker/cli#6052
  • containerd image store: Enable BuildKit garbage collector by default. moby/moby#49899
  • containerd image store: Fix docker build not persisting overridden images as dangling. moby/moby#49702
  • containerd image store: Fix docker system df reporting a negative reclaimable space amount. moby/moby#49707
  • containerd image store: Fix duplicate PUT requests when pushing a multi-platform image. moby/moby#49949

Packaging updates

  • Drop Ubuntu 20.04 "Focal" packages as it reached end of life. docker/docker-ce-packaging#1200
  • Fix install location for RPM-based docker-ce man-pages. docker/docker-ce-packaging#1203

title: Issues with fakeroot overlay on CephFS in Ubuntu 24.04
body:
Hi,

I upgraded my Slurm cluster from Ubuntu 20.04 to 24.04 (and also Apptainer).
In the new system I can't use overlay images with fakeroot on CephFS storage anymore.

Creation with `overlay create --fakeroot --size 10240 foo.img` seems to work, but the created image is not recognized as ext3 by "file" (says "data")
When trying to use the image with eg. `shell --fakeroot --overlay foo.img docker://ubuntu` I get:
`FATAL:   while loading overlay images: failed to open overlay foo.img: image format not recognized`

Overlay images on local block storage (eg. /tmp) work.

As mentioned this operation worked in my "old" system with the same CephFS mount (Ceph Cluster has Ceph 15):

Ubuntu 20.04 (works):
                        ceph 15.2.17
                        apptainer 1.3.3
                        kernel 5.4.0-200

Ubuntu 24.04 (fails)
                        ceph 19.2.0
                        apptainer 1.3.6/1.4.1
                        kernel 6.8.0-55

Can someone give me a hint what's happening?
thank you

Changelog

Sourced from github.com/opencontainers/runc's changelog.

[1.3.0] - 2025-04-30

Mr. President, we must not allow a mine shaft gap!

Fixed

  • Removed preemptive "full access to cgroups" warning when calling runc pause or runc unpause as an unprivileged user without --systemd-cgroups. Now the warning is only emitted if an actual permission error was encountered. (#4709)
  • Several fixes to our CI, mainly related to AlmaLinux and CRIU. (#4670, #4728, #4736)

Changed

  • In runc 1.2, we changed our mount behaviour to correctly handle clearing flags. However, the error messages we returned did not provide as much information to users about what clearing flags were conflicting with locked mount flags. We now provide more diagnostic information if there is an error when in the fallback path to handle locked mount flags. (#4734)
  • Upgrade our CI to use golangci-lint v2.0. (#4692)
  • runc version information is now filled in using //go:embed rather than being set through Makefile. This allows go install or other non-make builds to contain the correct version information. Note that make EXTRA_VERSION=... still works. (#418)
  • Remove exclude directives from our go.mod for broken cilium/ebpf versions. v0.17.3 resolved the issue we had, and exclude directives are incompatible with go install. (#4748)

[1.3.0-rc.2] - 2025-04-10

Eppur si muove.

Fixed

  • Use the container's /etc/passwd to set the HOME env var. After a refactor for 1.3, we were setting it reading the host's /etc/passwd file instead. (#4693, #4688)
  • Override HOME env var if it's set to the empty string. This fixes a regression after the same refactor for 1.3 and aligns the behavior with older versions of runc. (#4711)
  • Add time namespace to container config after checkpoint/restore. CRIU since version 3.14 uses a time namespace for checkpoint/restore, however it was not joining the time namespace in runc. (#4705)

[1.3.0-rc.1] - 2025-03-04

No tengo miedo al invierno, con tu recuerdo lleno de sol.

Changelog

Sourced from github.com/opencontainers/umoci's changelog.

[0.5.0] - 2025-05-21

A wizard is never late, Frodo Baggins. Nor is he early; he arrives precisely when he means to.

This version of umoci requires Go 1.23 to build.

Security

  • A security flaw was found in the OCI image-spec, where it is possible to cause a blob with one media-type to be interpreted as a different media-type. As umoci is not a registry nor does it handle signatures, this vulnerability had no real impact on umoci but for safety we implemented the now-recommended media-type embedding and verification. CVE-2021-41190

Breaking

  • The method of configuring the on-disk format and MapOptions in RepackOptions and UnpackOptions has been changed. The on-disk format is now represented with the OnDiskFormat interface, with DirRootfs and OverlayfsRootfs as possible options to use. MapOptions is now configured inside the OnDiskFormat setting, which will require callers to adjust their usage of the main umoci APIs. In particular, examples like

    unpackOptions := &layer.UnpackOptions{
    MapOptions: mapOptions,
    WhiteoutMode: layer.StandardOCIWhiteout, // or layer.OverlayFSWhiteout
}
err := layer.UnpackManifest(ctx, engineExt, bundle, manifest, unpackOptions)

    will have to now be written as

    unpackOptions := &layer.UnpackOptions{
    OnDiskFormat: layer.DirRootfs{ // or layer.OverlayfsRootfs
        MapOptions: mapOptions,
    },
}
err := layer.UnpackManifest(ctx, engineExt, bundle, manifest, unpackOptions)

    and similarly

    repackOptions := &layer.RepackOptions{
    MapOptions: mapOptions,
    TranslateOverlayWhiteouts: false, // or true
}
layerRdr, err := layer.GenerateLayer(path, deltas, repackOptions)

Bumps the opencontainers group with 1 update: [github.com/opencontainers/umoci](https://github.com/opencontainers/umoci). Updates `github.com/opencontainers/umoci` from 0.4.7 to 0.5.0
Changelog

Sourced from github.com/opencontainers/umoci's changelog.

[0.5.0] - 2025-05-21

A wizard is never late, Frodo Baggins. Nor is he early; he arrives precisely when he means to.

This version of umoci requires Go 1.23 to build.

Security

  • A security flaw was found in the OCI image-spec, where it is possible to cause a blob with one media-type to be interpreted as a different media-type. As umoci is not a registry nor does it handle signatures, this vulnerability had no real impact on umoci but for safety we implemented the now-recommended media-type embedding and verification. CVE-2021-41190

Breaking

  • The method of configuring the on-disk format and MapOptions in RepackOptions and UnpackOptions has been changed. The on-disk format is now represented with the OnDiskFormat interface, with DirRootfs and OverlayfsRootfs as possible options to use. MapOptions is now configured inside the OnDiskFormat setting, which will require callers to adjust their usage of the main umoci APIs. In particular, examples like

    unpackOptions := &layer.UnpackOptions{
    MapOptions: mapOptions,
    WhiteoutMode: layer.StandardOCIWhiteout, // or layer.OverlayFSWhiteout
}
err := layer.UnpackManifest(ctx, engineExt, bundle, manifest, unpackOptions)

    will have to now be written as

    unpackOptions := &layer.UnpackOptions{
    OnDiskFormat: layer.DirRootfs{ // or layer.OverlayfsRootfs
        MapOptions: mapOptions,
    },
}
err := layer.UnpackManifest(ctx, engineExt, bundle, manifest, unpackOptions)

    and similarly

    repackOptions := &layer.RepackOptions{
    MapOptions: mapOptions,
    TranslateOverlayWhiteouts: false, // or true
}
layerRdr, err := layer.GenerateLayer(path, deltas, repackOptions)

... (truncated)

title: Apptainer reports newgidmap setuid/capabilities related error message when the cause is related to /etc/subgid file
body:
Hello there,

I'm not sure if there is any action on your part, but figured I should post this so it will show up in Google in case other people encounter this. 

I am on a cluster running SLES 15.6 and install apptainer (no apptainer-suid) through zypper. Currently that is v1.3.6. My /etc/subuid and /etc/subgid files are actually symlinks to files in a shared filesystem. However, this is a problem because when trying to do an `apptainer build` I will get an error:

```
$ apptainer build lolcow.sif lolcow.def
ERROR  : 'newgidmap' execution failed. Check that 'newgidmap' is setuid root or has setcap cap_setgid+eip.
ERROR  : Error while waiting event for user namespace mappings: no event received
```

The error message is misleading because the reason newgidmap fails is not because of setuid or capabilities, but because newgidmap has O_NOFOLLOW in its `open` function that opens /etc/subgid. If you look at the code in [shadow-utils](https://github.com/shadow-maint/shadow/) (which `newuidmap` is a part of), line 600 within the [comonio_open](https://github.com/shadow-maint/shadow/blob/master/lib/commonio.c#L600) function (which is called from the [sub_gid_open function in subordinateio.c](https://github.com/shadow-maint/shadow/blob/master/lib/subordinateio.c#L740) which is called from [newgidmap.c](https://github.com/shadow-maint/shadow/blob/master/src/newgidmap.c#L214)) is what tries to open the file, but the `open` call uses `O_NOFOLLOW` which means it will error out if it encounters a symlink instead of trying to open the linked file. If you run Apptainer with strace, you will see this is reported in a line like `[pid 11668] openat(AT_FDCWD, "/etc/subgid", O_RDONLY|O_NOCTTY|O_NONBLOCK|O_NOFOLLOW) = -1 ELOOP (Too many levels of symbolic links)`. 

This then bubbles up to apptainer, which reports the error message saying its because of setuid root or setcap, but doesn't realize the error is because newgidmap doesn't like it when /etc/subgid is a symlink. 

If there is a way for apptainer to detect this and report an error with a more accurate message, that'd be cool. But I recognize that this is a rare use case.

[1.3.0-rc.2] - 2025-04-10

Eppur si muove.

title: Apptainer build command fails if home directory contains an @ character
body:
### Version of Apptainer affected

1.4.0 and 1.4.1

### Version of Apptainer not affected

1.3.7 and earlier versions

### Expected behavior

When running a build command such as

`apptainer build alpine.sif docker://alpine`

with a home directory containing an '@', for example _`/home/student101@edu.local`_, the image gets downloaded successfully.

### Actual behavior when using an Apptainer version >= 1.4.0

When running the command `apptainer build alpine.sif docker://alpine` as above, the build fails with the error: 


_INFO:    Starting build...
INFO:    Fetching OCI image...
0.0b / 3.5MiB [-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------] 0 % 0.0 b/s 0s
FATAL:   While performing build: conveyor failed to get: stat /home/student101/index.json: no such file or directory_

### Analysis of the error

Apptainer seems to mangle the home directory path by removing the portion after the '@' sign. For example, a home directory such as _`/home/student101@edu.local`_ becomes _`/home/student101`_. The problem with removing of the path portion after '@' is visible in Apptainers error message. 

Apptainer seems to have no problems with other special characters in the home directory name. There were no problems when I tested with '=', '+', '&' or even '*' in the home path name. (I haven't tested the effect of special characters in the home name exhaustively)

### Why is there an '@' char in the home directory name?

The '@' character is often used with the sssd daemon. For example when enrolling a Linux box into Active Directory, sssd automatically adds the AD Domain extension to the login name with an '@' character. 

### Steps to reproduce this behavior

#### Create a user with a '@' in the name, for example:
`useradd -m -s /bin/bash test@edu.local`

#### su to the user
`su test@edu.local`

#### run an apptainer build command such as
`apptainer build alpine.sif docker://alpine`

### Possible Workaround
1. Downgrade to a version before 1.3.* Version. I tested with 1.3.7, which accepts '@' signs in the users home directory name
2. Rename Home Directory

### What OS/distro are you running

Ubuntu 22.04.5 LTS

### How did you install Apptainer

Latest versions from 
- https://github.com/apptainer/apptainer/releases/download/v1.4.1/apptainer-suid_1.4.1_amd64.deb
- https://github.com/apptainer/apptainer/releases/download/v1.4.1/apptainer_1.4.1_amd64.deb

Mr. President, we must not allow a mine shaft gap!

Eppur si muove.

title: Binding /dev to a container causes all accesses to /dev/* to get permission denied
body:
If you add `-B /dev` to an `apptainer run` or `apptainer exec` command causes all things in /dev to no longer be available.  

`apptainer run docker://ubuntu:latest` works fine, but `apptainer run -B /dev docker://ubuntu:latest` throws  errors and may completely fail depending on what's going on. 

``` bash
$ apptainer run docker://ubuntu:latest head /dev/null
INFO:    Using cached SIF image
$ apptainer run -B /dev docker://ubuntu:latest head /dev/null
INFO:    Using cached SIF image
/usr/bin/head: cannot open '/dev/null' for reading: Permission denied
$
```

This is especially problematic for `/dev/null` as so many things need it to run.

title: Add support for downloading images from IPFS through a HTTP gateway
body:
Previously there was some discussion regarding IPFS support through `/ipfs`:

* https://github.com/apptainer/apptainer/issues/134#issuecomment-2183979619

But that requires mounting a fuse filesystem, which might not be doable.

Another approach is to link with go-ipfs or to call the `ipfs get` command...

The node needs to be connected to the IPFS peer-to-peer network, though.

And the extra go library or go program would add to the standard install.

----

But it would also be possible to support it through HTTP, like in curl 8.4.0+:

https://blog.ipfs.tech/ipfs-uri-support-in-curl/

https://curl.se/docs/ipfs.html

Then it only needs to rewrite the URL, and use the same code as in "net".

A bonus is that the sha256 is in the URL, so it doesn't need to do any HEAD call...

```console
$ ipfs add --cid-version=1 --wrap-with-directory alpine.sif 
added bafybeigmf4qbfae5zyacg6tp6q67fcb7w3ouw7gmvtbaxqpg5rmmznaf6i alpine.sif
added bafybeibpisnayrx6rb3eicvsxu6lench2xogxurrgonj67jujgofa2bpge 
 3.41 MiB / 3.41 MiB [=========================================================================================] 100.00%
$ apptainer run ipfs://bafybeigmf4qbfae5zyacg6tp6q67fcb7w3ouw7gmvtbaxqpg5rmmznaf6i
INFO:    Downloading network image
3.4MiB / 3.4MiB [==============================================================================================] 100 %0s
Apptainer> 
```

The CID can be [converted](https://cid.ipfs.tech/#bafybeigmf4qbfae5zyacg6tp6q67fcb7w3ouw7gmvtbaxqpg5rmmznaf6i) to a hex sha256, so that the cache directory looks "normal".

```console
$ cidsum --quiet alpine.sif 
bafybeigmf4qbfae5zyacg6tp6q67fcb7w3ouw7gmvtbaxqpg5rmmznaf6i
$ ipfs-inspect bafybeigmf4qbfae5zyacg6tp6q67fcb7w3ouw7gmvtbaxqpg5rmmznaf6i
base32-cidv1-dag-pb-(sha2-256:256:CC2F2012809DCE00237A6FF43DF2883FB6DD4B7CCCACC20BC1E6EC58CCB405F2)

$ # ~/.apptainer/cache/ipfs/cc2f2012809dce00237a6ff43df2883fb6dd4b7cccacc20bc1e6ec58ccb405f2
```

It is a [multihash](https://multiformats.io/), but only the base32 decoding is required - the rest can be CIDv1-only.

Only the gateway needs to be connected to the p2p network (which can be made private).

https://docs.ipfs.tech/quickstart/retrieve/#ipfs-retrieval-methods

https://docs.ipfs.tech/install/server-infrastructure/#features

title: add equivalent of MAMBA_DOCKERFILE_ACTIVATE
body:
My [dockerfile](https://github.com/ArcInstitute/scRecounter/blob/tiledb/docker/sc-recounter-star/Dockerfile) uses micromamba to install all dependencies. This allows for one source of truth for dependencies when running the nextflow pipeline with Conda or Docker. However, this setup does not work with apptainer, since there is no equivalent of `MAMBA_DOCKERFILE_ACTIVATE` for apptainer, so the env is not activated. 

It would be very helpful if apptainer supported micromamba activation, as is supported for docker.

[1.3.0] - 2025-04-30

Mr. President, we must not allow a mine shaft gap!

Fixed

  • Removed preemptive "full access to cgroups" warning when calling runc pause or runc unpause as an unprivileged user without --systemd-cgroups. Now the warning is only emitted if an actual permission error was encountered. (#4709)
  • Several fixes to our CI, mainly related to AlmaLinux and CRIU. (#4670, #4728, #4736)

Changed

  • In runc 1.2, we changed our mount behaviour to correctly handle clearing flags. However, the error messages we returned did not provide as much information to users about what clearing flags were conflicting with locked mount flags. We now provide more diagnostic information if there is an error when in the fallback path to handle locked mount flags. (#4734)
  • Upgrade our CI to use golangci-lint v2.0. (#4692)
  • runc version information is now filled in using //go:embed rather than being set through Makefile. This allows go install or other non-make builds to contain the correct version information. Note that make EXTRA_VERSION=... still works. (#418)
  • Remove exclude directives from our go.mod for broken cilium/ebpf versions. v0.17.3 resolved the issue we had, and exclude directives are incompatible with go install. (#4748)

[1.3.0-rc.2] - 2025-04-10

Eppur si muove.

Fixed

  • Use the container's /etc/passwd to set the HOME env var. After a refactor for 1.3, we were setting it reading the host's /etc/passwd file instead. (#4693, #4688)
  • Override HOME env var if it's set to the empty string. This fixes a regression after the same refactor for 1.3 and aligns the behavior with older versions of runc. (#4711)
  • Add time namespace to container config after checkpoint/restore. CRIU since version 3.14 uses a time namespace for checkpoint/restore, however it was not joining the time namespace in runc. (#4705)

No tengo miedo al invierno, con tu recuerdo lleno de sol.

body:
Bumps the opencontainers group with 2 updates: [github.com/opencontainers/runc](https://github.com/opencontainers/runc) and [github.com/opencontainers/selinux](https://github.com/opencontainers/selinux). Updates `github.com/opencontainers/runc` from 1.2.5 to 1.3.0
Changelog

Sourced from github.com/opencontainers/runc's changelog.

[1.3.0] - 2025-04-30

Mr. President, we must not allow a mine shaft gap!

Fixed

  • Removed preemptive "full access to cgroups" warning when calling runc pause or runc unpause as an unprivileged user without --systemd-cgroups. Now the warning is only emitted if an actual permission error was encountered. (#4709)
  • Several fixes to our CI, mainly related to AlmaLinux and CRIU. (#4670, #4728, #4736)

Changed

  • In runc 1.2, we changed our mount behaviour to correctly handle clearing flags. However, the error messages we returned did not provide as much information to users about what clearing flags were conflicting with locked mount flags. We now provide more diagnostic information if there is an error when in the fallback path to handle locked mount flags. (#4734)
  • Upgrade our CI to use golangci-lint v2.0. (#4692)
  • runc version information is now filled in using //go:embed rather than being set through Makefile. This allows go install or other non-make builds to contain the correct version information. Note that make EXTRA_VERSION=... still works. (#418)
  • Remove exclude directives from our go.mod for broken cilium/ebpf versions. v0.17.3 resolved the issue we had, and exclude directives are incompatible with go install. (#4748)

[1.3.0-rc.2] - 2025-04-10

Eppur si muove.

Fixed

  • Use the container's /etc/passwd to set the HOME env var. After a refactor for 1.3, we were setting it reading the host's /etc/passwd file instead. (#4693, #4688)
  • Override HOME env var if it's set to the empty string. This fixes a regression after the same refactor for 1.3 and aligns the behavior with older versions of runc. (#4711)
  • Add time namespace to container config after checkpoint/restore. CRIU since version 3.14 uses a time namespace for checkpoint/restore, however it was not joining the time namespace in runc. (#4705)

[1.3.0-rc.1] - 2025-03-04

No tengo miedo al invierno, con tu recuerdo lleno de sol.

libcontainer API

  • configs.CommandHook struct has changed, Command is now a pointer. Also, configs.NewCommandHook now accepts a *Command. (#4325)
  • The Process struct has User string field replaced with numeric

title: Timeline for v1.4.1 release
body:
Hi All,

Just wondering what the possible timeline for v.1.4.1 is? (I do not see any timeline on the milestones link). 

There is an arm64/v8 specification bug that was fixed and merged for 1.4.1 which is preventing us from using apptainer in arm64 nodes with containers that do not have the specific arm64/v8 tag attached https://github.com/apptainer/apptainer/pull/2907. Mostly happens with containers built through Github Actions with emulation that default to arm64 and ignore the v8 specification.

Thanks,
Jordan

## Description of the Pull Request (PR):

Newer versions of Docker (since 25) save images in a new format compatible with both docker (manifest.json) and oci (index.json)

This triggered some bugs with parsers of the old format, and the workarounds had some issues with performance and memory usage...

```
manifest.json
repositories
```

New format:

```
blobs/
blobs/sha256/
blobs/sha256/08000c18d16dadf9553d747a58cf44023423a9ab010aab96cf263d2216b8b350
blobs/sha256/11834567b56252a953f68289506f8ea00d4801769467ee8509e868c4b89ec56d

blobs/sha256/aded1e1a5b3705116fa0a92ba074a5e0b0031647d9c315983ccba2ee5428ec8b
index.json
manifest.json
oci-layout
repositories
```

OCI format: (`oci-archive`)

```
blobs/
blobs/sha256/
blobs/sha256/aded1e1a5b3705116fa0a92ba074a5e0b0031647d9c315983ccba2ee5428ec8b
blobs/sha256/b0f6f1c319a1570f67352d490370f0aeb5c0e67a087baf2d5f301ad51ec18858
blobs/sha256/b3454025ce78fa93aba879b2824a06a59e2b8c5005b2a4286368433cd0f41cde
index.json
oci-layout
```

Note: the oci-archive layer is saved in the legacy gzip compression, that's why the sha256 differs.

In the docker-archive, the layers were saved uncompressed and then you ran pigz on the archive.

Changelog

Changelog

This file documents all notable changes made to this project since runc 1.0.

The format is based on Keep a Changelog, and this project adheres to Semantic Versioning.

[Unreleased]

[1.3.0-rc.1] - 2025-03-04

No tengo miedo al invierno, con tu recuerdo lleno de sol.

libcontainer API

  • configs.CommandHook struct has changed, Command is now a pointer. Also, configs.NewCommandHook now accepts a *Command. (#4325)
  • The Process struct has User string field replaced with numeric UID and GID fields, and AdditionalGroups changed its type from []string to []int. Essentially, resolution of user and group names to IDs is no longer performed by libcontainer, so if a libcontainer user previously relied on this feature, now they have to convert names to IDs before calling libcontainer; it is recommended to use Go package github.com/moby/sys/user for that. (#3999)
  • Move libcontainer/cgroups to a separate repository. (#4618)

Fixed

  • runc exec -p no longer ignores specified ioPriority and scheduler settings. Similarly, libcontainer's Container.Start and Container.Run methods no longer ignore Process.IOPriority and Process.Scheduler settings. (#4585)
  • We no longer use F_SEAL_FUTURE_WRITE when sealing the runc binary, as it turns out this had some unfortunate bugs in older kernel versions and was never necessary in the first place. (#4641, #4640)
  • runc now uses a more flexible method of joining namespaces, which better matches the behaviour of nsenter(8). This is mainly useful for users that create a container with a runc-managed user namespace but want the container to join some externally-managed namespace as well. (#4492)
  • runc now properly handles joining time namespaces (such as with runc exec). Previously we would attempt to set the time offsets when joining, which would fail. (#4635, #4636)
  • Handle EINTR retries correctly for socket-related direct golang.org/x/sys/unix system calls. (#4637)
  • Handle close_range(2) errors more gracefully. (#4596)
  • Fix a stall issue that would happen if setting O_CLOEXEC with CloseExecFrom failed (#4599).
  • Handle errors on older kernels when resetting ambient capabilities more gracefully. (#4597)

Changed

  • runc now has an official release policy to help provide more consistency around our release schedules and better define our support policy for old

body:
Hello

I work in an HPC environment running Rocky Linux 8, and we have some independent clusters. I created an apptainer image, and I am able to do the following on **Cluster 1**, which uses **gpfs**. 
```
apptainer --version
> apptainer version 1.2.5-1.el8

apptainer overlay create --size 5120 $HOME/test.img
apptainer shell B $HOME --overlay $HOME/test.img container.sif
> # in container everything fine
> exit

# try again, which works
apptainer shell B $HOME --overlay $HOME/test.img container.sif
> # in container everything fine
> exit
```

Now when I try the same commands with the same container (.sif) on **Cluster 2**, which uses **weka-fs**, and everything has the same file permissions, I run into overlay locking issues.
```
apptainer --version

apptainer overlay create --size 5120 $HOME/test.img
apptainer shell B $HOME --overlay $HOME/test.img container.sif

```
I then tried to find out what process it is using, but **lsof** did not provide any info. Moreover I tried to fix the partition using the **fsck** binary (which I saw on another singularity thread for the same issue), the output looked fine, but this did not resolve the issue either.

Any help is appreciated.

Matthew

title: Create reproducible sif images if wanted

## Description of the Pull Request (PR):

When SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH is set, create reproducible/deterministic images that have an identical checksum (for the same contents).

title: Allow building reproducible images with SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH
body:
The [Reproducible Builds](https://reproducible-builds.org/) project aims to provide builds (and images) that are **reproducible**.

See https://reproducible-builds.org/news/2024/02/08/reproducible-builds-at-fosdem-2024/ "The First Ten Years"

That is, if you build a SIF image from the same content the output should be _exactly_ the same.
Bit-for-bit, the checksums of the .sif file should be identical. So the results needs to be deterministic.

For Apptainer, this means that the build date and other timestamps must honor [SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH](https://reproducible-builds.org/docs/source-date-epoch/).
This environment variable specifies the last modification (seconds UTC), and replaces the current time.

The information in the squashfs must also be sorted*, and the UUID of the SIF format removed (`nil`).

\* https://github.com/plougher/squashfs-tools/blob/master/Documentation/latest/TECHNICAL-INFO

----

This feature is optional. If you don't set the SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH variable, then it builds just like before.

But if you set it, then the output should be **identical**. For instance, the sha256 should be the same.

```console
$ export SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH=$(stat --format %Y squashfs-root)
$ apptainer build 1.sif squashfs-root
INFO:    Starting build...
INFO:    Extracting local image...
INFO:    Creating SIF file...
[=====================================================================] 100 % 0s
INFO:    Build complete: 1.sif
$ apptainer build 2.sif squashfs-root
INFO:    Starting build...
INFO:    Extracting local image...
INFO:    Creating SIF file...
[=====================================================================] 100 % 0s
INFO:    Build complete: 2.sif
$ diff -s 1.sif 2.sif 
Files 1.sif and 2.sif are identical
$ diffoscope 1.sif 2.sif
$
```

Without SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH, it will say `Binary files 1.sif and 2.sif differ` and diffoscope outputs.

----

This feature goes well with recording the input digest while using a docker image, and not just `latest`:

* https://github.com/apptainer/apptainer/issues/2764

You could set the SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH to the time when the original docker image was created:

`docker inspect --format "{{.Created}}"`

```shell
docker pull alpine
export SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH=$(date -d "$(docker inspect --format "{{.Created}}" alpine:latest)" +%s)
# have to pull it again, to get the image digest
apptainer build alpine.sif docker://alpine:latest
```

title: When resolv.conf is a symlink on host, its updates are not propagated into container
body:
systemd-resolved has 4 modes of operation, 3 of which depend on `/etc/resolv.conf` file being a symlink: https://www.freedesktop.org/software/systemd/man/latest/systemd-resolved.service.html#/etc/resolv.conf

However, when launching a container, `/etc/resolv.conf`, the symlink is resolved, and the inode where it points is mounted. I'm using mode 3 (`/run/systemd/resolve/resolv.conf`) and NetworkManager sometimes deletes the filesand recreates it instead of just editing its contents (probably when connection is completely lost?). This results in an invalid DNS configuration inside the container.

An easy way to trigger this is to connect a laptop via Ethernet, launch the container, then disconnect the wire and connect to a wifi that uses a different DNS setting.

title: Selective Mounting of Gaudi Devices into a Container
body:
## Description of the Pull Request (PR):

This PR introduces support for the selective mounting of Intel® Gaudi accelerators.

This feature is enabled via the `--hpu` option. The required devices are specified via the `HABANA_VISIBLE_DEVICES` environment variable, which should contain a comma-separated list of device IDs (e.g., `"1,2,3"`). This controls which accelerators are bound into the `/dev` directory in the container. A special value of "all" is also supported _(default if not provided)_, while an empty environment variable results in no devices being mounted.

This feature is effective when a minimal `/dev` directory is utilized, either by setting the `--contain` flag or configuring `mount dev` with the `minimal` option _(as otherwise, the entire `/dev` tree is mounted into the container)_.

[1.2.6] - 2025-03-17

Hasta la victoria, siempre.

Fixed

  • Fix a stall issue that would happen if setting O_CLOEXEC with CloseExecFrom failed (#4647).
  • runc now properly handles joining time namespaces (such as with runc exec). Previously we would attempt to set the time offsets when joining, which would fail. (#4635, #4649)
  • Handle EINTR retries correctly for socket-related direct golang.org/x/sys/unix system calls. (#4650)
  • We no longer use F_SEAL_FUTURE_WRITE when sealing the runc binary, as it turns out this had some unfortunate bugs in older kernel versions and was never necessary in the first place. (#4651, #4640)

Removed

  • Remove Fexecve helper from libcontainer/system. Runc 1.2.1 removed runc-dmz, but we forgot to remove this helper added only for that. (#4646)

Changed

  • Use Go 1.23 for official builds, run CI with Go 1.24 and drop Ubuntu 20.04 from CI. We need to drop Ubuntu 20.04 from CI because Github Actions announced it's already deprecated and it will be discontinued soon. (#4648)

title: How to attach gdb from within the apptainer to another process
body:
This issue is similar to https://github.com/apptainer/apptainer/issues/2913, but with a different setup. Sorry I'm not very familiar with apptainer so this could be a stupid question.

In my case, I have an application running inside the apptainer, and I need to attach gdb to it from within another apptainer. For context, I'm using Rez package manager and CLion as my IDE. Since CLion requires a different Rez environment to be able to read my project, I have to launch the second apptainer and create that environment, then use gdb from there.

So, I launch the second apptainer via `apptainer exec --nv --security=capability --add-caps CAP_SYS_PTRACE .... bash`, and then I run my `build-env` script to put me into the correct rez environment. From there on the command line, I tried to attach gdb to my application process using `gdb -p pid`, but that gives me the `ptrace: Operation not permitted` error.

In my case, `cat /proc/sys/kernel/yama/ptrace_scope` already returns 0 so it's not really restricted, I've also permanently raised caps on my GDB binary with `sudo setcap CAP_SYS_PTRACE=+eip`, still it doesn't work. I saw people have been running into the same issue with Dockers and that's usually solved by adding `--add-caps CAP_SYS_PTRACE` to the Docker command, but that doesn't work for apptainer. I also noticed that once inside the apptainer, `sudo` is no longer available so there's nothing I can do.

Maybe I'm just missing a flag on the `apptainer` command?

title: Record metadata for original image used from oci
body:
## Description of the Pull Request (PR):

Add two new fields to the metadata, when building from `docker:`

`org.opencontainers.image.base.name`
`org.opencontainers.image.base.digest`

The fields used for Apptainer are the same that is used in the OCI image specification:

https://github.com/opencontainers/image-spec/blob/main/annotations.md

These record the information that is available, but hidden away:

```console
$ docker pull alpine
Using default tag: latest
latest: Pulling from library/alpine
Digest: sha256:a8560b36e8b8210634f77d9f7f9efd7ffa463e380b75e2e74aff4511df3ef88c
Status: Image is up to date for alpine:latest
docker.io/library/alpine:latest
```

In addition to the basic metadata that was previously recorded:

```
org.label-schema.usage.singularity.deffile.bootstrap: docker
org.label-schema.usage.singularity.deffile.from: alpine
```

```
org.opencontainers.image.base.digest: sha256:a8560b36e8b8210634f77d9f7f9efd7ffa463e380b75e2e74aff4511df3ef88c
org.opencontainers.image.base.name: docker.io/library/alpine:latest
```

We don't need to record the Id (ConfigFile) or the Manifest checksums:

docker inspect
```
        "Id": "sha256:aded1e1a5b3705116fa0a92ba074a5e0b0031647d9c315983ccba2ee5428ec8b",
        "RepoTags": [
            "alpine:latest"
        ],
```

title: Reference request: technical issues with container adoption beyond the basics
body:
I'm looking for information on things that might cause problems trying to adopt (Linux namespaces based) containerization in HPC environments, beyond more common, seemingly portable stuff, like people being worried about "security".

I'm new to most of this so I'm not sure how much sense this makes, but for example:
- are there "issues" (depends on what you want to do I guess?) with Infiniband/RDMA/MPI...? (as opposed to just using MPI over an IP network which happens to be backed by infiniband?)
- a common distributed filesystem, I forget offhand which one, does not fully implement namespaces yet, which can lead to permissions issues

...

I initially made the assumption that I don't really see why HPC should have problems with containers (at least since docker got a rootless mode, or podman) (ok and perhaps cgroups shenanigans..and...and...), but now that I know a bit more, I'm starting to scratch my head.

(My cluster is a rather old system, but the question is general enough.)

Thanks.

title: How about creating a standalone executable redistribution?
body:
When I log into my friend's workstation, it's running an Ubuntu LTS version. But there isn't the apptainer environment. For some reason, they cannot install apptainer on this workstation. I can execute some pre-installed and portable programs. But I have some apptainer images to run. How can I solve this issue?
I found an interesting project on GitHub, Conty (https://github.com/Kron4ek/Conty). It's basic a containerized ArchLinux distro, but an executable. So I have an idea, why create a standalone executable for `apptainer` like Conty, or packing into an AppImage? What are the limitations to do so? To build a customized contry.sh seems not easy. Hope somebody can have a look. Thanks!

title: Registry mirror config via /etc/containers stopped working in v1.4.0
body:
Running a local registry mirror has been a convenient way to address Docker Hub rate limits. Putting the configuration in `/etc/containers` applies it to all local users, which is friendly for HPC environments. E.g.

`/etc/containers/registries.conf.d/registry-mirror.conf`
```
[[registry]]
location="docker.io"
[[registry.mirror]]
location="registry-mirror.example.edu"
```

@aaronmoate has noted this configuration is working with v1.3.6, but apparently stopped working in v1.4.0. Image pulls from Docker Hub are going directly, rather than through the mirror:
```apptainer build miniconda.sif docker://continuumio/miniconda3:latest```

Opening this issue as a placeholder, and currently working on gathering more information.

title: How can I use gdb on an executable running inside apptainer?
body:

`apptainer exec rhel8.sif /usr/bin/python3 -c 'import time; time.sleep(3600)'`

then in another window, I want to attach a debugger to it, I get:
