title: Build Dockerfile directly from apptainer bootstrap
body:
Some people have a workflow where they update a Dockerfile, and then use that as a bootstrap...

This requires either using docker-daemon, or pushing the results to a registry (over the network?)

```shell
docker build -t image .
apptainer build image.sif docker-daemon:image

docker save image > image.tar
apptainer build image.sif docker-archive:image.tar

docker push image 
apptainer build docker://image # (registry: docker.io)
```

It could be useful if apptainer could do both steps, and create a sif image from the build context.

Then you don't need any docker daemon (only a buildkit daemon), and you don't need any registry.

```shell
apptainer build image.sif buildkit:.
```

This also allows using a modern build framework (BuildKit), instead of legacy docker or podman.

https://github.com/moby/buildkit

```
buildctl build \
    --frontend=dockerfile.v0 \
    --local context=. \
    --local dockerfile=.

buildctl build ... --output type=oci,dest=path/to/output.tar
```

https://blog.mobyproject.org/introducing-buildkit-17e056cc5317 ([the LLB is a little like LLVM...](https://www.docker.com/blog/compiling-containers-dockerfiles-llvm-and-buildkit/))

Most of the code is shared with the OCI bootstrap, except for the new "buildImage" call.

----

Here is what it could experimentally look like:

```
Bootstrap: buildkit
From: build
```

Where "build" is a path to a directory with the Dockerfile, and optionally any other "build context".

```Dockerfile
FROM alpine
RUN true
```

The entire directory is transferred to the buildkit worker, and the result is saved as an `oci-archive`.

There is a build cache, so only those build steps that actually _need_ to be rebuilt are executed again.

```console
$ apptainer build --force buildkit.sif buildkit.def
INFO:    Starting build...
INFO:    Building OCI image...
[+] Building 0.5s (6/6) FINISHED                                                                                        
 => [internal] load build definition from Dockerfile                                                               0.0s
 => => transferring dockerfile: 58B                                                                                0.0s
 => [internal] load metadata for docker.io/library/alpine:latest                                                   0.4s
 => [internal] load .dockerignore                                                                                  0.0s
 => => transferring context: 2B                                                                                    0.0s
 => [1/2] FROM docker.io/library/alpine:latest@sha256:a8560b36e8b8210634f77d9f7f9efd7ffa463e380b75e2e74aff4511df3  0.0s
 => => resolve docker.io/library/alpine:latest@sha256:a8560b36e8b8210634f77d9f7f9efd7ffa463e380b75e2e74aff4511df3  0.0s
 => CACHED [2/2] RUN true                                                                                          0.0s
 => exporting to oci image format                                                                                  0.0s
 => => exporting layers                                                                                            0.0s
 => => exporting manifest sha256:43ea733cb28a8fb3b7076fc319053818f34468d4ef76722f2b8bf2aa1996167f                  0.0s
 => => exporting config sha256:d128407b81aff69eb707920fab5960c2cd6c258e7dbfe4decb3234fb7d3ea10f                    0.0s
 => => sending tarball                                                                                             0.0s
INFO:    Extracting OCI image...
INFO:    Inserting Apptainer configuration...
INFO:    Creating SIF file...
[=============================================================================================================] 100 % 0s
INFO:    Build complete: buildkit.sif
```

---

The requirement is to install BuildKit, and start the BuildKit server (possibly rootless).

It is possible to have workers for different architectures, to do multi-arch image builds.

```console
$ buildctl debug workers
ID				PLATFORMS
t4ddg3lhk5x535vl2ahk78bbv	linux/amd64,linux/amd64/v2,linux/amd64/v3,linux/arm64,linux/riscv64,linux/ppc64,linux/ppc64le,linux/s390x,linux/386,linux/mips64le,linux/mips64,linux/arm/v7,linux/arm/v6
tjjkniyozr2aie96sx52bq2um	linux/amd64,linux/amd64/v2,linux/amd64/v3,linux/arm64,linux/riscv64,linux/ppc64,linux/ppc64le,linux/s390x,linux/386,linux/mips64le,linux/mips64,linux/arm/v7,linux/arm/v6
```

The default workers are using QEMU for cross-builds, you can also use external workers.

The only other requirement is `runc`, but it is also bundled with the regular installation...

To start the system buildkitd:

`sudo buildkitd`

`/run/buildkit/buildkitd.sock`

To start the user buildkitd:

`rootlesskit buildkitd`

```shell
export BUILDKIT_HOST=unix://$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/buildkit/buildkitd.sock
```

There are also systemd units available upstream, to start the buildkit daemon.

The above does not use/need containerd, but instead the OCI worker (and CNI)

```
bin/
bin/buildctl
bin/buildkit-cni-bridge
bin/buildkit-cni-firewall
bin/buildkit-cni-host-local
bin/buildkit-cni-loopback
bin/buildkit-qemu-aarch64
bin/buildkit-qemu-arm
bin/buildkit-qemu-i386
bin/buildkit-qemu-ppc64le
bin/buildkit-qemu-riscv64
bin/buildkit-qemu-s390x
bin/buildkit-runc
bin/buildkitd
```

https://github.com/moby/buildkit/tree/master/examples/systemd/system

title: The oci-image format does not handle nested index
20x Memory requirements moving from v1.3.6 to 1.4.0
body:
Hi Team, 

We use apptainer to build sif containers from local docker containers. 
My docker containers are quite large (~26Gb). With version 1.3.6 apptainer needs about ~3.5GB to 4GB of RAM to build the container. Moving to v1.4 has increased the memory requirements to somewhere between 80GB to 90GB. 

I run the following command: 
`apptainer  build image.sif docker-daemon:image`

I noticed that on version 1.3.6 apptainer outputs: 
`INFO:    Starting build...`

Whereas on version 1.4.0 it outputs:

```
INFO:    Starting build...
INFO:    Fetching OCI image...
INFO:    Extracting OCI image...
INFO:    Inserting Apptainer configuration...
INFO:    Creating SIF file...
```

I am happy to attach the debug files (11MB each) and run additional profiling etc. 
However, I first wanted to check if this is a user error? 

Thank you.
Best,
Julius

body:
In our use case, we'd like to use the image mount mechanism to increase the modularity of our images.

How is it possible to build a “Data” image directly without dumping and re-adding the SIF object by modifying the parttype, which is a bit cumbersome ?

We could have a docker to squashfs conversion and a `sif add` step, but it would add a unnecessary step to our pipelines.

Having the means to build this type of image or to change it without dump/re-add would be fantastic!

labels.description: Something isn't working

body:
## Description of the Pull Request (PR):

### This fixes or addresses the following GitHub issues:

 - Fixes #2894


#### Before submitting a PR, make sure you have done the following:

- [ ] Added myself as a contributor to the [Contributors File](https://github.com/apptainer/apptainer/blob/main/CONTRIBUTORS.md).

### Root cause


```
docker manifest inspect -v nvcr.io/nvidia/tensorflow:25.01-tf2-py3
```

part of the manifest info are:
```
		"Ref": "nvcr.io/nvidia/tensorflow:25.01-tf2-py3@sha256:c3bb1ff7de89a02debf8f5ce971cebfaaae328e5a05c03fb00926e182f283cf8",
		"Descriptor": {
			"mediaType": "application/vnd.docker.distribution.manifest.v2+json",
			"digest": "sha256:c3bb1ff7de89a02debf8f5ce971cebfaaae328e5a05c03fb00926e182f283cf8",
			"size": 10744,
			"platform": {
				"architecture": "amd64",
				"os": "linux"
			}
		},
```
```
		"Ref": "nvcr.io/nvidia/tensorflow:25.01-tf2-py3@sha256:27af36d7014e0ee27a14b3cc9f1f49c3d95abf4c93bd4c0eee8ea87b997aa44c",
		"Descriptor": {
			"mediaType": "application/vnd.docker.distribution.manifest.v2+json",
			"digest": "sha256:27af36d7014e0ee27a14b3cc9f1f49c3d95abf4c93bd4c0eee8ea87b997aa44c",
			"size": 10746,
			"platform": {
				"architecture": "arm64",
				"os": "linux"
			}
		},
```

when apptainer pulls with `--arch arm64`, the `--arch-variant` will be automatically appended as `v8`, this causes the error, `no child with platform linux/arm64/v8 in index nvcr.io/nvidia/tensorflow:25.01-tf2-py3`.

after pathcing this PR
```
➜  test apptainer exec tensorflow_25.01-tf2-py3.sif uname -m
aarch64
```

title: RFE: add a --no-env option
body:
Hi!

Following up on #2563, I would like to request the addition of a new `--no-env` option to `run`/`exec`/`shell` commands, which would be the counterpart of `--env` and prevent specific host environment variables from being passed on to the container environment.

Currently, to prevent host env vars from being passed to the container, one can use:
* `APPTAINERENV_MYVAR=` to override the value of `MYVAR` in the container, but that also has the negative effect of overriding the value of a `MYVAR` variable that would be pre-defined in the container definition, and may not be suitable in all cases
* `-e`/`--cleanenv`, which will prevent *all* host env vars from being passed to the container. But in many cases, some host-side variables need to be transmitted to the container, like the ones defining storage locations (`$PROJECT`, `$SCRATCH`) or other common variables.

So, there is a number of use cases for something in the middle, that would only selectively "mask" specific host-level environment variables in the container, while preserving the value of pre-defined container variables, and still allow passing most of the host environment to the container.

Which is why it would be beneficial to add a new `--no-env` option (and corresponding `APPTAINERNOENV_*` variables), on the same model as the existing `--env` / `APPTAINERENV_*` system, that would prevent those variables from being passed to the container, without overriding their value if they're already defined in the container environment.

In practice, according to the [order of precedence](https://apptainer.org/docs/user/latest/environment_and_metadata.html#environment-variable-precedence) this could be an extra check in the last step, that would become:
> Restore environment variables from the host, if they have not already been set in the container, and the `--cleanenv` / `--containall` options were not specified, and those variables are not part of the exclusion list specificed by `--no-env` / `APPTAINERNOENV_*`

Thanks for considering this!

[1.2.6] - 2025-03-17

Hasta la victoria, siempre.

Fixed

  • Fix a stall issue that would happen if setting O_CLOEXEC with CloseExecFrom failed (#4647).

title: Small issue with riscv architecture detection
body:
Apparently I added the `__riscv` macro, which is defined for **both** 32-bit and 64-bit.

Now it is very unlikely to discover a 32-bit architecture outside multilib, but anyway...

riscv32

```
#define __riscv 1
#define __riscv_cmodel_medlow 1
#define __riscv_float_abi_soft 1
#define __riscv_xlen 32
```

riscv64

```
#define __riscv 1
#define __riscv_atomic 1
#define __riscv_cmodel_medlow 1
#define __riscv_fdiv 1
#define __riscv_float_abi_double 1
#define __riscv_flen 64
#define __riscv_compressed 1
#define __riscv_mul 1
#define __riscv_muldiv 1
#define __riscv_xlen 64
#define __riscv_fsqrt 1
#define __riscv_div 1
```

Only want to support riscv64 (not riscv32), like it only supports ppc64 (not ppc32)

So should remove the check for the riscv macro, from the mconfig basechecks.

title: Using a network bridge as non-root user doesn't work on Ubuntu 24.04.
body:
I am running a container with `--net --network=bridge` as non-root users.  In the past this worked with the following steps:

```
sudo apptainer config global --set "allow net groups" foo
sudo apptainer config global --set "allow net networks" bridge
```
Now users of the group "foo" could run a container with `--net --network=bridge`.

Since upgrading the host system to Ubuntu 24.04 (previously it was 18.04), this now results in an error.

## Steps to reproduce

```
sudo apptainer config global --set "allow net groups" foo
sudo apptainer config global --set "allow net networks" bridge
apptainer pull docker://ubuntu:24.04  # I think it doesn't really matter which image, I get the same with alpine

# run this with a user in the "foo" group:
apptainer shell --net --network=bridge ubuntu_24.04.sif
```

## Expected behaviour

The container is created with the network bridge.

## Actual behaviour

The `apptainer shell` command fails with 

> INFO:    Terminating squashfuse_ll after timeout
> INFO:    Timeouts can be caused by a running background process
> ERROR:   could not delete networks: plugin type="firewall" failed (delete): could not initialize iptables protocol 0: exec: "iptables": executable file not found in $PATH
> FATAL:   container creation failed: invalid argument

## Additional information

- I'm using Apptainer 1.4.0
- Host OS is Ubuntu 24.04
- iptables is installed on the host (located in `/usr/sbin/iptables`)
- I tried installing iptables in the container as well but it didn't help
- It _does_ work when running with sudo, so maybe only a PATH issue with `/usr/sbin` for non-root users?
- It is working on Ubuntu 18.04/Apptainer 1.0.3

Not sure if relevant but I gave it a try with Apptainer 1.0.3 on Ubuntu 24.04.  It also fails but with a different error:

> ERROR:   could not delete networks: plugin type="firewall" failed (delete): could not initialize iptables protocol 0: could not get iptables version: exit status 111
> FATAL:   container creation failed: plugin type="bridge" failed (add): failed to locate iptables: could not get iptables version: exit status 111

Changelog

Sourced from github.com/opencontainers/runc's changelog.

[1.2.6] - 2025-03-17

Hasta la victoria, siempre.

Fixed

  • Fix a stall issue that would happen if setting O_CLOEXEC with CloseExecFrom failed (#4647).
  • runc now properly handles joining time namespaces (such as with runc exec). Previously we would attempt to set the time offsets when joining, which would fail. (#4635, #4649)
  • Handle EINTR retries correctly for socket-related direct golang.org/x/sys/unix system calls. (#4650)
  • We no longer use F_SEAL_FUTURE_WRITE when sealing the runc binary, as it turns out this had some unfortunate bugs in older kernel versions and was never necessary in the first place. (#4651, #4640)

Removed

  • Remove Fexecve helper from libcontainer/system. Runc 1.2.1 removed runc-dmz, but we forgot to remove this helper added only for that. (#4646)

Changed

  • Use Go 1.23 for official builds, run CI with Go 1.24 and drop Ubuntu 20.04 from CI. We need to drop Ubuntu 20.04 from CI because Github Actions announced it's already deprecated and it will be discontinued soon. (#4648)

title: Fix Archlinux pacman.conf URL
body:
## Fix Archlinux `pacman.conf` URL

In the Arch bootstrap, a default pacman config is downloaded. But the repo `github.com/archlinux/svntogit-packages` the config file is downloaded from, has been archived on May 20, 2023. The old `pacman.conf` in that repo includes the `[community]` package repo, which has been removed [1]. This causes building an Arch-based container to fail, if the user doesn't provide a `pacman.conf`.

This PR updates the URL to `pacman.conf` URL to the newest Archlinux repo on their Gitlab.

[1] https://archlinux.org/news/cleaning-up-old-repositories/

title: arch bootstrap: Honor local `pacman.conf`
body:
When building a container using the `arch`-bootstrap, apparently a custom `pacman.conf` is used for `pacstrap`:

```
INFO    [U=0,P=1942035]    Full()                        Starting build...
DEBUG   [U=0,P=1942035]    findOnPath()                  Found "pacstrap" at "/usr/bin/pacstrap"
DEBUG   [U=0,P=1942035]    Get()                         
	Pacstrap Path: /usr/bin/pacstrap
	Pac Conf: /tmp/build-temp-3873071224/rootfs/pac-conf-1487610166
	Rootfs: /tmp/build-temp-3873071224/rootfs
	Install List: [base]
```

Why does apptainer not use the user's configuration stored at `/etc/pacman.conf` for pacstrap, like it would be used if the user would use `pacstrap` to create a non-apptainer container? Is there another way to customize the `pacstrap` execution when using apptainer?

This is especially annoying, as the `community` repository got deprecated, and despite removing it in my `pacman.conf`, `apptainer build` now always waits for a timeout for the `community` repository.

Thanks a lot!

title: binfmt
body:
Dear Apptainer team,

We are running the arm64 version of apptainer and we want to shell into an x86 simg container, which should then be emulated through binfmt.

The problem is that we get this error from apptainer:
```
While checking container encryption: could not open image niimath_1.0.0_20240902.simg: the image's architecture (amd64) could not run on the host's (arm64)
```

We found a workaround by mounting binfmt to the location that apptainer expects:
```
sudo mount -t binfmt_misc binfmt /proc/sys/fs/binfmt_misc
```

and then it works. Is there a chance apptainer could figure this out?

Could this problem be related to this commit?
https://github.com/apptainer/apptainer/commit/83d36933ecd4ae02a9b86c5aaad33547c75f823e

Here is a minimal example to reproduce the problem on an arm64 machine:
```
curl -X GET https://neurocontainers.neurodesk.org/niimath_1.0.0_20240902.simg -O
apptainer shell --overlay /tmp niimath_1.0.0_20240902.simg
```

title: Apptainer loses Docker WORKDIR information during SIF conversion
body:
When converting a Docker image to SIF, all information about the WORKDIR is seemingly lost.

I see #2573 touches this issue, but does not address cases where WORKDIR information is necessary for container execution.

This loss of information is catastrophic in my use case. [Our application](https://github.com/DigitalSlideArchive/digital_slide_archive/tree/slurm/devops/slurm) executes user-specified Docker container-based CLIs, which rely on an arbitrarily set WORKDIR to find code to execute. We are interested in using Apptainer to add support for HPC systems where Docker execution is disallowed. However, without a way to capture WORKDIR information in a Docker-less environment, Apptainer isn't as seamlessly usable as it could be.

Is there any known way to recover Docker WORKDIR information without a Docker client? Is there any rationale for why this information is not captured during the SIF conversion process?

title: fix: don't flatten layers with ggcr before extracting, from sylabs 2685
body:
This cherry-picks sylabs/singularity#2685 which had the following description:

> The ggcr module has a bug in its `mutate.Extract` function, due to optimisations that do not correctly track hard links that are manipulated in specific ways across layers:
> https://github.com/google/go-containerregistry/issues/977
>
> Prior to this PR, we were using `mutate.Extract` to flatten an image so that we were only extracting a single tar into a rootfs with umoci. This meant that the bug above could cause umoci to fail, as the flattened tar is invalid in certain circumstances.
> 
> Fix the issue by avoiding `mutate.Extract`. Instead extract each layer, in order, using umoci.

- Fixes #2841

title: Github clone with ssh in %setup fails if root-owned file exists in ssh_config.d
body:
In my `.def` file, I clone a repo using ssh credentials with:
```
%setup
    git clone git@github.com:<org_name>/<repo_name>.git ${APPTAINER_ROOTFS}/<repo_name>
```
When running build with `--fakeroot`, this command fails with a bad permissions error for a root-owned config file in `/etc/ssh/ssh_config.d/`:
```
INFO:    User not listed in /etc/subuid, trying root-mapped namespace
INFO:    The %post section will be run under fakeroot
INFO:    Starting build...
INFO:    Verifying bootstrap image <base_image>.sif
INFO:    Running setup scriptlet
+ git clone git@github.com:<org_name>/<repo_name>.git /tmp/build-temp-2079637988/rootfs/<repo_name>
Cloning into '/tmp/build-temp-2079637988/rootfs/<repo_name>'...
Bad owner or permissions on /etc/ssh/ssh_config.d/<conf_filename>.conf
fatal: Could not read from remote repository.

Please make sure you have the correct access rights
and the repository exists.
```

title: Containers built as non-root do not preserve file ownership from oci original
body:
With apptainer version 1.3.6-1.el8, non-suid install.

If I build two sif containers from the same dockerhub source, one with sudo and one without, then executing the container with subuid fakeroot shows that the one built with sudo preserves file user and group ownership but the one built without does not:
```
$ apptainer build rootless-rocky8.sif docker://rockylinux:8
...
$ sudo apptainer build sudo-rocky8.sif docker://rockylinux:8
...
$ apptainer exec -f sudo-rocky8.sif ls -l /usr/bin/write
-rwxr-sr-x 1 root tty 21104 Aug 10  2023 /usr/bin/write
$ apptainer exec -f rootless-rocky8.sif ls -l /usr/bin/write
-rwxr-sr-x 1 root root 21104 Aug 10  2023 /usr/bin/write
```

I'm not sure there's anything that can be done about it.  In the related issue #1123 there's a reference to documented [limitations on the umoci rootless mode](https://umo.ci/quick-start/rootless) which may be the cause.

Non-subuid fakeroot also loses the original ownership:
```
$ apptainer exec -f --ignore-subuid sudo-rocky8.sif ls -l /usr/bin/write
INFO:    User not listed in /etc/subuid, trying root-mapped namespace
INFO:    Using fakeroot command combined with root-mapped namespace
-rwxr-sr-x 1 root root 21104 Aug 10  2023 /usr/bin/write
```

title: chroot sif
body:
Is sif execution allowed in a chroot? I know there are easier ways to run sif files, but as an academic exercise here's my (probably naive) attempt:

### host info

```
# whoami
root
# head -n1 /etc/os-release
PRETTY_NAME="Debian GNU/Linux 12 (bookworm)"
# uname -r
6.1.0-31-amd64
```

### install apptainer on host

```
# cd ~
# wget https://github.com/apptainer/apptainer/releases/download/v1.3.6/apptainer_1.3.6_amd64.deb
# dpkg -i apptainer_1.3.6_amd64.deb
# apt-get install -fy
# apptainer --version
apptainer version 1.3.6
# apptainer pull docker://ghcr.io/apptainer/lolcow
# apptainer run lolcow_latest.sif
 _____________________________
< Sat Mar 1 18:27:59 GMT 2025 >
 -----------------------------
        \   ^__^
         \  (oo)\_______
            (__)\       )\/\
                ||----w |
                ||     ||
```

### create chroot directory and verify bash works

```
export LFS=~/initfs

mkdir -pv $LFS
mkdir -pv $LFS/{etc,var} $LFS/usr/{bin,lib,sbin}

for i in bin lib sbin; do
  ln -sv usr/$i $LFS/$i
done

case $(uname -m) in
  x86_64) mkdir -pv $LFS/lib64 ;;
esac

cp /usr/bin/bash $LFS/usr/bin/

cp /lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libtinfo.so.6 $LFS/lib/
cp /lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libc.so.6 $LFS/lib/
cp /lib64/ld-linux-x86-64.so.2 $LFS/lib64/

chroot $LFS  # bash-5.2 prompt appears, then type exit
```

### initialize chroot as described [here](https://www.usenix.org/publications/loginonline/building-linux-appliances)

```
cat > ~/copy_appliance_libs << EOF
#!/bin/bash

export MYINIT=\${MYINIT:=''}
export BINS=\${BINS:=''}

for bins in \${BINS}; do
    echo \$bins
    ## figure out where program lives
    bins_loc=\$(which \$bins)
    bins_dir_loc=\$(which \$bins | xargs -I '{}' dirname '{}')
    ## if program does not exist in initramfs
    if [[ ! -e "\${MYINIT}/\${bins_loc}" ]]; then
        echo \$bins_loc
        echo "\${MYINIT}/\${bins_dir_loc}"
        ## set up directory and copy programs to initramfs
        [[ -e "\${MYINIT}/\${bins_dir_loc}" ]] || mkdir -p "\${MYINIT}/\${bins_dir_loc}"
        cp \$bins_loc "\${MYINIT}/\${bins_dir_loc}"
        ## figure out library dependencies of \$bins
        libs_loc=\$(ldd \$bins_loc | grep "=> /" | awk '{print \$3}')
        ## set up directory and copy libs to initramfs
        for libs in \${libs_loc}; do
            libs_dir=\$(dirname \$libs)
            ## if library does not exist in initramfs
            if [[ ! -e "\${MYINIT}/\${libs}" ]]; then
            echo \$libs
            [[ -e "\${MYINIT}/\${libs_dir}" ]] || mkdir -p "\${MYINIT}/\${libs_dir}"
            cp \$libs "\${MYINIT}/\${libs_dir}"
            fi
        done
        echo "+++++++++++++"
    fi
done

EOF

chmod +x ~/copy_appliance_libs

MYINIT=$LFS BINS="ls cd pwd cat mount umount mkdir mknod cp mv install ln touch chgrp chmod poweroff reboot readlink ip dhclient ps wc uname hostname more tail head grep find df free" ~/copy_appliance_libs

chroot $LFS

mkdir -pv /{dev,proc,sys,run}
mkdir -pv /dev/pts
mknod -m 600 /dev/console c 5 1
mknod -m 666 /dev/null c 1 3

mkdir -pv /{boot,home,mnt,opt,srv}
mkdir -pv /etc/{opt,sysconfig}
mkdir -pv /lib/firmware
mkdir -pv /media/{floppy,cdrom}
mkdir -pv /usr/{,local/}{include,src}
mkdir -pv /usr/local/{bin,lib,sbin}
mkdir -pv /usr/{,local/}share/{color,dict,doc,info,locale,man}
mkdir -pv /usr/{,local/}share/{misc,terminfo,zoneinfo}
mkdir -pv /usr/{,local/}share/man/man{1..8}
mkdir -pv /var/{cache,local,log,mail,opt,spool}
mkdir -pv /var/lib/{color,misc,locate}
install -dv -m 0750 /root
install -dv -m 1777 /tmp /var/tmp
ln -sv /proc/self/mounts /etc/mtab
touch /var/log/{btmp,lastlog,faillog,wtmp}
chgrp -v utmp /var/log/lastlog
chmod -v 664  /var/log/lastlog
chmod -v 600  /var/log/btmp

cat > /etc/hosts << EOF
127.0.0.1  localhost applianceos
::1        localhost
EOF

cat > /etc/resolv.conf << EOF
nameserver 8.8.8.8
nameserver 8.8.4.4
EOF

cat > /etc/passwd << EOF
root:x:0:0:root:/root:/bin/bash
EOF

cat > /etc/group << EOF
root:x:0:
bin:x:1:daemon
sys:x:2:
kmem:x:3:
tape:x:4:
tty:x:5:
daemon:x:6:
floppy:x:7:
disk:x:8:
lp:x:9:
dialout:x:10:
users:x:999:
EOF

exit
```

### copy in apptainer and dependencies

```
MYINIT=$LFS BINS="apptainer sh fakeroot mksquashfs" ~/copy_appliance_libs
mkdir $LFS/usr/libexec $LFS/etc/ssl
cp /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libgcc_s.so.1 $LFS/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/
cp -R /etc/apptainer $LFS/etc/
cp -R /usr/libexec/apptainer $LFS/usr/libexec/
cp -R /etc/ssl/certs $LFS/etc/ssl/
```

### build sif file


Bumps the moby group with 2 updates in the / directory: [github.com/docker/docker](https://github.com/docker/docker) and [github.com/docker/cli](https://github.com/docker/cli). Updates `github.com/docker/docker` from 27.5.1+incompatible to 28.0.1+incompatible
Release notes

Sourced from github.com/docker/docker's releases.

v28.0.1

28.0.1

For a full list of pull requests and changes in this release, refer to the relevant GitHub milestones:

  • docker/cli, 28.0.1 milestone
  • moby/moby, 28.0.1 milestone

Networking

  • Remove dependency on kernel modules ip_set, ip_set_hash_net and netfilter_xt_set.
    • The dependency was introduced in release 28.0.0 but proved too disruptive. The iptables rules using these modules have been replaced. moby/moby#49530
  • Allow daemon startup on a host with IPv6 disabled without requiring --ip6tables=false. moby/moby#49525
  • Fix a bug that was causing containers with --restart=always and a published port already in use to restart in a tight loop. moby/moby#49507
  • Fix an issue with Swarm ingress, caused by incorrect ordering of iptables rules. moby/moby#49538
  • Fix creation of a swarm-scoped network from a --config-only network. moby/moby#49521
  • Fix docker network inspect reporting an IPv6 gateway with CIDR suffix for a newly created network with no specific IPAM config, until a daemon restart. moby/moby#49520
  • Improve the error reported when kernel modules ip_set, ip_set_hash_net and netilter_xt_set are not available. moby/moby#49524
  • Move most of Docker's iptables rules out of the filter-FORWARD chain, so that other applications are free to append rules that must follow Docker's rules. moby/moby#49518
  • Update --help output and man page lo state which options only apply to the default bridge network. moby/moby#49522

Bug fixes and enhancements

  • Fix docker context create always returning an error when using the "skip-tls-verify" option. docker/cli#5850
  • Fix shell completion suggesting IDs instead of names for services and nodes. docker/cli#5848
  • Fix unintentionally printing exit status to standard error output when docker exec/run returns a non-zero status. docker/cli#5854
  • Fix regression protocol "tcp" is not supported by the RootlessKit port driver "slirp4netns". moby/moby#49514
  • containerd image store: Fix docker inspect not being able to show multi-platform images with missing layers for all platforms. moby/moby#49533
  • containerd image store: Fix docker images --tree reporting wrong content size. moby/moby#49535
  • Fix compilation on i386 moby/moby#49526

  • Update Buildx to v0.21.1. docker/docker-ce-packaging#1167
  • Update Compose to v2.33.1. docker/docker-ce-packaging#1168

API

  • containerd image store: Fix GET /images/json?manifests=1 not filling Manifests for index-only images. moby/moby#49533
  • containerd image store: Fix GET /images/json and /images/<name>/json Size.Content field including the size of content that's not available locally. moby/moby#49535

title: Poor Man's remote build
body:
It is possible to use `sshocker`  (a predecessor and subset of [Lima](https://lima-vm.io)), to build on a remote Linux machine.

Assuming that the remote machine has `sshfs` (and thus FUSE) installed, the whole procedure goes like:

```console
$ sshocker -v /tmp/apptainer:/tmp/apptainer user@host apptainer build /tmp/apptainer/python.sif docker://python
```

Any build context, and the resulting SIF file, will be copied to a local `sftpd` server started in background...

https://github.com/lima-vm/sshocker

Similar to `apptainer.lima`, but simpler.

----

The command runs "reverse-sshfs", so it is tunneled over the SSH connection.

It also does port forwarding, but that shouldn't really be needed in this context.

In order to allow mounting filesystems, one normally has to edit `/etc/fuse.conf`:

```
# mount_max = 1000
user_allow_other
```

You could do the same procedure with only `ssh` and `scp` too, but this is "on-demand".

Any file that is needed to be read, or result that needs to be written, is copied automatically.

title: Consider defaulting `arm` architecture to the `v7` variant
body:
For docker and others, choosing `arm` now always means `armv7`...

If you need an older variant, you explicitly have to say linux/arm/v6.

```
$ docker run --rm --platform linux/arm busybox arch
armv7l
$ apptainer pull --arch arm busybox.sif docker://busybox
FATAL:   While processing the arch and arch variant: arch: arm needs variant specification, supported variants are [5, 6, 7], please set --arch-variant option
```

One could have arch-variant default to "7" automatically.

Like how choosing arm64 automatically defaults to "8"?

----

Should probably change the documentation to use the real names, too?

And allow the "7" variant as a backwards-compatible spelling of "v7".

For Raspberry Pi 1, there **used** to be a need for "Raspbian" rebuilds (v6).

But with Raspberry Pi 2 (since 2015) and on, it now runs regular Debian.

title: Architecture `riscv64` is blocked in the architecture list
body:
The riscv64 architecture needs to be added to the allowed list:

```console
$ docker run --rm --platform linux/riscv64 busybox arch
riscv64
$ apptainer pull --arch riscv64 busybox.sif docker://busybox
FATAL:   While processing the arch and arch variant: arch: riscv64 is not valid, supported archs are: [arm arm64 amd64 386 ppc64le s390x]
```

The hardware is not so common (yet), but Lima does support it...

https://ubuntu.com/blog/empowering-risc-v-with-open-source-through-ubuntu

----

The list is currently hardcoded within apptainer itself:

```go
// Convert CLI options GOARCH and arch variant to recognized docker arch
func ConvertArch(arch, archVariant string) (string, error) {
        supportedArchs := []string{"arm", "arm64", "amd64", "386", "ppc64le", "s390x"}
```

title: Support cgroups v2 in nested containers
body:
As mentioned in sylabs/singularity#3542, bind-mounting `/sys/fs/cgroup` is required to use cgroups in nested containers, and that is not happening in apptainer.  Their use case is oci mode, but apptainer supports nesting in normal user namespace mode.

Some inspiration may be able to be taken from sylabs/singularity#3542.  At least the rename of the included libcontainer/cgroups module to lccgroups in internal/pkg/cgroups/util.go is a good idea to keep it separate from the apptainer cgroups module.  Note that that PR bind-mounts `/sys/fs/cgroup` in read-only mode for unprivileged users (and also root unless `--keep-privs` is used), although I don't know why.

Bumps the moby group with 2 updates: [github.com/docker/docker](https://github.com/docker/docker) and [github.com/docker/cli](https://github.com/docker/cli). Updates `github.com/docker/docker` from 27.5.1+incompatible to 28.0.0+incompatible
Release notes

Sourced from github.com/docker/docker's releases.

v28.0.0

28.0.0

For a full list of pull requests and changes in this release, refer to the relevant GitHub milestones:

  • docker/cli, 28.0.0 milestone
  • moby/moby, 28.0.0 milestone
  • Deprecated and removed features, see Deprecated Features.
  • Changes to the Engine API, see API version history.

New

  • Add ability to mount an image inside a container via --mount type=image. moby/moby#48798
    • You can also specify --mount type=image,image-subpath=[subpath],... option to mount a specific path from the image. docker/cli#5755
  • docker images --tree now shows metadata badges. docker/cli#5744
  • docker load, docker save, and docker history now support a --platform flag allowing you to choose a specific platform for single-platform operations on multi-platform images. docker/cli#5331
  • Add OOMScoreAdj to docker service create and docker stack. docker/cli#5145
  • docker buildx prune now supports reserved-space, max-used-space, min-free-space and keep-bytes filters. moby/moby#48720
  • Windows: Add support for running containerd as a child process of the daemon, instead of using a system-installed containerd. moby/moby#47955

Networking

  • The docker-proxy binary has been updated, older versions will not work with the updated dockerd. moby/moby#48132
    • Close a window in which the userland proxy (docker-proxy) could accept TCP connections, that would then fail after iptables NAT rules were set up.
    • The executable rootlesskit-docker-proxy is no longer used, it has been removed from the build and distribution.
  • DNS nameservers read from the host's /etc/resolv.conf are now always accessed from the host's network namespace. moby/moby#48290
    • When the host's /etc/resolv.conf contains no nameservers and there are no --dns overrides, Google's DNS servers are no longer used, apart from by the default bridge network and in build containers.
  • Container interfaces in bridge and macvlan networks now use randomly generated MAC addresses. moby/moby#48808
    • Gratuitous ARP / Neighbour Advertisement messages will be sent when the interfaces are started so that, when IP addresses are reused, they're associated with the newly generated MAC address.
    • IPv6 addresses in the default bridge network are now IPAM-assigned, rather than being derived from the MAC address.
  • The deprecated OCI prestart hook is now only used by build containers. For other containers, network interfaces are added to the network namespace after task creation is complete, before the container task is started. moby/moby#47406
  • Add a new gw-priority option to docker run, docker container create, and docker network connect. This option will be used by the Engine to determine which network provides the default gateway for a container. On docker run, this option is only available through the extended --network syntax. docker/cli#5664
  • Add a new netlabel com.docker.network.endpoint.ifname to customize the interface name used when connecting a container to a network. It's supported by all built-in network drivers on Linux. moby/moby#49155
    • When a container is created with multiple networks specified, there's no guarantee on the order networks will be connected to the container. So, if a custom interface name uses the same prefix as the auto-generated names, for example eth, the container might fail to start.
    • The recommended practice is to use a different prefix, for example en0, or a numerical suffix high enough to never collide, for example eth100.
    • This label can be specified on docker network connect via the --driver-opt flag, for example docker network connect --driver-opt=com.docker.network.endpoint.ifname=foobar ….
    • Or via the long-form --network flag on docker run, for example docker run --network=name=bridge,driver-opt=com.docker.network.endpoint.ifname=foobar …

Port publishing in bridge networks

  • dockerd now requires ipset support in the Linux kernel. moby/moby#48596
    • The iptables and ip6tables rules used to implement port publishing and network isolation have been extensively modified. This enables some of the following functional changes, and is a first step in refactoring to enable native nftables support in a future release. moby/moby#48815
    • If it becomes necessary to downgrade to an earlier version of the daemon, some manual cleanup of the new rules will be necessary. The simplest and surest approach is to reboot the host, or use iptables -F and ip6tables -F to flush all existing iptables rules from the filter table before starting the older version of the daemon. When that is not possible, run the following commands as root:
      • iptables -D FORWARD -m set --match-set docker-ext-bridges-v4 dst -m conntrack --ctstate RELATED,ESTABLISHED -j ACCEPT; ip6tables -D FORWARD -m set --match-set docker-ext-bridges-v6 dst -m conntrack --ctstate RELATED,ESTABLISHED -j ACCEPT
      • iptables -D FORWARD -m set --match-set docker-ext-bridges-v4 dst -j DOCKER; ip6tables -D FORWARD -m set --match-set docker-ext-bridges-v6 dst -j DOCKER

  • Fix a security issue that was allowing remote hosts to connect directly to a container on its published ports. moby/moby#49325

Release notes

Sourced from github.com/docker/docker's releases.

v28.0.0

28.0.0

For a full list of pull requests and changes in this release, refer to the relevant GitHub milestones:

  • docker/cli, 28.0.0 milestone
  • moby/moby, 28.0.0 milestone
  • Deprecated and removed features, see Deprecated Features.
  • Changes to the Engine API, see API version history.

New

  • Add ability to mount an image inside a container via --mount type=image. moby/moby#48798
    • You can also specify --mount type=image,image-subpath=[subpath],... option to mount a specific path from the image. docker/cli#5755
  • docker images --tree now shows metadata badges. docker/cli#5744
  • docker load, docker save, and docker history now support a --platform flag allowing you to choose a specific platform for single-platform operations on multi-platform images. docker/cli#5331
  • Add OOMScoreAdj to docker service create and docker stack. docker/cli#5145
  • docker buildx prune now supports reserved-space, max-used-space, min-free-space and keep-bytes filters. moby/moby#48720
  • Windows: Add support for running containerd as a child process of the daemon, instead of using a system-installed containerd. moby/moby#47955

Networking

  • The docker-proxy binary has been updated, older versions will not work with the updated dockerd. moby/moby#48132
    • Close a window in which the userland proxy (docker-proxy) could accept TCP connections, that would then fail after iptables NAT rules were set up.
    • The executable rootlesskit-docker-proxy is no longer used, it has been removed from the build and distribution.
  • DNS nameservers read from the host's /etc/resolv.conf are now always accessed from the host's network namespace. moby/moby#48290
    • When the host's /etc/resolv.conf contains no nameservers and there are no --dns overrides, Google's DNS servers are no longer used, apart from by the default bridge network and in build containers.
  • Container interfaces in bridge and macvlan networks now use randomly generated MAC addresses. moby/moby#48808
    • Gratuitous ARP / Neighbour Advertisement messages will be sent when the interfaces are started so that, when IP addresses are reused, they're associated with the newly generated MAC address.
    • IPv6 addresses in the default bridge network are now IPAM-assigned, rather than being derived from the MAC address.
  • The deprecated OCI prestart hook is now only used by build containers. For other containers, network interfaces are added to the network namespace after task creation is complete, before the container task is started. moby/moby#47406
  • Add a new gw-priority option to docker run, docker container create, and docker network connect. This option will be used by the Engine to determine which network provides the default gateway for a container. On docker run, this option is only available through the extended --network syntax. docker/cli#5664
  • Add a new netlabel com.docker.network.endpoint.ifname to customize the interface name used when connecting a container to a network. It's supported by all built-in network drivers on Linux. moby/moby#49155
    • When a container is created with multiple networks specified, there's no guarantee on the order networks will be connected to the container. So, if a custom interface name uses the same prefix as the auto-generated names, for example eth, the container might fail to start.
    • The recommended practice is to use a different prefix, for example en0, or a numerical suffix high enough to never collide, for example eth100.
    • This label can be specified on docker network connect via the --driver-opt flag, for example docker network connect --driver-opt=com.docker.network.endpoint.ifname=foobar ….
    • Or via the long-form --network flag on docker run, for example docker run --network=name=bridge,driver-opt=com.docker.network.endpoint.ifname=foobar …
  • If a custom network driver reports capability GwAllocChecker then, before a network is created, it will get a GwAllocCheckerRequest with the network's options. The custom driver may then reply that no gateway IP address should be allocated. moby/moby#49372

Port publishing in bridge networks

  • dockerd now requires ipset support in the Linux kernel. moby/moby#48596
    • The iptables and ip6tables rules used to implement port publishing and network isolation have been extensively modified. This enables some of the following functional changes, and is a first step in refactoring to enable native nftables support in a future release. moby/moby#48815
    • If it becomes necessary to downgrade to an earlier version of the daemon, some manual cleanup of the new rules will be necessary. The simplest and surest approach is to reboot the host, or use iptables -F and ip6tables -F to flush all existing iptables rules from the filter table before starting the older version of the daemon. When that is not possible, run the following commands as root:
      • iptables -D FORWARD -m set --match-set docker-ext-bridges-v4 dst -m conntrack --ctstate RELATED,ESTABLISHED -j ACCEPT; ip6tables -D FORWARD -m set --match-set docker-ext-bridges-v6 dst -m conntrack --ctstate RELATED,ESTABLISHED -j ACCEPT
      • iptables -D FORWARD -m set --match-set docker-ext-bridges-v4 dst -j DOCKER; ip6tables -D FORWARD -m set --match-set docker-ext-bridges-v6 dst -j DOCKER
      • If you were previously running with the iptables filter-FORWARD policy set to ACCEPT and need to restore access to unpublished ports, also delete per-bridge-network rules from the DOCKER chains. For example, iptables -D DOCKER ! -i docker0 -o docker0 -j DROP.
  • Fix a security issue that was allowing remote hosts to connect directly to a container on its published ports. moby/moby#49325
  • Fix a security issue that was allowing neighbor hosts to connect to ports mapped on a loopback address. moby/moby#49325

title: mount source /etc/localtime doesn't exist
body:
There is no `/etc/localtime` on the host system:

```txt
apptainer run --containall docker://fedora
^[[34mINFO:   ^[[0m Using cached SIF image
^[[31mFATAL:  ^[[0m container creation failed: mount hook function failure: mount /etc/localtime->/etc/localtime error: while mounting /etc/localtime: mount source /etc/localtime doesn't exist
```

I could not find a wait to modify `apptainer.conf` to disable mounting localtime (related https://github.com/apptainer/singularity/issues/5301) so all users must `--no-mount /etc/localtime`. 

`bind path = /etc/localtime` has been removed. `mount localtime = no` is set, but doesn't seem to do anything (with no complaints).

Seems like if there is no `/etc/localtime`, it shouldn't try to mount it.

````
apptainer build python.sif docker-archive://python.tar
````

````
apptainer build python.sif docker://python
````

title: Show progressbar for SIF creation without requiring verbose mode
body:
Currently there is support for showing the entire `mksquashfs` output in verbose mode...
But that also shows a lot of other output as shown here: https://github.com/apptainer/apptainer-userdocs/issues/318

```
INFO:    Creating SIF file...
[==========================>----------------------------------------------------------] 25 % 1m0s
```

title: Consider bundling a `mksquashfs` with more compression options etc
body:
One _could_ add some information to documentation and packaging, on how to build "[squashfs-tools](https://github.com/plougher/squashfs-tools)" with more compression support.

On some platforms, the support for alternatives to gzip have been disabled by packaging (or age) and excludes the newer alternatives.

The implementation should be as simple as putting it first in the PATH, possibly choosing a different name than `/usr/bin/mksquashfs`?

The software normally builds without too many complications, all that is needed is to override some variables for better support...

* https://github.com/apptainer/apptainer/issues/1022

```
Makefile:GZIP_SUPPORT ?= 1
Makefile:XZ_SUPPORT ?= 0
Makefile:LZO_SUPPORT ?= 0
Makefile:LZ4_SUPPORT ?= 0
Makefile:ZSTD_SUPPORT ?= 0
```

Having zstd and lz4 "always" available would be nice, assuming that one is also providing a `squashfuse_ll` with similar support.

They both feature much better (5-10x) performance than gzip, and in the case of zstd it also provides compression similar to xz.

* https://github.com/apptainer/apptainer/pull/2707

* https://github.com/apptainer/apptainer-userdocs/issues/308

----

See also: https://facebook.github.io/zstd/#benchmarks

Compressor name	| Ratio	| Compression	| Decompress.
--- | --- | --- | ---
zlib 1.2.11 -1	| 2.743	| 95 MB/s	| 400 MB/s
zstd 1.5.6 -1	| 2.887	| 510 MB/s	| 1580 MB/s
zstd 1.5.6 --fast=1	| 2.437	| 545 MB/s	| 1890 MB/s
zstd 1.5.6 --fast=3	| 2.239	| 650 MB/s	| 2000 MB/s
lzo1x 2.10 -1	| 2.106	| 650 MB/s	| 825 MB/s
lz4 1.9.4	| 2.101	| 700 MB/s	| 4000 MB/s

Since 1.0: https://engineering.fb.com/2016/08/31/core-infra/smaller-and-faster-data-compression-with-zstandard/

CLI | Ratio | Comp Speed | Decomp Speed
--- | --- | --- | ---
`gzip` | 3.11 | 19.66 MB/s | 125.55 MB/s
`zstd` | 3.14 | 100.1 MB/s | 459.40 MB/s

title: rocky9: transaction failed error with filesystem-3.16-5.el9
body:
os version: rocky 9.5, 5.14.0-503.22.1.el9_5.x86_64
apptainer version 1.3.6-1.el9

when I try to create a simple apptainer containing following

```
BootStrap: docker
From: rockylinux:9

%post
    dnf update -y
```

I get an ‘transaction failed’ error with the filesystem-3.16-5.el9 package similar to [Filesystem-3.16-5 package broken?](https://forums.rockylinux.org/t/filesystem-3-16-5-package-broken/16570)

I modified the apptainer and installed filesystem package with rpm -Uvh to see the errors:

```
[...]
+ rpm -Uvh --force filesystem-3.16-5.el9.x86_64.rpm
Verifying...                          ################################# [100%]

Updating / installing...

error: filesystem-3.16-5.el9.x86_64: install failed
error: filesystem-3.16-2.el9.x86_64: erase skipped
```

it seems filesystem-3.16-5.el9 checks the ownership of /dev and fails if it cannot fix it. Is it a bug in the package, apptainer or did I miss a configuration option ?

title: Issue with running apptainer in a privileged docker container with `--platform linux/arm64`
body:
Hello,

I'm trying to upgrade our usage of Singularity from a very early version to something more modern. We are also starting to run on ARM64. I'm trying apptainer but I'm getting build issues and I'm not sure where to dig. This is the debug output when trying to build a singularity image from a docker image run with `docker run -it --platform linux/arm64 --privileged <arm64 ubuntu 24.04 image>`:

```
root@f33227291c5a:~# singularity -v --debug build test.simg docker://ubuntu:24.04
DEBUG   [U=0,P=1403]       persistentPreRun()            Apptainer version: 1.3.4
DEBUG   [U=0,P=1403]       persistentPreRun()            Parsing configuration file /etc/apptainer/apptainer.conf
DEBUG   [U=0,P=1403]       SetBinaryPath()               Setting binary path to /usr/libexec/apptainer/bin:/usr/local/sbin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/sbin:/usr/bin:/sbin:/bin:/usr/local/sbin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/sbin:/usr/bin:/sbin:/bin
DEBUG   [U=0,P=1403]       SetBinaryPath()               Using that path for all binaries
DEBUG   [U=0,P=1403]       handleConfDir()               /root/.apptainer already exists. Not creating.
DEBUG   [U=0,P=1403]       getCacheParentDir()           environment variable APPTAINER_CACHEDIR not set, using default image cache
DEBUG   [U=0,P=1403]       newBundle()                   Created temporary directory "/tmp/bundle-temp-3002099959" for the bundle
DEBUG   [U=0,P=1403]       newBundle()                   Created directory "/tmp/build-temp-2315311038/rootfs" for the bundle

DEBUG   [U=0,P=1403]       ensureGzipComp()              Ensuring gzip compression for mksquashfs
DEBUG   [U=0,P=1403]       findOnPath()                  Found "mksquashfs" at "/usr/bin/mksquashfs"
FATAL   [U=0,P=1403]       runBuildLocal()               Unable to create build: while ensuring correct compression algorithm: while creating squashfs: create command failed: fork/exec /usr/bin/mksquashfs: invalid argument:
```

If I do a `amd64` build with `docker run -it --platform linux/amd64 --privileged <amd64 ubuntu 24.04 image>` it seems to work OK.

I was reading that `mksquashfs` changed how it handled unknown arguments, but since both images are based off of Ubuntu 24.04 I don't see a version difference.

Thanks for your time.

title: Reliable way to reproduce a .sif image
body:
If I build an image file using the `latest` tag, there doesn't appear to be reliable way to discover the version (or ideally the SHA digest) that was used so that it can be reproduced at a later date.

My initial attempt was to use `apptainer inspect` command to get the `org.label-schema.version` label, but this appears to be missing from some images.

title: Add a simple fakeroot build mode based on seccomp
body: See the [charliecloud paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.06085) describing a fakeroot that's not a complete emulation but is fast and doesn't have any library mis-match problems.  It does require intercepting `apt` and `apt-get` in debian-based build definitions and interjecting an extra option.  For that reason it may not be appropriate as a default for the general `--fakeroot` exec/run/shell option.

apptainer version 1.3.6-1.el9

## Expected behavior

I expect apptainer to cleanup the CVMFS mounts

## Actual behavior

CVMFS mounts linger after the container has exited

## Steps to reproduce this behavior

This is a difficult one, since I've only seen this behavior on one system. There, I do:

```
apptainer  run  --scratch "/var/lib/cvmfs,/var/run/cvmfs" --fusemount "container:cvmfs2 cvmfs-config.cern.ch /cvmfs/cvmfs-config.cern.ch" --fusemount "container:cvmfs2 software.eessi.io /cvmfs/software.eessi.io" docker://ghcr.io/eessi/build-node:debian11 ls -al /cvmfs/software.eessi.io
```
which results in
```
INFO:    Using cached SIF image
CernVM-FS: pre-mounted on file descriptor 3
CernVM-FS: pre-mounted on file descriptor 3
CernVM-FS: loading Fuse module... done
CernVM-FS: loading Fuse module... done
total 8
drwxr-xr-x 4 casparl casparl 4096 Sep 11  2023 .
-rw-r--r-- 1 casparl casparl  605 Sep  5 13:48 .cvmfsdirtab
-rw-r--r-- 1 casparl casparl  565 Dec  2  2023 README.eessi
lrwxrwxrwx 1 casparl casparl   10 Oct  3  2023 host_injections -> /opt/eessi
drwxr-xr-x 3 casparl casparl   21 Sep  5 13:48 init
drwxr-xr-x 3 casparl casparl   21 Jul 22  2024 versions
INFO:    Terminating squashfuse_ll after timeout
INFO:    Timeouts can be caused by a running background process
```
Note that on this system:
```
$ fuse-overlayfs --version
fuse-overlayfs: version 1.13-dev
FUSE library version 3.10.2
using FUSE kernel interface version 7.31
fusermount3 version: 3.10.2
```

I tried to reproduce this on another system. There, I got to
```
$ apptainer --version
apptainer version 1.3.2
$ fuse-overlayfs --version
fuse-overlayfs: version 1.7.1
FUSE library version 3.10.2
using FUSE kernel interface version 7.31
fusermount3 version: 3.10.2
```

 but still wasn't able to reproduce the issue. I.e. there is no lingering cvmfs2 mounts, and the messages

```
INFO:    Terminating squashfuse_ll after timeout
INFO:    Timeouts can be caused by a running background process
```
do not appear.

I then tried to build `fuse-overlayfs` v 1.13 from sources as per the instructions on https://github.com/containers/fuse-overlayfs, but that provides a statically linked version built in a container, and against a different FUSE library version. So after, I had
```
$ fuse-overlayfs --version
fuse-overlayfs: version 1.13-dev
FUSE library version 3.14.0
using FUSE kernel interface version 7.31
fusermount3 version: 3.10.5
```
but still wasn't able to reproduce the issue

## What OS/distro are you running

RHEL9

## How did you install Apptainer

The system administrators did, so I'm not sure, but from the `el9` suffix, it seems to be a package built specifically for RHEL9.

## Possibly related

I saw [this comment](https://github.com/apptainer/apptainer/issues/2104#issuecomment-2067767448) that looks like I'm not the first to have seen such issues, but I'm unclear on the exact cause or fix.

## Potential fixes

On the same system, if I build Apptainer from sources (using EasyBuild), I don't see the same issue. For those familiar with EasyBuild, I've attached the Easyconfig I used below.

<details>
  <summary>EasyConfig</summary>

(HPC) environments."""

sources = [SOURCELOWER_TAR_GZ]

    ('binutils', '2.40'),
    ('Go', '1.22.1'),

    ('Autotools', '20220317'),
    ('zlib', '1.2.13'),
]

osdependencies = [
    ('openssl-devel'),
    ('libuuid-devel'),
    ('libseccomp-devel'),
    ('squashfs-tools'),
    ('cryptsetup'),
]

preinstallopts = 'cd builddir &&'

    'files': ['bin/apptainer'],
    'dirs': [],
}

sanity_check_commands = [('apptainer', '--version')]

moduleclass = 'tools'

</details>

The only difference that stands out is that in my the `libexec` folder in both installations seems different:

```
[casparl@gcn157 ~]$ ls /usr/libexec/apptainer/bin/
fuse-overlayfs  fuse2fs  gocryptfs  squashfuse_ll  starter
[casparl@gcn157 ~]$ ls /home/casparl/.local/easybuild/RHEL9/2024/software/Apptainer/1.3.6/libexec/apptainer/bin
starter
```

(where the first is for the installation that does _not_ work). It might be relevant, since it contains `squashfuse_ll`, which is the application that throws the 'Note' only in the failing case. It might be an optional codepath that causes the issue, and that is only taken if `sqaushfuse_ll` is present in the installation?

I know it's a lot of information, but I've reached my limits on diagnosing the issue - any help is greatly appreciated.

Cherry-pick sylabs/singularity#2159.

Remove special UNLICENSE handling because go-licenses 1.6.0 already handles it.

Use a template approach for the markdown generation, rather than converting from CSV ourselves.

The template includes full license text, per-dependency, rather than a link to the URL for the dependency's license. This is useful as it:

title: Docs say cwd is automatically mounted but it might not be true
body:
I am using `apptainer 1.3.2` on an HPC system, and from a directory which is not my home (e.g. `home/my_user/some/path`) I am running,

`apptainer exec my_image.sif pwd`

obtaining 

`home/my_user`

I understand this might be wanted behavior from singularity 2.x.x (see apptainer/singularity#5846), but [the current docs](https://apptainer.org/docs/user/main/bind_paths_and_mounts.html#system-defined-bind-paths) state that the working directory is one of the paths automatically bounded from the host to the guest file system.

If this is not true due to some configuration of `apptainer` set by the HPC system admins I think this should be made clear with a way to check/debug the required configuration option (via e.g., `apptainer config global --get`).

title: PAM account management error
body:
# Basic description
After an update from OpenSuse LEAP 15.5 to 15.6, with a fairly new kernel version of the host operating system, our application no longer runs in the container. We used "apptainer instance start" to start to container.  
The application requires sudo inside the container and we get the following error message:
"sudo: PAM account management error: Authentication service cannot retrieve authentication info
sudo: a password is required"
We are not sure whether this problem is related to apptainer or to the latest linux kernel or PAM version.
However using podman will not show this problem.

## Task to reproduce the problem
we have reduced the problem to a few simple steps:
~ # apptainer pull docker://rockylinux:8.8
~ # apptainer exec --writable-tmpfs rockylinux_8.8.sif /bin/bash
Apptainer> dnf -y install sudo
....
Apptainer> sudo ls
bin  inst-sys  rockylinux_8.8.sif  rockylinux_9.3.sif
\# works with pam-1.3.1-25.el8.src.rpm
Apptainer> dnf -y update
....
Apptainer> sudo ls
sudo: PAM account management error: Authentication service cannot retrieve authentication info
sudo: a password is required
\#failed with pam-1.3.1-36.el8_10.src.rpm   

## Problem perspective 
We build the container for the application almost a year ago. At that time OpenSuse LEAP 15.5 was the basic OS on the host.   
~ # uname -a
Linux .... 5.14.21-150500.53-default #1 SMP PREEMPT_DYNAMIC Wed May 10 07:56:26 UTC 2023 (b630043) x86_64 x86_64 x86_64 GNU/Linux
Inside the container we used Rocky 8.8. We expected that using a container for the application wil protect us from having to adapt the container during OS updates.  Unfortunately, that didn't work out. 
As a quick countermeasure, we have excluded the container image from the update of the existing PAM module. 
In the definition file we used "dnf -y update --exclude=pam" to avoid updating PAM.   
This worked, but does not explain why updating the external host operating system causes this problem inside of the container.    
Downgrading the kernel of the host operating system did not work either.  
As PAM is security-relevant, we are reluctant not to update the PAM module within the container.

apptainer version 1.3.6

title: Consider changing the default shell prompt
body:
The default shell prompt is `Apptainer> ` without any path information. This can make mistakes like `rm -rf *` inside the wrong directory much easier. In combination with #2754, this makes it simple to accidentally land in the wrong directory and not notice it.

The shell prompt currently most resembles REPL-like prompts from things like Python, Julia or GDB. Looking across different shells implementations and configurations, I have not encountered any distribution and shell beyond the most basic `sh` that does not include at least the name of the current directory in the prompt (e.g. RHEL) or the full path (e.g. Ubuntu).

As an inspiration, we can take a look at Python venv or commonly used git-aware prompts, which add some indication of the current shell being inside a venv/git repository, but keeps the path/user/hostname information from the original prompt.

In short, what Apptainer is doing here seems to me like a very uncommon way of setting the prompt in a way that is not shared by any container runtimes or development environments I am aware of.

title: Workdir mounting broken with symlinks
body:
When executing apptainer exec/shell from a workdir that contains a symlink in its path, and this symlink resolves to a path that is not mounted in the container, the chdir to the workdir after setting up the container fails.
Running from the latest `main` state:

```
[tribizel@head ~]$ ls -l foo
lrwxrwxrwx. 1 tribizel tribizel 30 Dec 19 15:09 foo -> /storage/home/tribizel/foo/
[tribizel@head foo]$ cd foo
[tribizel@head foo]$ pwd
/home/tribizel/foo
[tribizel@head foo]$ realpath `pwd`
/storage/home/tribizel/foo
[tribizel@head foo]$ ~/apptainer/prefix/bin/apptainer exec ~/apptainer/prefix/bin/ubuntu_latest.sif pwd
/home/tribizel
```

Possible solutions:

1. Fail loudly when chdir to the workdir fails
2. Warn when chdir to the workdir fails
3. Replace the workdir by its `realpath`
4. Bind-mount all symlinks on the path up to `/`

My comments on the suggested solutions:

1. makes working in symlinked dirs slightly more inconvenient, but is the safest option
2. is safer than the current state, without much complexity in its resolution
3. changes behavior for applications that assume the workdir stays the same between host and container
4. involves a lot of complexity, and potentially makes the container confinement much less strict
